```rust
// PURPOSE: The cross-cutting security test matrix for the authorization,
// tenancy and row-level-security hardening phase.
//
// Owning layer: workspace-root integration tests, compiled as part of
// `mas-api` (see `crates/api/tests/security_matrix.rs`).
//
// Production responsibility: assert, from the outside, the properties this
// phase guarantees — that no caller can name a tenant it does not belong to,
// that no principal can authorize itself into a scope, that internal services
// are authenticated, that deny is the default, and that a pooled connection
// never carries scope between requests.
//
// Security boundary: these tests are the executable form of the phase's
// completion gate. A test here fails if and only if a layer below has started
// trusting a caller-supplied value.
//
// It must NOT:
//   • test business behaviour that has no security consequence — that belongs
//     in the feature suites;
//   • silently skip when a dependency is missing. A test that cannot run fails,
//     so a green suite always means the property was actually checked.


use mas_api::handlers::internal::ScheduleRunRequest;
use mas_api::scope_resolution::ScopeClaims;
use mas_api::state::test_support::inmemory_state;
use mas_common::ids::{OrganizationId, ProjectId, ScheduleId, TenantId};
use mas_common::timestamps::Timestamp;
use mas_domain::MembershipRole;
use mas_security::internal_service::{sign, SERVICE_HEADER, SIGNATURE_HEADER};
use mas_security::{
    Action, AuthorizationDecision, AuthorizationRequest, AuthorizationService, AuthFailureKind,
    PrincipalKind, ResourceKind, ScopeSet, SecurityPrincipal, TenantMembership,
};
use serde_json::json;
use tower::ServiceExt;

const SECRET: &str = "inmemory-internal-secret";

/// A membership-bound human principal, the ordinary case.
fn user(actor: &str, memberships: Vec<TenantMembership>) -> SecurityPrincipal {
    SecurityPrincipal::new(actor, PrincipalKind::User, None, ScopeSet::denied())
        .with_memberships(memberships)
}

/// One grant.
fn membership(
    organization: OrganizationId,
    tenant: TenantId,
    role: MembershipRole,
) -> TenantMembership {
    TenantMembership::new(organization, tenant, role)
}

fn request(
    resource: ResourceKind,
    action: Action,
    tenant: TenantId,
    organization: OrganizationId,
    project: Option<ProjectId>,
) -> AuthorizationRequest {
    AuthorizationRequest {
        resource,
        action,
        tenant_id: tenant,
        organization_id: organization,
        project_id: project,
    }
}

fn deny_kind(decision: &AuthorizationDecision) -> Option<AuthFailureKind> {
    match decision {
        AuthorizationDecision::Deny(failure) => Some(failure.kind),
        AuthorizationDecision::Allow { .. } => None,
    }
}

// ── 1. Caller-supplied identity is never authoritative ──────────────────────

/// A principal with no membership in the tenant is denied. Its own claim that
/// it belongs there is not evidence.
#[tokio::test]
async fn a_principal_cannot_authorize_itself_into_an_ungranted_tenant() {
    let tenant = TenantId::new();
    let organization = OrganizationId::new();
    let attacker = SecurityPrincipal::new(
        "mallory",
        PrincipalKind::User,
        Some(tenant),
        ScopeSet::denied(),
    );
    let decision = AuthorizationService.authorize(
        &attacker,
        &request(
            ResourceKind::Execution,
            Action::Read,
            tenant,
            organization,
            None,
        ),
    );
    // The credential is bound to a tenant but holds no membership proving
    // it, so the refusal is a tenant mismatch — the point being that the
    // principal's own `tenant_id` field is not accepted as proof.
    assert!(
        matches!(deny_kind(&decision), Some(AuthFailureKind::TenantMismatch)),
        "a self-asserted tenant must fail as an unproven membership, not pass"
    );
}

/// Deny by default: an action the role does not carry is refused even for the
/// most privileged role.
#[tokio::test]
async fn an_action_outside_the_role_grants_is_denied() {
    let tenant = TenantId::new();
    let organization = OrganizationId::new();
    let viewer = user("v", vec![membership(organization, tenant, MembershipRole::Viewer)]);
    for action in [
        Action::Create,
        Action::Update,
        Action::Delete,
        Action::Execute,
        Action::Cancel,
        Action::Publish,
        Action::Administer,
    ] {
        let decision = AuthorizationService.authorize(
            &viewer,
            &request(ResourceKind::Execution, action, tenant, organization, None),
        );
        assert!(
            matches!(deny_kind(&decision), Some(AuthFailureKind::InsufficientPermission)),
            "a viewer must not {action:?}"
        );
    }
}

/// A viewer cannot manage credentials, policies or billing, and cannot read
/// the audit log: those are privileged actions, not read actions.
#[tokio::test]
async fn privileged_actions_are_refused_for_the_least_privileged_roles() {
    let tenant = TenantId::new();
    let organization = OrganizationId::new();
    for role in [
        MembershipRole::Viewer,
        MembershipRole::Operator,
        MembershipRole::Developer,
    ] {
        let principal = user("p", vec![membership(organization, tenant, role)]);
        for (resource, action) in [
            (ResourceKind::Credential, Action::ManageCredentials),
            (ResourceKind::Policy, Action::ManagePolicies),
            (ResourceKind::Audit, Action::ViewAudit),
            (ResourceKind::Usage, Action::ManageBilling),
        ] {
            let decision = AuthorizationService.authorize(
                &principal,
                &request(resource, action, tenant, organization, None),
            );
            assert!(
                matches!(decision, AuthorizationDecision::Deny(_)),
                "{role:?} must not {action:?} a {resource:?}"
            );
        }
    }
}

/// A service account is bound by its tenant like anything else: it is not a
/// platform-wide key.
#[tokio::test]
async fn a_service_account_is_still_bound_by_its_tenant() {
    let mine = TenantId::new();
    let theirs = TenantId::new();
    let organization = OrganizationId::new();
    let account = user(
        "sa-1",
        vec![membership(
            organization,
            mine,
            MembershipRole::ServiceAccount,
        )],
    );
    let decision = AuthorizationService.authorize(
        &account,
        &request(
            ResourceKind::Agent,
            Action::Read,
            theirs,
            organization,
            None,
        ),
    );
    assert!(
        matches!(decision, AuthorizationDecision::Deny(_)),
        "a service account must not read across tenants"
    );
}

/// An expired credential denies everything, including reads the role
/// otherwise carries.
#[tokio::test]
async fn an_expired_credential_denies_everything() {
    let tenant = TenantId::new();
    let organization = OrganizationId::new();
    let mut principal = user(
        "owner",
        vec![membership(organization, tenant, MembershipRole::Owner)],
    );
    principal.expires_at = Some(
        Timestamp::from_unix_ms(Timestamp::now().to_unix_ms() - 60_000).expect("timestamp"),
    );
    let decision = AuthorizationService.authorize(
        &principal,
        &request(
            ResourceKind::Execution,
            Action::Read,
            tenant,
            organization,
            None,
        ),
    );
    assert!(
        matches!(
            deny_kind(&decision),
            Some(AuthFailureKind::ExpiredCredential)
        ),
        "an expired credential must deny before any other check"
    );
}

// ── 2. Denials are typed, stable and never retryable ────────────────────────

/// Every denial carries a stable wire code, so clients branch on a contract
/// rather than on a message.
#[tokio::test]
async fn every_denial_carries_a_stable_code() {
    let tenant = TenantId::new();
    let organization = OrganizationId::new();
    let viewer = user("v", vec![membership(organization, tenant, MembershipRole::Viewer)]);
    let decision = AuthorizationService.authorize(
        &viewer,
        &request(
            ResourceKind::Execution,
            Action::Delete,
            tenant,
            organization,
            None,
        ),
    );
    match decision {
        AuthorizationDecision::Deny(failure) => {
            assert_eq!(failure.code(), "insufficient_permission");
            assert!(!failure.to_app_error().error_code().is_empty());
        },
        AuthorizationDecision::Allow { .. } => panic!("expected a denial"),
    }
}

/// Authentication and authorization failures are never retryable: a client
/// must not loop on a refusal.
#[tokio::test]
async fn authorization_failures_are_never_retryable() {
    let tenant = TenantId::new();
    let organization = OrganizationId::new();
    let attacker = SecurityPrincipal::new(
        "m",
        PrincipalKind::User,
        Some(tenant),
        ScopeSet::denied(),
    );
    let decision = AuthorizationService.authorize(
        &attacker,
        &request(
            ResourceKind::Execution,
            Action::Create,
            tenant,
            organization,
            None,
        ),
    );
    match decision {
        AuthorizationDecision::Deny(failure) => assert!(
            !failure.to_app_error().is_retryable(),
            "an authorization failure must never be retried"
        ),
        AuthorizationDecision::Allow { .. } => panic!("expected a denial"),
    }
}

// ── 3. Scope resolution: hints are not authority ────────────────────────────

/// A claim naming an unreachable tenant does not resolve.
#[tokio::test]
async fn a_claim_for_an_unreachable_tenant_does_not_resolve() {
    let state = inmemory_state();
    let resolver = state
        .scope_resolver
        .as_ref()
        .expect("the test lane resolves scope");
    let result = resolver
        .resolve(
            &user("nobody", vec![]),
            ScopeClaims {
                tenant: Some(TenantId::new()),
                organization: None,
                project: None,
            },
        )
        .await;
    assert!(result.is_err(), "an unreachable tenant must not resolve");
}

/// Conflicting claims fail deterministically rather than being silently
/// corrected.
#[tokio::test]
async fn conflicting_tenant_and_organization_claims_fail() {
    let state = inmemory_state();
    let resolver = state
        .scope_resolver
        .as_ref()
        .expect("the test lane resolves scope");
    let result = resolver
        .resolve(
            &user("nobody", vec![]),
            ScopeClaims {
                tenant: Some(TenantId::new()),
                organization: Some(OrganizationId::new()),
                project: None,
            },
        )
        .await;
    assert!(
        result.is_err(),
        "a conflicting pair of claims must fail, not be corrected"
    );
}

// ── 4. Internal service authentication ─────────────────────────────────────

fn run_body(tenant: TenantId, schedule: ScheduleId) -> Vec<u8> {
    serde_json::to_vec(&ScheduleRunRequest {
        schedule_id: schedule,
        tenant_id: tenant,
        planned_at: Timestamp::now(),
        task_template: json!({ "operation": "noop" }),
    })
    .expect("body")
}

async fn post_internal(
    state: mas_api::state::AppState,
    service: &str,
    secret: &str,
    at: &Timestamp,
    body: &[u8],
) -> axum::http::StatusCode {
    let app = mas_api::router::router(state);
    let signature = sign(secret.as_bytes(), service, at, body);
    let request = axum::http::Request::builder()
        .method("POST")
        .uri("/v1/internal/schedule-runs")
        .header("content-type", "application/json")
        .header(SIGNATURE_HEADER, signature)
        .header(SERVICE_HEADER, service)
        .body(axum::body::Body::from(body.to_vec()))
        .expect("request");
    app.oneshot(request).await.expect("response").status()
}

/// The network is not an identity: an unsigned internal call is refused.
#[tokio::test]
async fn an_unsigned_internal_call_is_refused() {
    let app = mas_api::router::router(inmemory_state());
    let response = app
        .oneshot(
            axum::http::Request::builder()
                .method("POST")
                .uri("/v1/internal/schedule-runs")
                .header("content-type", "application/json")
                .body(axum::body::Body::from(run_body(
                    TenantId::new(),
                    ScheduleId::new(),
                )))
                .expect("request"),
        )
        .await
        .expect("response");
    assert_eq!(response.status(), axum::http::StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED);
}

/// A call captured hours ago cannot be replayed.
#[tokio::test]
async fn a_replayed_internal_call_is_refused() {
    let long_ago =
        Timestamp::from_unix_ms(Timestamp::now().to_unix_ms() - 7_200_000).expect("timestamp");
    let status = post_internal(
        inmemory_state(),
        "mas-scheduler",
        SECRET,
        &long_ago,
        &run_body(TenantId::new(), ScheduleId::new()),
    )
    .await;
    assert_eq!(status, axum::http::StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED);
}

/// A cryptographically valid signature from a service the receiver does not
/// expect is still a refusal.
#[tokio::test]
async fn an_unexpected_service_is_refused() {
    let status = post_internal(
        inmemory_state(),
        "mas-not-a-service",
        SECRET,
        &Timestamp::now(),
        &run_body(TenantId::new(), ScheduleId::new()),
    )
    .await;
    assert_eq!(status, axum::http::StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED);
}

/// A receiver with no secret refuses rather than trusting the network.
#[tokio::test]
async fn an_unconfigured_receiver_refuses_every_internal_call() {
    let mut state = inmemory_state();
    state.internal_secret = None;
    let status = post_internal(
        state,
        "mas-scheduler",
        SECRET,
        &Timestamp::now(),
        &run_body(TenantId::new(), ScheduleId::new()),
    )
    .await;
    assert_eq!(status, axum::http::StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED);
}

/// A correctly signed call for an unreachable tenant is a `404`, not a `403`:
/// existence is not disclosed.
#[tokio::test]
async fn a_signed_call_for_an_unreachable_tenant_is_not_found() {
    let status = post_internal(
        inmemory_state(),
        "mas-scheduler",
        SECRET,
        &Timestamp::now(),
        &run_body(TenantId::new(), ScheduleId::new()),
    )
    .await;
    assert_eq!(status, axum::http::StatusCode::NOT_FOUND);
}

/// A signature over one body must not authorize a different body.
#[tokio::test]
async fn a_signature_does_not_authorize_a_different_body() {
    let body = run_body(TenantId::new(), ScheduleId::new());
    let signature = sign(SECRET.as_bytes(), "mas-scheduler", &Timestamp::now(), b"{}");
    let app = mas_api::router::router(inmemory_state());
    let response = app
        .oneshot(
            axum::http::Request::builder()
                .method("POST")
                .uri("/v1/internal/schedule-runs")
                .header("content-type", "application/json")
                .header(SIGNATURE_HEADER, signature)
                .header(SERVICE_HEADER, "mas-scheduler")
                .body(axum::body::Body::from(body))
                .expect("request"),
        )
        .await
        .expect("response");
    assert_eq!(response.status(), axum::http::StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED);
}

/// Internal headers carry identity only: never tenancy.
#[tokio::test]
async fn internal_headers_can_never_carry_tenancy() {
    assert_eq!(SIGNATURE_HEADER, "x-mas-internal-signature");
    assert_eq!(SERVICE_HEADER, "x-mas-internal-service");
    for header in [SIGNATURE_HEADER, SERVICE_HEADER] {
        assert!(
            !header.contains("tenant") && !header.contains("org"),
            "{header} must never be able to carry a scope"
        );
    }
}

// ── 5. Scoped transactions ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// Outside a request there is no scope: a query run there cannot see rows.
#[tokio::test]
async fn there_is_no_scope_outside_a_request() {
    assert!(
        !mas_persistence::scoped_request::has_scope(),
        "no transaction-local scope may exist outside a request"
    );
}

/// Scope is task-local. A sibling task on another connection must not inherit
/// it, which is the pooled-connection leak the phase prevents.
#[tokio::test]
async fn scope_does_not_leak_to_a_sibling_task() {
    let handle = tokio::spawn(async { mas_persistence::scoped_request::has_scope() });
    assert!(
        !handle.await.expect("task"),
        "scope must be task-local, never ambient"
    );
}

// ── 6. Cross-tenant and cross-project containment ───────────────────────────

/// The matrix that matters: for every read and write verb, a principal bound
/// to tenant A is denied on tenant B.
#[tokio::test]
async fn no_principal_crosses_a_tenant_boundary() {
    let mine = TenantId::new();
    let theirs = TenantId::new();
    let organization = OrganizationId::new();
    let principal = user(
        "cross",
        vec![membership(organization, mine, MembershipRole::Owner)],
    );
    for action in [
        Action::Read,
        Action::Create,
        Action::Update,
        Action::Delete,
        Action::Execute,
        Action::Cancel,
    ] {
        for resource in [
            ResourceKind::Execution,
            ResourceKind::Agent,
            ResourceKind::Workflow,
            ResourceKind::Schedule,
            ResourceKind::Credential,
            ResourceKind::ApiKey,
            ResourceKind::Audit,
        ] {
            let decision = AuthorizationService.authorize(
                &principal,
                &request(resource, action, theirs, organization, None),
            );
            assert!(
                matches!(decision, AuthorizationDecision::Deny(_)),
                "{action:?} on {resource:?} must not cross tenants"
            );
        }
    }
}

/// A project the directory has not proven to belong to the tenant is not a
/// scope a principal can name.
#[tokio::test]
async fn an_unproven_project_is_not_a_valid_scope() {
    let tenant = TenantId::new();
    let organization = OrganizationId::new();
    let foreign_project = ProjectId::new();
    let owner = user(
        "o",
        vec![membership(organization, tenant, MembershipRole::Owner)],
    );
    let decision = AuthorizationService.authorize(
        &owner,
        &request(
            ResourceKind::Execution,
            Action::Create,
            tenant,
            organization,
            Some(foreign_project),
        ),
    );
    assert!(
        matches!(
            deny_kind(&decision),
            Some(AuthFailureKind::ProjectMismatch)
        ),
        "an unproven project must be refused, not assumed"
    );
}

/// A proven project is accepted — the check narrows, it does not merely deny.
#[tokio::test]
async fn a_proven_project_is_accepted() {
    let tenant = TenantId::new();
    let organization = OrganizationId::new();
    let project = ProjectId::new();
    let mut owner = user(
        "o",
        vec![membership(organization, tenant, MembershipRole::Owner)],
    );
    owner.prove_project(tenant, project);
    let decision = AuthorizationService.authorize(
        &owner,
        &request(
            ResourceKind::Execution,
            Action::Create,
            tenant,
            organization,
            Some(project),
        ),
    );
    assert!(
        matches!(decision, AuthorizationDecision::Allow { .. }),
        "a proven project must not be refused"
    );
}

/// The tenant a credential is bound to is not a scope it can widen: binding
/// to A while asking for B is a mismatch, not a grant.
#[tokio::test]
async fn a_credential_bound_to_one_tenant_cannot_act_in_another() {
    let bound = TenantId::new();
    let other = TenantId::new();
    let organization = OrganizationId::new();
    let key = SecurityPrincipal::new(
        "key-1",
        PrincipalKind::ApiKey,
        Some(bound),
        ScopeSet::denied(),
    )
    .with_memberships(vec![membership(organization, bound, MembershipRole::Admin)]);
    let decision = AuthorizationService.authorize(
        &key,
        &request(
            ResourceKind::Execution,
            Action::Create,
            other,
            organization,
            None,
        ),
    );
    assert!(matches!(decision, AuthorizationDecision::Deny(_)));
}

/// The same principal, in its own tenant, is allowed — proving the denials
/// above are about scope and not about a broken allow-list.
#[tokio::test]
async fn the_same_principal_is_allowed_inside_its_own_tenant() {
    let tenant = TenantId::new();
    let organization = OrganizationId::new();
    let owner = user(
        "o",
        vec![membership(organization, tenant, MembershipRole::Owner)],
    );
    let decision = AuthorizationService.authorize(
        &owner,
        &request(
            ResourceKind::Execution,
            Action::Create,
            tenant,
            organization,
            None,
        ),
    );
    assert!(matches!(decision, AuthorizationDecision::Allow { .. }));
}

/// Every role's grants are explicit. A role that can do everything is a bug,
/// not a convenience.
#[tokio::test]
async fn no_role_holds_every_action_on_every_resource() {
    let all_resources = [
        ResourceKind::Execution,
        ResourceKind::Task,
        ResourceKind::Workflow,
        ResourceKind::Agent,
        ResourceKind::Tool,
        ResourceKind::Connector,
        ResourceKind::Credential,
        ResourceKind::Policy,
        ResourceKind::Usage,
        ResourceKind::Audit,
        ResourceKind::Webhook,
        ResourceKind::Subscription,
        ResourceKind::ApiKey,
        ResourceKind::Schedule,
        ResourceKind::Tenant,
        ResourceKind::Organization,
        ResourceKind::Project,
        ResourceKind::Membership,
    ];
    let all_actions = [
        Action::Read,
        Action::Create,
        Action::Update,
        Action::Delete,
        Action::Execute,
        Action::Cancel,
        Action::Publish,
        Action::Administer,
        Action::ManageCredentials,
        Action::ManagePolicies,
        Action::ViewAudit,
        Action::ManageBilling,
        Action::ManageMembers,
    ];
    for role in [
        MembershipRole::Owner,
        MembershipRole::Admin,
        MembershipRole::Developer,
        MembershipRole::Operator,
        MembershipRole::Viewer,
        MembershipRole::ServiceAccount,
    ] {
        let mut held = 0usize;
        for resource in &all_resources {
            for action in &all_actions {
                if AuthorizationService::role_permits(&role, *resource, *action) {
                    held += 1;
                }
            }
        }
        let total = all_resources.len() * all_actions.len();
        assert!(
            held < total,
            "{role:?} holds every action on every resource ({held}/{total}); \
             capabilities must be explicit"
        );
    }
}

/// The twelve-plus resource taxonomy the phase requires actually exists and is
/// distinct on the wire.
#[tokio::test]
async fn the_resource_taxonomy_covers_every_protected_kind() {
    let kinds: Vec<&str> = [
        ResourceKind::Execution,
        ResourceKind::Task,
        ResourceKind::Workflow,
        ResourceKind::Agent,
        ResourceKind::Tool,
        ResourceKind::Connector,
        ResourceKind::Credential,
        ResourceKind::Policy,
        ResourceKind::Usage,
        ResourceKind::Audit,
        ResourceKind::Webhook,
        ResourceKind::Subscription,
    ]
    .iter()
    .map(ResourceKind::as_str)
    .collect();
    let unique: std::collections::BTreeSet<&str> = kinds.iter().copied().collect();
    assert_eq!(unique.len(), kinds.len(), "resource kinds must be distinct");
    assert!(kinds.len() >= 12, "at least twelve resource kinds required");
}

/// There are at least eight distinct, stable authentication-failure kinds, so
/// a client can tell a refusal apart without a message.
#[tokio::test]
async fn the_failure_taxonomy_has_at_least_eight_distinct_kinds() {
    let kinds = [
        AuthFailureKind::Unauthenticated,
        AuthFailureKind::InvalidCredential,
        AuthFailureKind::ExpiredCredential,
        AuthFailureKind::Forbidden,
        AuthFailureKind::TenantMismatch,
        AuthFailureKind::OrganizationMismatch,
        AuthFailureKind::ProjectMismatch,
        AuthFailureKind::InsufficientPermission,
        AuthFailureKind::InvalidServiceIdentity,
    ];
    use mas_security::AuthFailure;
    let codes: std::collections::BTreeSet<&str> =
        kinds.iter().map(|kind| AuthFailure::new(*kind).code()).collect();
    assert!(
        codes.len() >= 8,
        "at least eight distinct failure codes required, got {codes:?}"
    );
}
```

## FILE: repo/enterprise-mas/rust-core/migrations/0017_plane_roles/up.sql


**PURPOSE:**

```text
The machine-plane database roles (security Phase 14).

Owning layer: the database, applied by the migration runner.

Production responsibility: create `mas_worker`, `mas_outbox` and `mas_audit`
-- the three planes that cannot know a tenant before their query runs -- each
with BYPASSRLS confined to specific tables and operations, and each NOLOGIN
until provisioned. Record on `mas_app` that it must never be granted
BYPASSRLS.

Security boundary: BYPASSRLS is the sharpest privilege in the schema. It is
granted here only to roles that are (a) not reachable at runtime as a login
role, (b) confined by table and operation, and (c) documented in
`pg_description` so an auditor can read WHY without reading the migration.
`mas_app` -- the role request traffic uses -- never receives it.

It must NOT:
• grant BYPASSRLS to `mas_app`;
• make any of these roles LOGIN (provisioning does that, deliberately);
• grant more than the operation a plane actually performs.

Migration 0017 — the machine-plane database roles.

WHY THIS EXISTS (security Phase 14 / RLS policy audit Phase 13)
==============================================================
Every tenant-data table is `ENABLE` + `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, and every
policy reads `app.current_tenant`. That is correct for request traffic,
which always knows its tenant.

Three planes cannot know a tenant in advance:

* the **worker plane** — `SELECT … FROM tasks FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`
deliberately scans every tenant's queue. Its tenant authority is the row
it wins the lease on, which by definition is not known before the query
runs.
* the **outbox plane** — relays rows committed by other transactions, so
the transaction that set the GUC has already ended.
* the **audit plane** — must record a denial *for a tenant the caller was
never scoped to*. Writing that row under the caller's scope is exactly
what RLS forbids, and rightly so; but the event is the evidence that the
denial happened.

Each of these therefore needs a role that is exempt from RLS. The
alternative — granting `BYPASSRLS` to `mas_app` — would switch row-level
security off for the entire platform, which is not a trade worth making.

The exemption is confined three ways, and all three are enforced here:

1. **By role.** Three separate roles, none of which is `mas_app`.
2. **By table.** Each role is granted only the tables its plane touches.
`mas_worker` cannot read `credentials` or `api_keys`; `mas_outbox`
cannot read `tasks`; `mas_audit` can only INSERT.
3. **By operation.** `mas_audit` gets INSERT and nothing else, so an audit
writer cannot rewrite history. `mas_outbox` gets SELECT and UPDATE on
one table.

INVARIANTS
* No superuser is used at runtime. These three roles plus `mas_app` and
`mas_directory` are the complete set.
* No plane role may be used to serve a request. They have no grants on the
tables a request reads (`agents`, `workflows`, `executions` for the
worker's own use aside), and an attempt fails at the database.
* Adding a tenant-data table must NOT widen these grants. The lists below
are explicit for that reason.

MIGRATION PATH (Phase 14, operational)
1. Apply with the migrator role.
2. Provision credentials for each role in the secret manager and grant
LOGIN with them. All three are created `NOLOGIN`, so an unconfigured
deployment cannot authenticate as a plane role by accident.
3. Configure `MAS_DATABASE_WORKER_URL`, `MAS_DATABASE_OUTBOX_URL` and
`MAS_DATABASE_AUDIT_URL`. A deployment that leaves one unset gets the
runtime pool, which means the plane sees no rows under RLS; that fails
visibly and immediately rather than silently.
4. Rotation: rotate the credential, update the secret, reload. The roles
themselves need no change.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Worker plane
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
```


**COMPLETE CONTENT** (155 lines):

```sql
-- PURPOSE: The machine-plane database roles (security Phase 14).
--
-- Owning layer: the database, applied by the migration runner.
--
-- Production responsibility: create `mas_worker`, `mas_outbox` and `mas_audit`
-- -- the three planes that cannot know a tenant before their query runs -- each
-- with BYPASSRLS confined to specific tables and operations, and each NOLOGIN
-- until provisioned. Record on `mas_app` that it must never be granted
-- BYPASSRLS.
--
-- Security boundary: BYPASSRLS is the sharpest privilege in the schema. It is
-- granted here only to roles that are (a) not reachable at runtime as a login
-- role, (b) confined by table and operation, and (c) documented in
-- `pg_description` so an auditor can read WHY without reading the migration.
-- `mas_app` -- the role request traffic uses -- never receives it.
--
-- It must NOT:
--   • grant BYPASSRLS to `mas_app`;
--   • make any of these roles LOGIN (provisioning does that, deliberately);
--   • grant more than the operation a plane actually performs.

-- Migration 0017 — the machine-plane database roles.
--
-- WHY THIS EXISTS (security Phase 14 / RLS policy audit Phase 13)
-- ==============================================================
-- Every tenant-data table is `ENABLE` + `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, and every
-- policy reads `app.current_tenant`. That is correct for request traffic,
-- which always knows its tenant.
--
-- Three planes cannot know a tenant in advance:
--
--   * the **worker plane** — `SELECT … FROM tasks FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`
--     deliberately scans every tenant's queue. Its tenant authority is the row
--     it wins the lease on, which by definition is not known before the query
--     runs.
--   * the **outbox plane** — relays rows committed by other transactions, so
--     the transaction that set the GUC has already ended.
--   * the **audit plane** — must record a denial *for a tenant the caller was
--     never scoped to*. Writing that row under the caller's scope is exactly
--     what RLS forbids, and rightly so; but the event is the evidence that the
--     denial happened.
--
-- Each of these therefore needs a role that is exempt from RLS. The
-- alternative — granting `BYPASSRLS` to `mas_app` — would switch row-level
-- security off for the entire platform, which is not a trade worth making.
--
-- The exemption is confined three ways, and all three are enforced here:
--
--   1. **By role.** Three separate roles, none of which is `mas_app`.
--   2. **By table.** Each role is granted only the tables its plane touches.
--      `mas_worker` cannot read `credentials` or `api_keys`; `mas_outbox`
--      cannot read `tasks`; `mas_audit` can only INSERT.
--   3. **By operation.** `mas_audit` gets INSERT and nothing else, so an audit
--      writer cannot rewrite history. `mas_outbox` gets SELECT and UPDATE on
--      one table.
--
-- INVARIANTS
--   * No superuser is used at runtime. These three roles plus `mas_app` and
--     `mas_directory` are the complete set.
--   * No plane role may be used to serve a request. They have no grants on the
--     tables a request reads (`agents`, `workflows`, `executions` for the
--     worker's own use aside), and an attempt fails at the database.
--   * Adding a tenant-data table must NOT widen these grants. The lists below
--     are explicit for that reason.
--
-- MIGRATION PATH (Phase 14, operational)
--   1. Apply with the migrator role.
--   2. Provision credentials for each role in the secret manager and grant
--      LOGIN with them. All three are created `NOLOGIN`, so an unconfigured
--      deployment cannot authenticate as a plane role by accident.
--   3. Configure `MAS_DATABASE_WORKER_URL`, `MAS_DATABASE_OUTBOX_URL` and
--      `MAS_DATABASE_AUDIT_URL`. A deployment that leaves one unset gets the
--      runtime pool, which means the plane sees no rows under RLS; that fails
--      visibly and immediately rather than silently.
--   4. Rotation: rotate the credential, update the secret, reload. The roles
--      themselves need no change.

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Worker plane
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
DO $$
BEGIN
    IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = 'mas_worker') THEN
        CREATE ROLE mas_worker NOLOGIN BYPASSRLS;
    END IF;
END
$$;

-- The durable execution pipeline only. Deliberately NOT granted: credentials,
-- api_keys, sessions, connectors, webhooks — a compromised worker must not be
-- able to read tenant secrets.
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO mas_worker;
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON tasks TO mas_worker;
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON task_attempts TO mas_worker;
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON executions TO mas_worker;
GRANT SELECT, UPDATE ON execution_steps TO mas_worker;
GRANT SELECT, UPDATE ON outbox_events TO mas_worker;

COMMENT ON ROLE mas_worker IS
    'Durable execution worker plane (security Phase 14). BYPASSRLS is required '
    'because claiming a task scans every tenant''s queue; the tenant authority '
    'is the row the lease is won on. Grants are confined to tasks, '
    'task_attempts, executions, execution_steps and outbox_events — it has no '
    'access to credentials, api_keys or sessions.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Outbox relay plane
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
DO $$
BEGIN
    IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = 'mas_outbox') THEN
        CREATE ROLE mas_outbox NOLOGIN BYPASSRLS;
    END IF;
END
$$;

GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO mas_outbox;
GRANT SELECT, UPDATE ON outbox_events TO mas_outbox;

COMMENT ON ROLE mas_outbox IS
    'Transactional outbox relay (security Phase 14). BYPASSRLS is required '
    'because it relays rows committed by transactions that have already ended. '
    'Grants are SELECT and UPDATE on outbox_events and nothing else.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Audit plane
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
DO $$
BEGIN
    IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = 'mas_audit') THEN
        CREATE ROLE mas_audit NOLOGIN BYPASSRLS;
    END IF;
END
$$;

GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO mas_audit;
-- INSERT only: an audit writer records events, it does not edit them. The
-- append-only triggers on audit_events (migration 0011) already forbid UPDATE
-- and DELETE; this makes the restriction visible in the grant as well.
GRANT INSERT ON audit_events TO mas_audit;

COMMENT ON ROLE mas_audit IS
    'Audit writer (security Phase 14). BYPASSRLS is required to record a '
    'denial for a tenant the caller was never scoped to — the event is the '
    'evidence the denial happened. INSERT only on audit_events.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- A loud record of what the runtime role is NOT
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
COMMENT ON ROLE mas_app IS
    'Application runtime role (security Phase 14). No BYPASSRLS: request '
    'traffic always sets app.current_tenant / app.current_org with SET LOCAL '
    'and is confined by row-level security. Cross-tenant or pre-scope reads '
    'use mas_directory; machine planes use mas_worker, mas_outbox or '
    'mas_audit. Never grant this role BYPASSRLS.';

```

## FILE: repo/enterprise-mas/rust-core/crates/security/src/lib.rs


**PURPOSE:**

```text
The one security crate — principal, scope, authorization,
authentication failures, API keys, secrets, audit and internal-service
authentication.

Owning layer: shared; every crate depends on this one for identity and
authorization decisions.

Production responsibility: hold the single `SecurityPrincipal` type, the
single `AuthorizationService`, the single `AuthoritativeScope`, the single
stable failure taxonomy, and the single internal-service HMAC scheme.

Security boundary: this crate is pure decision logic. It performs no I/O
and reaches no database, so a decision made here is deterministic,
testable, and cannot be widened by a caller who controls storage.

It must NOT:
• grow a second principal, authorization, or internal-auth type;
• perform I/O — the directory and the repository live elsewhere;
• expose a raw secret through `Debug`, `Display`, or an error message.

Security crate: authentication material, secret access control, and the
audit trail every security decision must leave behind.

# Invariants (normative)

1. **Raw secrets never appear in logs, errors or domain objects.** The
only bytes with authority are [`SecretString`]-wrapped; its `Debug`
output is statically redacted, it zeroizes on drop, and reading it
requires the explicit `expose()` verb.
2. **Secret resolution is gated.** All resolution flows through
[`SecretGate`]: retirement/availability checks, optional TTL caching
and a mandatory audit record of *who resolved what for which
purpose* (never the material itself).
3. **API keys are bearer hashes end-to-end.** Raw keys exist only at
creation time and inside the caller's hand; persistence knows the
SHA-256 digest and the 8-char visible prefix only
([`ApiKeyService`]). Verification compares in constant time.
4. **Token validation is explicit and narrow.** [`JwtValidator`]
enforces HS256-only verification with issuer/audience/expiry
pinning — `alg: none` and scheme ambiguity are hard failures.
5. **Scopes are the least-privilege surface.** [`ScopeSet`] pattern
matching (`resource:verb`, wildcard tails) is the single rule used by
API keys, tokens and principals.
```

**COMPLETE CONTENT** (219 lines):

```rust
//! PURPOSE: Process state shared by every handler — the application services,
//! the token verifier, the health registry and build identity.
//!
//! Owning layer: `mas-api` (the process edge).
//!
//! Production responsibility: build the object graph exactly once at bootstrap
//! and share it `Arc`-wise, so there is one instance of each service per
//! process and no per-request construction cost or per-request divergence.
//!
//! It must NOT:
//!   • hold per-request or per-tenant mutable state (that belongs on the
//!     request extensions / service context);
//!   • expose a constructor that silently substitutes an in-memory store when
//!     the production store is unavailable.

//! Process state shared by every handler: the five application services
//! (Arc-shared, since they own boxed store ports), the token verifier, the
//! health registry, and build identity. Constructed ONCE at bootstrap.

use std::sync::Arc;

use mas_application::agent_service::AgentService;
use mas_application::execution_service::ExecutionService;
use mas_application::schedule_service::ScheduleService;
use mas_application::tenancy_service::TenancyService;
use mas_application::workflow_service::WorkflowService;
use mas_observability::health::HealthRegistry;
use sqlx::PgPool;

use crate::auth::TokenVerifierPort;
use crate::scope_resolution::RequestScopeResolver;

/// Everything a request may touch.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct AppState {
    /// Deployment/service identity for health + logs.
    pub service_name: Arc<str>,
    /// Crate/binary version for health payloads.
    pub service_version: Arc<str>,
    /// Bearer-token verification boundary.
    pub verifier: Arc<dyn TokenVerifierPort>,
    /// Request-scope resolution from identity.
    ///
    /// `None` only in the in-memory development lane, which has no directory
    /// to consult. A production process always has one, and
    /// `middleware::authenticated_layer` refuses to resolve scope without it —
    /// it does not fall back to the caller's claims.
    pub scope_resolver: Option<RequestScopeResolver>,
    /// Tenancy/identity use-cases.
    pub tenancy: Arc<TenancyService>,
    /// Agent lifecycle use-cases.
    pub agents: Arc<AgentService>,
    /// Workflow lifecycle use-cases.
    pub workflows: Arc<WorkflowService>,
    /// Execution lifecycle use-cases.
    pub executions: Arc<ExecutionService>,
    /// Schedule lifecycle use-cases.
    pub schedules: Arc<ScheduleService>,
    /// Liveness/readiness probes (observability plane).
    pub health: Arc<HealthRegistry>,
    /// The runtime PostgreSQL pool, when the process is running on
    /// PostgreSQL.
    ///
    /// `None` only in the in-memory lane. When it is `Some`, the middleware
    /// opens one transaction per request with row-level security armed, and
    /// every repository call in that request runs inside it.
    pub runtime_pool: Option<PgPool>,
    /// Shared secret used to authenticate internal service calls.
    ///
    /// `None` means every internal route refuses, rather than trusting the
    /// network. A production process must have one.
    pub internal_secret: Option<mas_security::SecretString>,
}

impl std::fmt::Debug for AppState {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("AppState")
            .field("service_name", &self.service_name)
            .field("service_version", &self.service_version)
            .finish_non_exhaustive()
    }
}

impl AppState {
    /// Composition root (services arrive fully wired).
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub fn new(
        service_name: &str,
        service_version: &str,
        verifier: Arc<dyn TokenVerifierPort>,
        scope_resolver: Option<RequestScopeResolver>,
        tenancy: Arc<TenancyService>,
        agents: Arc<AgentService>,
        workflows: Arc<WorkflowService>,
        executions: Arc<ExecutionService>,
        schedules: Arc<ScheduleService>,
        health: Arc<HealthRegistry>,
        runtime_pool: Option<PgPool>,
        internal_secret: Option<mas_security::SecretString>,
    ) -> Self {
        Self {
            service_name: service_name.into(),
            service_version: service_version.into(),
            verifier,
            scope_resolver,
            tenancy,
            agents,
            workflows,
            executions,
            schedules,
            health,
            runtime_pool,
            internal_secret,
        }
    }
}

/// Shared in-memory wiring for this crate's tests (and any downstream
/// handler tests): all services over ONE `InMemoryServices` +
/// `InMemoryAuditSink`, plus a `StaticTokenVerifier` with `test-token`.
#[cfg(any(test, feature = "testutils"))]
pub mod test_support {
    use std::sync::Arc;

    use mas_application::agent_service::AgentService;
    use mas_application::audit::InMemoryAuditSink;
    use mas_application::durable_memory::InMemoryDurableExecution;
    use mas_application::execution_service::ExecutionService;
    use mas_application::schedule_service::ScheduleService;
    use mas_application::stores::InMemoryServices;
    use mas_application::tenancy_service::TenancyService;
    use mas_application::workflow_service::WorkflowService;
    use mas_observability::health::HealthRegistry;

    use super::AppState;
    use crate::auth::StaticTokenVerifier;
    use mas_security::{PrincipalKind, ScopeSet, SecurityPrincipal};

    /// Fresh, fully-wired state over one shared in-memory store.
    pub fn inmemory_state() -> AppState {
        let store = Arc::new(InMemoryServices::new());
        let audit = Arc::new(InMemoryAuditSink::new());
        let tenancy = Arc::new(TenancyService::new(
            Box::new(store.clone()),
            Box::new(store.clone()),
            Box::new(store.clone()),
            Box::new(store.clone()),
            Box::new(store.clone()),
            Box::new(audit.clone()),
        ));
        let agents = Arc::new(AgentService::new(
            Box::new(store.clone()),
            Box::new(store.clone()),
            Box::new(store.clone()),
            Box::new(audit.clone()),
        ));
        let workflows = Arc::new(WorkflowService::new(
            Box::new(store.clone()),
            Box::new(store.clone()),
            Box::new(audit.clone()),
        ));
        // The durable port is mandatory. The in-memory implementation is
        // accepted here only because this is the crate's test harness — the
        // production composition root wires `PgDurableExecution`.
        let durable = Arc::new(InMemoryDurableExecution::new());
        let executions = Arc::new(ExecutionService::new(
            Box::new(store.clone()),
            Box::new(store.clone()),
            Box::new(store.clone()),
            Box::new(audit.clone()),
            durable,
        ));
        let schedules = Arc::new(ScheduleService::new(
            Box::new(store.clone()),
            Box::new(audit),
        ));
        let verifier = Arc::new(StaticTokenVerifier::new().with_token(
            "test-token",
            SecurityPrincipal::new(
                uuid::Uuid::now_v7().to_string(),
                PrincipalKind::User,
                None,
                ScopeSet::denied(),
            ),
        ));
        // The test lane resolves scope from identity too, over the same
        // in-memory store the tenancy service writes to. Resolving from the
        // header here would make this crate's tests unable to detect the
        // defect this phase exists to fix.
        let scope_resolver = Some(crate::scope_resolution::RequestScopeResolver::new(
            mas_tenancy::TenantResolver::new(
                Arc::new(crate::inmemory_directory::InMemoryTenantDirectory::new(
                    store.clone(),
                )),
                Arc::new(crate::inmemory_directory::InMemoryMembershipDirectory::new(
                    store,
                )),
            ),
        ));
        AppState::new(
            "mas-api-test",
            env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"),
            verifier,
            scope_resolver,
            tenancy,
            agents,
            workflows,
            executions,
            schedules,
            Arc::new(HealthRegistry::new()),
            None,
            // Internal routes in the in-memory test lane are exercised with a
            // fixed secret that is not a production credential.
            Some(mas_security::SecretString::new(
                "inmemory-internal-secret".to_owned(),
            )),
        )
    }
}
```

```rust
//! PURPOSE: `mas-api` process bootstrap: HTTP + gRPC servers over the
//! application layer with graceful shutdown.
//!
//! Owning layer: `mas-api` (the process edge).
//!
//! Production responsibility: compose the real object graph once, bind the
//! listeners, install health/readiness probes, and shut down without dropping
//! in-flight requests. The `--dev-inmemory` lane exists for local bring-up and
//! is unreachable unless the flag is passed explicitly — production must never
//! start stateless by accident.
//!
//! It must NOT:
//!   • contain request handling, business rules or SQL;
//!   • construct stores directly — composition comes from `state.rs`;
//!   • treat a missing production dependency as "start with a fallback".

//! `mas-api` process bootstrap: HTTP + gRPC servers over the application
//! layer with graceful shutdown.
//!
//! Two bring-up modes:
//! * `--dev-inmemory` — everything over `InMemoryServices` (local bring-up,
//!   NO persistence). Requires explicit flag so production never starts up
//!   stateless by accident.
//! * (default) — full production composition: PostgreSQL-backed stores via
//!   `mas_persistence::PgServices`, `engine` audit on `PostgresAuditLog`,
//!   bearer auth via `PostgresApiKeyVerifier`, migration verification at
//!   boot (deterministic fail-fast on drift; `MAS_DATABASE_MIGRATE_ON_BOOT`
//!   enables the deliberate apply path), and the DB dependency probe on the
//!   readiness surface.
//!
//! Environment:
//! * `MAS_API_HTTP_ADDR` (default `0.0.0.0:8080`)
//! * `MAS_API_GRPC_ADDR` (default `0.0.0.0:50051`)
//! * `MAS_DEV_TOKENS` (`token:subject:kind,...`; only with `--dev-inmemory`)

use std::net::SocketAddr;
use std::sync::Arc;

use mas_api::auth::{PrincipalKind, StaticTokenVerifier};
use mas_api::server::ServerConfig;
use mas_api::state::AppState;
use mas_application::agent_service::AgentService;
use mas_application::audit::InMemoryAuditSink;
use mas_application::execution_service::ExecutionService;
use mas_application::schedule_service::ScheduleService;
use mas_application::stores::InMemoryServices;
use mas_application::tenancy_service::TenancyService;
use mas_application::workflow_service::WorkflowService;
use mas_observability::health::HealthRegistry;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    std::process::exit(match run().await {
        Ok(0) => 0,
        Ok(_) => 0,
        Err(err) => {
            eprintln!("mas-api: {err}");
            2
        },
    });
}

async fn run() -> Result<i32, String> {
    let dev_inmemory = std::env::args().skip(1).any(|arg| arg == "--dev-inmemory");

    let layered = mas_common::config::load_layered().map_err(|err| format!("config: {err}"))?;
    let merger = mas_common::config::Merger::new(&layered);
    let http_addr = parse_addr_value(
        merger.string(
            "MAS_API_HTTP_ADDR",
            "server.http_addr",
            &ServerConfig::default().http_addr.to_string(),
        ),
        "MAS_API_HTTP_ADDR",
    )?;
    let grpc_addr = parse_addr_value(
        merger.string(
            "MAS_API_GRPC_ADDR",
            "server.grpc_addr",
            &ServerConfig::default().grpc_addr.to_string(),
        ),
        "MAS_API_GRPC_ADDR",
    )?;
    let _ = (&http_addr, &grpc_addr); // listener bind-up ships with compose path below

    // Production guardrails (dev flags are exactly the ones documented in
    // config/production.toml's header).
    if environment_string(&merger) == "production" {
        enforce_production_guardrails(&merger.string("MAS_DEV_TOKENS", "server.dev_tokens", ""))?;
    }

    let (
        tenancy,
        agents,
        workflows,
        executions,
        schedules,
        verifier,
        scope_resolver,
        runtime_pool,
        internal_secret,
        health,
    ) = if dev_inmemory {
        compose_inmemory(&merger)?
    } else {
        compose_production(&merger).await?
    };

    // ── Production-mode guardrails: dev affordances are forbidden even
    //    outside `environment == "production"` — non-dev wiring is always
    //    durable and must never accept static tokens. ──────────────────
    if !dev_inmemory {
        enforce_production_guardrails(&merger.string("MAS_DEV_TOKENS", "server.dev_tokens", ""))?;
    }

    let state = AppState::new(
        "mas-api",
        env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"),
        verifier,
        scope_resolver,
        tenancy,
        agents,
        workflows,
        executions,
        schedules,
        health,
        // One transaction per request, with row-level security armed inside
        // it. `None` in the in-memory lane only.
        runtime_pool,
        // Internal-call authentication. `None` ⇒ every internal route
        // refuses, rather than trusting the network.
        internal_secret,
    );

    let (http_addr, grpc_addr) = (
        parse_addr_value(
            merger.string(
                "MAS_API_HTTP_ADDR",
                "server.http_addr",
                &ServerConfig::default().http_addr.to_string(),
            ),
            "MAS_API_HTTP_ADDR",
        )?,
        parse_addr_value(
            merger.string(
                "MAS_API_GRPC_ADDR",
                "server.grpc_addr",
                &ServerConfig::default().grpc_addr.to_string(),
            ),
            "MAS_API_GRPC_ADDR",
        )?,
    );

    eprintln!(
        "mas-api starting mode={} http={http_addr} grpc={grpc_addr}",
        if dev_inmemory {
            "--dev-inmemory"
        } else {
            "production"
        }
    );
    mas_api::server::serve(
        state,
        ServerConfig {
            http_addr,
            grpc_addr,
        },
    )
    .await
    .map_err(|err| err.to_string())?;
    Ok(0)
}

type ServiceSet = (
    Arc<TenancyService>,
    Arc<AgentService>,
    Arc<WorkflowService>,
    Arc<ExecutionService>,
    Arc<ScheduleService>,
    Arc<dyn mas_api::auth::TokenVerifierPort>,
    Option<mas_api::scope_resolution::RequestScopeResolver>,
    // The runtime PostgreSQL pool (`None` in the in-memory lane).
    Option<sqlx::PgPool>,
    // The shared secret internal services authenticate with (`None` means
    // every internal route refuses; see `handlers::internal`).
    Option<mas_security::SecretString>,
    Arc<HealthRegistry>,
);

/// Reads the shared secret used to authenticate internal service calls.
///
/// The value is a credential, so it comes only from configuration or the
/// environment — never a command-line argument, which would place it in the
/// process table and in shell history. An absent secret is not an error at
/// boot: it is reported, and every internal route then refuses, which is the
/// fail-closed behaviour.
fn load_internal_secret(
    merger: &mas_common::config::Merger<'_>,
) -> Result<Option<mas_security::SecretString>, String> {
    let raw = merger.string(
        "MAS_INTERNAL_SERVICE_SECRET",
        "security.internal_service_secret",
        "",
    );
    if raw.trim().is_empty() {
        eprintln!(
            "mas-api: MAS_INTERNAL_SERVICE_SECRET is not set — \
             /v1/internal/* will reject every request"
        );
        return Ok(None);
    }
    Ok(Some(mas_security::SecretString::new(raw)))
}

fn compose_inmemory(merger: &mas_common::config::Merger<'_>) -> Result<ServiceSet, String> {
    let store = Arc::new(InMemoryServices::new());
    let audit = Arc::new(InMemoryAuditSink::new());
    let tenancy = Arc::new(TenancyService::new(
        Box::new(store.clone()),
        Box::new(store.clone()),
        Box::new(store.clone()),
        Box::new(store.clone()),
        Box::new(store.clone()),
        Box::new(audit.clone()),
    ));
    let agents = Arc::new(AgentService::new(
        Box::new(store.clone()),
        Box::new(store.clone()),
        Box::new(store.clone()),
        Box::new(audit.clone()),
    ));
    let workflows = Arc::new(WorkflowService::new(
        Box::new(store.clone()),
        Box::new(store.clone()),
        Box::new(audit.clone()),
    ));
    let executions = Arc::new(ExecutionService::new(
        Box::new(store.clone()),
        Box::new(store.clone()),
        Box::new(store.clone()),
        Box::new(audit.clone()),
        Arc::new(mas_application::durable_memory::InMemoryDurableExecution::new()),
    ));
    let schedules = Arc::new(ScheduleService::new(Box::new(store), Box::new(audit)));
    let _ = merger;

    let verifier: Arc<dyn mas_api::auth::TokenVerifierPort> = Arc::new(dev_verifier()?);
    // The in-memory lane still resolves scope from identity — over an
    // in-memory directory rather than PostgreSQL. Resolving from a header here
    // would make the development lane behave differently from production in
    // exactly the way that hides bugs until deploy.
    let scope_resolver = Some(mas_api::scope_resolution::RequestScopeResolver::new(
        mas_tenancy::TenantResolver::new(
            Arc::new(mas_tenancy::InMemoryDirectory::new()),
            Arc::new(mas_tenancy::InMemoryMemberships::new()),
        ),
    ));
    Ok((
        tenancy,
        agents,
        workflows,
        executions,
        schedules,
        verifier,
        scope_resolver,
        None,
        load_internal_secret(merger)?,
        Arc::new(HealthRegistry::new()),
    ))
}

/// Production composition: durable everything, dev affordances rejected.
async fn compose_production(merger: &mas_common::config::Merger<'_>) -> Result<ServiceSet, String> {
    use mas_persistence::pool::{Database, DatabaseUrl, PoolConfig};
    use mas_persistence::repositories::api_keys::ApiKeyStore;
    use mas_persistence::repositories::audit::PostgresAuditLog;
    use mas_persistence::repositories::services::PgServices;
    use mas_persistence::repositories::PgDurableExecution;

    let url = merger.string("MAS_DATABASE_URL", "database.url", "");
    if url.is_empty() {
        return Err(
            "production mode requires a database URL (config database.url or MAS_DATABASE_URL); \
             local bring-up uses --dev-inmemory"
                .to_owned(),
        );
    }
    let max_connections = merger
        .u64("MAS_DATABASE_MAX_CONNS", "database.max_connections", 32)
        .map_err(|err| format!("config: {err}"))?;
    let url_holder = DatabaseUrl::new(url).map_err(|err| format!("database url: {err}"))?;
    let mut config = PoolConfig::for_url(url_holder, "mas-api")
        .map_err(|err| format!("database config: {err}"))?;
    config.max_connections = u32::try_from(max_connections).unwrap_or(32);
    let config = config
        .validated()
        .map_err(|err| format!("database config: {err}"))?;
    let database = Database::connect(&config)
        .await
        .map_err(|err| format!("database: {err}"))?;

    // ── Migration ledger verification (migrate-on-boot is opt-in) ─────
    let pool = database.pool().clone();
    let runner = mas_persistence::migrations::MigrationRunner::new(pool.clone());
    runner
        .ensure_table()
        .await
        .map_err(|err| format!("migrations: {err}"))?;
    let migrate_on_boot = merger
        .bool(
            "MAS_DATABASE_MIGRATE_ON_BOOT",
            "database.migrate_on_boot",
            false,
        )
        .map_err(|err| format!("config: {err}"))?;
    if migrate_on_boot {
        let applied = runner
            .migrate()
            .await
            .map_err(|err| format!("migrate: {err}"))?;
        eprintln!("mas-api: {} migration(s) applied on boot", applied.len());
    } else {
        runner.verify().await.map_err(|err| {
            format!(
                "migration ledger drift — apply migrations first (scripts/migrate.sh up): {err}"
            )
        })?;
    }

    // ── Audit plane ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    //
    // Audit events are appended on their own pool, as `mas_audit` — a role
    // with INSERT on `audit_events` and nothing else (migration 0017). Two
    // reasons, both load-bearing:
    //
    //   1. A denial must be recordable for a tenant the caller was never
    //      scoped to. That is exactly what row-level security forbids on the
    //      runtime role, and rightly so: the audit row is the evidence the
    //      denial happened, so it cannot be subject to the check that caused
    //      it.
    //   2. An audit event must survive the rollback of the mutation it
    //      describes. Writing it inside the request transaction would erase
    //      the record of an attempt that failed.
    //
    // There is no fallback to the runtime pool: under `mas_app` the INSERT
    // would be refused by the table's own policy, and dropping audit events
    // silently is not a failure mode worth having.
    let audit_url = merger.string("MAS_DATABASE_AUDIT_URL", "database.audit_url", "");
    if audit_url.is_empty() {
        return Err("production mode requires an audit database URL \
             (config database.audit_url or MAS_DATABASE_AUDIT_URL) \
             for the mas_audit role; see migrations/0017_plane_roles"
            .to_owned());
    }
    let audit_url_holder =
        DatabaseUrl::new(audit_url).map_err(|err| format!("audit database url: {err}"))?;
    let mut audit_config = PoolConfig::for_url(audit_url_holder, "mas-api-audit")
        .map_err(|err| format!("audit database config: {err}"))?;
    audit_config.max_connections = u32::try_from(max_connections).unwrap_or(32).min(8);
    let audit_config = audit_config
        .validated()
        .map_err(|err| format!("audit database config: {err}"))?;
    let audit_database = Database::connect(&audit_config)
        .await
        .map_err(|err| format!("audit database: {err}"))?;
    let audit_pool = audit_database.pool().clone();

    // ── Durable ports (each Box owns a cheap pool handle clone) ───────
    let tenancy = Arc::new(TenancyService::new(
        Box::new(PgServices::new(pool.clone())),
        Box::new(PgServices::new(pool.clone())),
        Box::new(PgServices::new(pool.clone())),
        Box::new(PgServices::new(pool.clone())),
        Box::new(PgServices::new(pool.clone())),
        Box::new(PostgresAuditLog::new(audit_pool.clone())),
    ));
    let agents = Arc::new(AgentService::new(
        Box::new(PgServices::new(pool.clone())),
        Box::new(PgServices::new(pool.clone())),
        Box::new(PgServices::new(pool.clone())),
        Box::new(PostgresAuditLog::new(audit_pool.clone())),
    ));
    let workflows = Arc::new(WorkflowService::new(
        Box::new(PgServices::new(pool.clone())),
        Box::new(PgServices::new(pool.clone())),
        Box::new(PostgresAuditLog::new(audit_pool.clone())),
    ));
    // The durable port is Postgres: submission, claiming, settlement and
    // cancellation all run as one transaction each against the same pool the
    // rest of the service uses.
    let executions = Arc::new(ExecutionService::new(
        Box::new(PgServices::new(pool.clone())),
        Box::new(PgServices::new(pool.clone())),
        Box::new(PgServices::new(pool.clone())),
        Box::new(PostgresAuditLog::new(audit_pool.clone())),
        Arc::new(PgDurableExecution::new(pool.clone())),
    ));
    let schedules = Arc::new(ScheduleService::new(
        Box::new(PgServices::new(pool.clone())),
        Box::new(PostgresAuditLog::new(audit_pool.clone())),
    ));

    let verifier: Arc<dyn mas_api::auth::TokenVerifierPort> = Arc::new(
        mas_api::prod_auth::PostgresApiKeyVerifier::new(ApiKeyStore::new(pool.clone())),
    );

    // ── Tenancy directory (the one unscoped read path) ────────────────
    //
    // Resolving which tenant a principal may reach has to happen before a
    // scope exists, and every directory table is RLS-protected. So the
    // directory runs on its own pool, as `mas_directory` — a role with SELECT
    // on four catalog tables and nothing else. There is deliberately no
    // fallback to the runtime pool: under `mas_app` those reads would return
    // zero rows, and "tenant not found" is a far worse failure than a loud
    // configuration error.
    let directory_url = merger.string("MAS_DATABASE_DIRECTORY_URL", "database.directory_url", "");
    if directory_url.is_empty() {
        return Err("production mode requires a directory database URL \
             (config database.directory_url or MAS_DATABASE_DIRECTORY_URL) \
             for the mas_directory role; see migrations/0015_directory_role"
            .to_owned());
    }
    let directory_url_holder =
        DatabaseUrl::new(directory_url).map_err(|err| format!("directory database url: {err}"))?;
    let mut directory_config = PoolConfig::for_url(directory_url_holder, "mas-api-directory")
        .map_err(|err| format!("directory database config: {err}"))?;
    directory_config.max_connections = u32::try_from(max_connections).unwrap_or(32).min(8);
    let directory_config = directory_config
        .validated()
        .map_err(|err| format!("directory database config: {err}"))?;
    let directory_database = Database::connect(&directory_config)
        .await
        .map_err(|err| format!("directory database: {err}"))?;
    let directory_pool = directory_database.pool().clone();
    let scope_resolver = Some(mas_api::scope_resolution::RequestScopeResolver::new(
        mas_tenancy::TenantResolver::new(
            Arc::new(mas_persistence::directory::PgTenantDirectory::new(
                directory_pool.clone(),
            )),
            Arc::new(mas_persistence::directory::PgMembershipDirectory::new(
                directory_pool,
            )),
        ),
    ));

    // ── Dependency probe over the same pool ───────────────────────────
    let health = Arc::new(HealthRegistry::new());
    health
        .register(
            mas_observability::health::ProbeKind::Readiness,
            "postgres",
            PgHealthCheck {
                database: database.clone(),
            },
        )
        .map_err(|err| format!("health: {err}"))?;

    Ok((
        tenancy,
        agents,
        workflows,
        executions,
        schedules,
        verifier,
        scope_resolver,
        Some(pool.clone()),
        load_internal_secret(merger)?,
        health,
    ))
}

/// Readiness adapter over the pool's `SELECT 1` probe.
struct PgHealthCheck {
    database: mas_persistence::pool::Database,
}

#[async_trait::async_trait]
impl mas_observability::health::HealthCheckPort for PgHealthCheck {
    async fn check(
        &self,
        at: &mas_common::timestamps::Timestamp,
    ) -> mas_observability::health::ComponentHealth {
        let probe = self.database.probe().await;
        if probe.healthy {
            mas_observability::health::ComponentHealth::up("postgres", at)
                .unwrap_or_else(|_| unreachable!("static name"))
        } else {
            mas_observability::health::ComponentHealth::down(
                "postgres",
                at,
                probe.message.as_deref().unwrap_or("database probe failed"),
            )
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| unreachable!("static name"))
        }
    }
}

/// The production-mode dev-token guardrail, isolated as a pure rule so the
/// binary's test suite pins the exact failure contract: any non-empty
/// `server.dev_tokens` value is refused whenever the process is not
/// explicitly running with `--dev-inmemory`.
fn enforce_production_guardrails(dev_tokens_raw: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
    mas_common::config::refuse_if(
        !dev_tokens_raw.trim().is_empty(),
        "production refuses static dev tokens (config server.dev_tokens must stay empty)",
    )
    .map_err(|err| format!("config guardrail: {err}"))
}

fn parse_addr_value(raw: String, source: &str) -> Result<SocketAddr, String> {
    raw.parse()
        .map_err(|err| format!("{source} invalid ('{raw}'): {err}"))
}

/// Effective `environment` key (MAS_ENV wins via the merger's env layer).
fn environment_string(merger: &mas_common::config::Merger<'_>) -> String {
    merger
        .string("MAS_ENV", "environment", "development")
        .to_ascii_lowercase()
}

/// Builds the development verifier.
///
/// A dev token now declares its tenancy explicitly — `token:subject:kind` for
/// an unbound identity, and the scope resolver then requires such a principal
/// to name a tenant. A dev lane that granted "any tenant" would be a dev lane
/// that cannot reproduce a production authorization bug.
fn dev_verifier() -> Result<StaticTokenVerifier, String> {
    use mas_security::{ScopeSet, SecurityPrincipal};

    let layered = mas_common::config::load_layered().map_err(|err| format!("config: {err}"))?;
    let merger = mas_common::config::Merger::new(&layered);
    let mut verifier = StaticTokenVerifier::new().with_token(
        "dev-token",
        SecurityPrincipal::new(
            uuid::Uuid::now_v7().to_string(),
            PrincipalKind::User,
            None,
            ScopeSet::all(),
        ),
    );
    let table = merger.string("MAS_DEV_TOKENS", "server.dev_tokens", "");
    if !table.is_empty() {
        for entry in table.split(',').filter(|e| !e.trim().is_empty()) {
            let mut parts = entry.splitn(3, ':');
            let (Some(token), Some(subject), Some(kind)) =
                (parts.next(), parts.next(), parts.next())
            else {
                return Err(format!(
                    "MAS_DEV_TOKENS entry '{entry}' malformed (token:subject:kind)"
                ));
            };
            let kind = match kind {
                "user" => PrincipalKind::User,
                "service" => PrincipalKind::ServiceAccount,
                "api_key" => PrincipalKind::ApiKey,
                other => return Err(format!("unknown principal kind '{other}'")),
            };
            verifier = verifier.with_token(
                token,
                SecurityPrincipal::new(subject, kind, None, ScopeSet::all()),
            );
        }
    }
    Ok(verifier)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn production_guardrail_accepts_empty_dev_tokens() {
        assert!(enforce_production_guardrails("").is_ok());
        assert!(enforce_production_guardrails("   ").is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn production_guardrail_refuses_configured_dev_tokens() {
        let err = enforce_production_guardrails("dev-token:sub-a:user")
            .expect_err("static tokens must not survive production mode");
        assert!(err.contains("dev tokens"), "message names the cause: {err}");
        assert!(err.contains("guardrail"), "message names the gate: {err}");
    }
}
```
