```rust
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#[tonic::async_trait]
impl gen::tenancy_api_server::TenancyApi for GrpcServices {
    async fn register_organization(
        &self,
        request: Request<gen::RegisterOrganizationRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<gen::OrganizationReply>, Status> {
        let ctx = context_from(&self.state, request.metadata()).await?;
        let service_ctx = unscoped(&ctx)?;
        let msg = request.into_inner();
        let organization = self
            .state
            .tenancy
            .register_organization(&service_ctx, &msg.legal_name, &msg.display_name, &msg.slug)
            .await
            .map_err(to_status)?;
        Ok(Response::new(gen::OrganizationReply {
            id: organization.id.to_string(),
            legal_name: organization.legal_name.clone(),
            display_name: organization.display_name.clone(),
            slug: organization.slug.as_str().to_owned(),
        }))
    }

    async fn list_organizations(
        &self,
        request: Request<gen::Empty>,
    ) -> Result<Response<gen::ListOrganizationsReply>, Status> {
        let ctx = context_from(&self.state, request.metadata()).await?;
        let service_ctx = unscoped(&ctx)?;
        let organizations = self
            .state
            .tenancy
            .list_organizations(&service_ctx)
            .await
            .map_err(to_status)?;
        Ok(Response::new(gen::ListOrganizationsReply {
            organizations: organizations
                .iter()
                .map(|org| gen::OrganizationReply {
                    id: org.id.to_string(),
                    legal_name: org.legal_name.clone(),
                    display_name: org.display_name.clone(),
                    slug: org.slug.as_str().to_owned(),
                })
                .collect(),
        }))
    }

    async fn register_tenant(
        &self,
        request: Request<gen::RegisterTenantRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<gen::TenantReply>, Status> {
        let ctx = context_from(&self.state, request.metadata()).await?;
        let service_ctx = unscoped(&ctx)?;
        let msg = request.into_inner();
        let environment = serde_json::from_value::<mas_common::enums::Environment>(
            serde_json::Value::String(msg.environment.clone()),
        )
        .map_err(|_| {
            Status::new(
                Code::InvalidArgument,
                "environment: development | staging | production",
            )
        })?;
        let isolation = serde_json::from_value::<mas_domain::IsolationMode>(
            serde_json::Value::String(msg.isolation.clone()),
        )
        .map_err(|_| {
            Status::new(
                Code::InvalidArgument,
                "isolation: shared_rls | schema_per_tenant | dedicated_database",
            )
        })?;
        let tenant = self
            .state
            .tenancy
            .register_tenant(&service_ctx, &msg.name, &msg.slug, environment, isolation)
            .await
            .map_err(to_status)?;
        Ok(Response::new(gen::TenantReply {
            id: tenant.id.to_string(),
            name: tenant.name.clone(),
            slug: tenant.slug.as_str().to_owned(),
            environment: tenant.environment.to_string(),
            isolation: tenant.isolation.to_string(),
        }))
    }

    async fn list_tenants(
        &self,
        request: Request<gen::Empty>,
    ) -> Result<Response<gen::ListTenantsReply>, Status> {
        let ctx = context_from(&self.state, request.metadata()).await?;
        let service_ctx = unscoped(&ctx)?;
        let tenants = self
            .state
            .tenancy
            .list_tenants(&service_ctx)
            .await
            .map_err(to_status)?;
        Ok(Response::new(gen::ListTenantsReply {
            tenants: tenants
                .iter()
                .map(|tenant| gen::TenantReply {
                    id: tenant.id.to_string(),
                    name: tenant.name.clone(),
                    slug: tenant.slug.as_str().to_owned(),
                    environment: tenant.environment.to_string(),
                    isolation: tenant.isolation.to_string(),
                })
                .collect(),
        }))
    }

    async fn register_project(
        &self,
        request: Request<gen::RegisterProjectRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<gen::ProjectReply>, Status> {
        let ctx = context_from(&self.state, request.metadata()).await?;
        let service_ctx = scoped(&ctx)?;
        let msg = request.into_inner();
        let project = scoped_call(
            &self.state,
            &ctx,
            self.state
                .tenancy
                .register_project(&service_ctx, &msg.name, &msg.slug),
        )
        .await?;
        Ok(Response::new(gen::ProjectReply {
            id: project.id.to_string(),
            name: project.name.clone(),
            slug: project.slug.as_str().to_owned(),
        }))
    }

    async fn invite_membership(
        &self,
        request: Request<gen::InviteMembershipRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<gen::MembershipReply>, Status> {
        let ctx = context_from(&self.state, request.metadata()).await?;
        let service_ctx = scoped(&ctx)?;
        let msg = request.into_inner();
        let user_id: UserId = parse_id("user_id", &msg.user_id)?;
        let role = serde_json::from_value::<mas_domain::MembershipRole>(serde_json::Value::String(
            msg.role.clone(),
        ))
        .map_err(|_| {
            Status::new(
                Code::InvalidArgument,
                "role: owner | admin | developer | operator | viewer | service_account",
            )
        })?;
        let membership = scoped_call(
            &self.state,
            &ctx,
            self.state
                .tenancy
                .invite_membership(&service_ctx, user_id, role),
        )
        .await?;
        Ok(Response::new(gen::MembershipReply {
            id: membership.id.to_string(),
            user_id: membership.user_id.to_string(),
            role: membership
                .roles
                .iter()
                .next()
                .map(ToString::to_string)
                .unwrap_or_default(),
            status: membership.status.to_string(),
        }))
    }
}

#[tonic::async_trait]
impl gen::agent_api_server::AgentApi for GrpcServices {
    async fn register_agent(
        &self,
        request: Request<gen::RegisterAgentRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<gen::AgentReply>, Status> {
        let ctx = context_from(&self.state, request.metadata()).await?;
        let service_ctx = scoped(&ctx)?;
        let msg = request.into_inner();
        let project_id: ProjectId = parse_id("project_id", &msg.project_id)?;
        let kind = serde_json::from_value::<mas_domain::AgentKind>(serde_json::Value::String(
            msg.kind.clone(),
        ))
        .map_err(|_| {
            Status::new(
                Code::InvalidArgument,
                "kind: standard | supervisor | tool_user",
            )
        })?;
        let agent = scoped_call(
            &self.state,
            &ctx,
            self.state
                .agents
                .register(&service_ctx, project_id, &msg.name, &msg.slug, kind),
        )
        .await?;
        Ok(Response::new(agent_reply(&agent)))
    }

    async fn publish_agent_version(
        &self,
        request: Request<gen::PublishAgentVersionRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<gen::AgentVersionReply>, Status> {
        let ctx = context_from(&self.state, request.metadata()).await?;
        let service_ctx = scoped(&ctx)?;
        let msg = request.into_inner();
        let agent_id: AgentId = parse_id("agent_id", &msg.agent_id)?;
        let user_id: UserId = parse_id("published_by", &msg.published_by)?;
        let snapshot: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&msg.configuration_snapshot_json)
            .map_err(|_| {
                Status::new(
                    Code::InvalidArgument,
                    "configuration_snapshot_json: not valid JSON",
                )
            })?;
        let version = self
            .state
            .agents
            .publish_version(
                &service_ctx,
                agent_id,
                &msg.configuration_checksum,
                snapshot,
                user_id,
            )
            .await
            .map_err(to_status)?;
        Ok(Response::new(gen::AgentVersionReply {
            id: version.id().to_string(),
            version_number: version.version_number(),
            checksum: version.configuration_checksum().to_owned(),
        }))
    }

    async fn get_agent(
        &self,
        request: Request<gen::GetAgentRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<gen::AgentReply>, Status> {
        let ctx = context_from(&self.state, request.metadata()).await?;
        let service_ctx = scoped(&ctx)?;
        let agent_id: AgentId = parse_id("agent_id", &request.into_inner().agent_id)?;
        let agent = scoped_call(
            &self.state,
            &ctx,
            self.state.agents.get(&service_ctx, agent_id),
        )
        .await?;
        Ok(Response::new(agent_reply(&agent)))
    }

    async fn list_agents(
        &self,
        request: Request<gen::ListAgentsRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<gen::ListAgentsReply>, Status> {
        let ctx = context_from(&self.state, request.metadata()).await?;
        let service_ctx = scoped(&ctx)?;
        let project_id: ProjectId = parse_id("project_id", &request.into_inner().project_id)?;
        let agents = scoped_call(
            &self.state,
            &ctx,
            self.state.agents.list(&service_ctx, project_id),
        )
        .await?;
        Ok(Response::new(gen::ListAgentsReply {
            agents: agents.iter().map(agent_reply).collect(),
        }))
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// WorkflowApi
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#[tonic::async_trait]
impl gen::workflow_api_server::WorkflowApi for GrpcServices {
    async fn create_workflow(
        &self,
        request: Request<gen::CreateWorkflowRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<gen::WorkflowReply>, Status> {
        let ctx = context_from(&self.state, request.metadata()).await?;
        let service_ctx = scoped(&ctx)?;
        let msg = request.into_inner();
        let project_id: ProjectId = parse_id("project_id", &msg.project_id)?;
        let workflow = scoped_call(
            &self.state,
            &ctx,
            self.state
                .workflows
                .create(&service_ctx, project_id, &msg.name),
        )
        .await?;
        Ok(Response::new(gen::WorkflowReply {
            id: workflow.id.to_string(),
            project_id: workflow.project_id.to_string(),
            name: workflow.name.clone(),
            node_count: u32::try_from(workflow.graph.nodes.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX),
            graph_version: workflow.published_version.unwrap_or(0),
        }))
    }

    async fn update_workflow_graph(
        &self,
        request: Request<gen::UpdateWorkflowGraphRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<gen::UpdateWorkflowGraphReply>, Status> {
        let ctx = context_from(&self.state, request.metadata()).await?;
        let service_ctx = scoped(&ctx)?;
        let msg = request.into_inner();
        let workflow_id: WorkflowId = parse_id("workflow_id", &msg.workflow_id)?;
        let mut nodes = Vec::with_capacity(msg.nodes.len());
        for node in &msg.nodes {
            let node_type = serde_json::from_value::<mas_domain::WorkflowNodeType>(
                serde_json::Value::String(node.node_type.clone()),
            )
            .map_err(|_| {
                Status::new(
                    Code::InvalidArgument,
                    "node_type: not a recognized node type",
                )
            })?;
            let config: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> =
                serde_json::from_str(&node.config_json).map_err(|_| {
                    Status::new(Code::InvalidArgument, "config_json: not a JSON object")
                })?;
            let mut built = mas_domain::WorkflowNode::new(&node.node_key, node_type, &node.name)
                .map_err(to_status)?;
            built.config = config;
            nodes.push(built);
        }
        let mut edges = Vec::with_capacity(msg.edges.len());
        for edge in &msg.edges {
            edges.push(
                mas_domain::WorkflowEdge::new(&edge.from_key, &edge.to_key).map_err(to_status)?,
            );
        }
        let order = scoped_call(
            &self.state,
            &ctx,
            self.state
                .workflows
                .update_graph(&service_ctx, workflow_id, nodes, edges),
        )
        .await?;
        Ok(Response::new(gen::UpdateWorkflowGraphReply {
            workflow_id: workflow_id.to_string(),
            topological_order: order,
        }))
    }

    async fn get_workflow(
        &self,
        request: Request<gen::GetWorkflowRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<gen::WorkflowReply>, Status> {
        let ctx = context_from(&self.state, request.metadata()).await?;
        let service_ctx = scoped(&ctx)?;
        let workflow_id: WorkflowId = parse_id("workflow_id", &request.into_inner().workflow_id)?;
        let workflow = scoped_call(
            &self.state,
            &ctx,
            self.state.workflows.get(&service_ctx, workflow_id),
        )
        .await?;
        Ok(Response::new(gen::WorkflowReply {
            id: workflow.id.to_string(),
            project_id: workflow.project_id.to_string(),
            name: workflow.name.clone(),
            node_count: u32::try_from(workflow.graph.nodes.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX),
            graph_version: workflow.published_version.unwrap_or(0),
        }))
    }

    async fn list_workflows(
        &self,
        request: Request<gen::ListWorkflowsRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<gen::ListWorkflowsReply>, Status> {
        let ctx = context_from(&self.state, request.metadata()).await?;
        let service_ctx = scoped(&ctx)?;
        let project_id: ProjectId = parse_id("project_id", &request.into_inner().project_id)?;
        let workflows = scoped_call(
            &self.state,
            &ctx,
            self.state.workflows.list(&service_ctx, project_id),
        )
        .await?;
        Ok(Response::new(gen::ListWorkflowsReply {
            workflows: workflows
                .iter()
                .map(|workflow| gen::WorkflowReply {
                    id: workflow.id.to_string(),
                    project_id: workflow.project_id.to_string(),
                    name: workflow.name.clone(),
                    node_count: u32::try_from(workflow.graph.nodes.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX),
                    graph_version: workflow.published_version.unwrap_or(0),
                })
                .collect(),
        }))
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// ExecutionApi
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#[tonic::async_trait]
impl gen::execution_api_server::ExecutionApi for GrpcServices {
    async fn submit_execution(
        &self,
        request: Request<gen::SubmitExecutionRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<gen::ExecutionReply>, Status> {
        let ctx = context_from(&self.state, request.metadata()).await?;
        let idempotency_key = meta_str(request.metadata(), crate::context::IDEMPOTENCY_HEADER)
            .map(str::trim)
            .filter(|v| !v.is_empty())
            .map(str::to_owned);
        let service_ctx = scoped(&ctx)?;
        let msg = request.into_inner();
        let project_id: ProjectId = parse_id("project_id", &msg.project_id)?;
        let workflow_id: Option<WorkflowId> = match msg.workflow_id {
            Some(raw) => Some(parse_id("workflow_id", &raw)?),
            None => None,
        };
        let agent_id: Option<AgentId> = match msg.agent_id {
            Some(raw) => Some(parse_id("agent_id", &raw)?),
            None => None,
        };
        let input: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&msg.input_json)
            .map_err(|_| Status::new(Code::InvalidArgument, "input_json: not valid JSON"))?;
        let outcome = self
            .state
            .executions
            .submit(
                &service_ctx,
                project_id,
                workflow_id,
                agent_id,
                input,
                idempotency_key.as_deref(),
            )
            .await
            .map_err(to_status)?;
        Ok(Response::new(execution_reply(
            &outcome.execution,
            outcome.replayed,
        )))
    }

    async fn transition_execution(
        &self,
        request: Request<gen::TransitionExecutionRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<gen::ExecutionReply>, Status> {
        let ctx = context_from(&self.state, request.metadata()).await?;
        let service_ctx = scoped(&ctx)?;
        let msg = request.into_inner();
        let execution_id: mas_common::ids::ExecutionId =
            parse_id("execution_id", &msg.execution_id)?;
        let action = gen::TransitionAction::try_from(msg.action)
            .unwrap_or(gen::TransitionAction::Unspecified);
        let execution = match action {
            gen::TransitionAction::Start => {
                self.state
                    .executions
                    .start(&service_ctx, execution_id)
                    .await
            },
            gen::TransitionAction::Pause => {
                self.state
                    .executions
                    .pause(&service_ctx, execution_id)
                    .await
            },
            gen::TransitionAction::Resume => {
                self.state
                    .executions
                    .resume(&service_ctx, execution_id)
                    .await
            },
            gen::TransitionAction::Cancel => {
                self.state
                    .executions
                    .request_cancellation(&service_ctx, execution_id)
                    .await
            },
            gen::TransitionAction::Unspecified => {
                return Err(Status::new(Code::InvalidArgument, "action is required"));
            },
        }
        .map_err(to_status)?;
        Ok(Response::new(execution_reply(&execution, false)))
    }

    async fn get_execution(
        &self,
        request: Request<gen::GetExecutionRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<gen::ExecutionReply>, Status> {
        let ctx = context_from(&self.state, request.metadata()).await?;
        let service_ctx = scoped(&ctx)?;
        let execution_id: mas_common::ids::ExecutionId =
            parse_id("execution_id", &request.into_inner().execution_id)?;
        let execution = scoped_call(
            &self.state,
            &ctx,
            self.state.executions.get(&service_ctx, execution_id),
        )
        .await?;
        Ok(Response::new(execution_reply(&execution, false)))
    }

    async fn list_executions(
        &self,
        request: Request<gen::Empty>,
    ) -> Result<Response<gen::ListExecutionsReply>, Status> {
        let ctx = context_from(&self.state, request.metadata()).await?;
        let service_ctx = scoped(&ctx)?;
        let executions =
            scoped_call(&self.state, &ctx, self.state.executions.list(&service_ctx)).await?;
        Ok(Response::new(gen::ListExecutionsReply {
            executions: executions
                .iter()
                .map(|e| execution_reply(e, false))
                .collect(),
        }))
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// ScheduleApi
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#[tonic::async_trait]
impl gen::schedule_api_server::ScheduleApi for GrpcServices {
    async fn register_schedule(
        &self,
        request: Request<gen::RegisterScheduleRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<gen::ScheduleReply>, Status> {
        let ctx = context_from(&self.state, request.metadata()).await?;
        let service_ctx = scoped(&ctx)?;
        let msg = request.into_inner();
        let project_id = match msg.project_id {
            Some(raw) => Some(parse_id::<ProjectId>("project_id", &raw)?),
            None => None,
        };
        let kind = match msg.kind.as_str() {
            "interval" => mas_domain::ScheduleKind::Interval {
                every_seconds: msg.every_seconds,
            },
            other => {
                return Err(Status::new(
                    Code::InvalidArgument,
                    format!("unsupported schedule kind '{other}' (interval)"),
                ));
            },
        };
        let template: serde_json::Value =
            serde_json::from_str(&msg.task_template_json).map_err(|_| {
                Status::new(Code::InvalidArgument, "task_template_json: not valid JSON")
            })?;
        let schedule = scoped_call(
            &self.state,
            &ctx,
            self.state
                .schedules
                .register(&service_ctx, project_id, &msg.name, kind, template),
        )
        .await?;
        Ok(Response::new(gen::ScheduleReply {
            id: schedule.id.to_string(),
            name: schedule.name.clone(),
            status: schedule.status.to_string(),
        }))
    }

    async fn set_schedule_state(
        &self,
        request: Request<gen::SetScheduleStateRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<gen::ScheduleReply>, Status> {
        let ctx = context_from(&self.state, request.metadata()).await?;
        let service_ctx = scoped(&ctx)?;
        let msg = request.into_inner();
        let schedule_id = parse_str_id("schedule_id", &msg.schedule_id)
            .map(mas_common::ids::ScheduleId::from_uuid)?;
        let schedule = match gen::ScheduleStateAction::try_from(msg.action) {
            Ok(gen::ScheduleStateAction::Pause) => {
                self.state.schedules.pause(&service_ctx, schedule_id).await
            },
            Ok(gen::ScheduleStateAction::Resume) => {
                self.state.schedules.resume(&service_ctx, schedule_id).await
            },
            Ok(gen::ScheduleStateAction::Disable) => {
                self.state
                    .schedules
                    .disable(&service_ctx, schedule_id)
                    .await
            },
            _ => return Err(Status::new(Code::InvalidArgument, "action is required")),
        }
        .map_err(to_status)?;
        Ok(Response::new(gen::ScheduleReply {
            id: schedule.id.to_string(),
            name: schedule.name.clone(),
            status: schedule.status.to_string(),
        }))
    }

    async fn list_schedules(
        &self,
        request: Request<gen::Empty>,
    ) -> Result<Response<gen::ListSchedulesReply>, Status> {
        let ctx = context_from(&self.state, request.metadata()).await?;
        let service_ctx = scoped(&ctx)?;
        let schedules =
            scoped_call(&self.state, &ctx, self.state.schedules.list(&service_ctx)).await?;
        Ok(Response::new(gen::ListSchedulesReply {
            schedules: schedules
                .iter()
                .map(|schedule| gen::ScheduleReply {
                    id: schedule.id.to_string(),
                    name: schedule.name.clone(),
                    status: schedule.status.to_string(),
                })
                .collect(),
        }))
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Tests (in-process, no sockets — the tonic service traits are plain async)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::state::test_support::inmemory_state;
    use mas_common::timestamps::Timestamp;
    use tonic::metadata::MetadataMap;

    fn authed_metadata(tenant: TenantId, organization: OrganizationId) -> MetadataMap {
        let mut metadata = MetadataMap::new();
        metadata.insert("x-tenant-id", tenant.to_string().parse().expect("meta"));
        metadata.insert(
            "x-organization-id",
            organization.to_string().parse().expect("meta"),
        );
        metadata.insert("x-correlation-id", "grpc-it-1".parse().expect("meta"));
        metadata.insert(
            tonic::metadata::MetadataKey::from_static("authorization"),
            tonic::metadata::MetadataValue::from_static("Bearer test-token"),
        );
        metadata
    }

    async fn seed() -> (AppState, TenantId, OrganizationId, ProjectId) {
        let state = inmemory_state();
        let system =
            ServiceContext::for_service("seed", "grpc-seed-1", &Timestamp::now()).expect("ctx");
        let organization = state
            .tenancy
            .register_organization(&system, "Acme Ltd.", "Acme", "acme-grpc")
            .await
            .expect("org");
        let org_scoped = system.clone().with_scope(TenantId::new(), organization.id);
        let tenant = state
            .tenancy
            .register_tenant(
                &org_scoped,
                "Prod",
                "prod-grpc",
                mas_common::enums::Environment::Production,
                mas_domain::IsolationMode::SharedRls,
            )
            .await
            .expect("tenant");
        let tenant_scoped = system.clone().with_scope(tenant.id, organization.id);
        // Provisioned tenants are not operational and the resolver refuses
        // them, so the seed activates the tenant before use.
        state
            .tenancy
            .activate_tenant(&tenant_scoped, tenant.id)
            .await
            .expect("activate");
        let project = state
            .tenancy
            .register_project(&tenant_scoped, "Core", "core-grpc")
            .await
            .expect("project");
        (state, tenant.id, organization.id, project.id)
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn unauthenticated_calls_fail_closed() {
        let (state, tenant, organization, _project) = seed().await;
        let services = GrpcServices::new(state);

        let mut metadata = authed_metadata(tenant, organization);
        metadata.remove("authorization");
        let request = Request::from_parts(metadata, tonic::Extensions::default(), gen::Empty {});
        use gen::execution_api_server::ExecutionApi;
        let denial = services.list_executions(request).await.expect_err("401");
        assert_eq!(denial.code(), Code::Unauthenticated);

        // Malformed scope uuid → InvalidArgument, not a panic.
        let mut metadata = authed_metadata(tenant, organization);
        metadata.insert("x-tenant-id", "not-a-uuid".parse().expect("meta"));
        let request = Request::from_parts(metadata, tonic::Extensions::default(), gen::Empty {});
        let bad_scope = services
            .list_executions(request)
            .await
            .expect_err("invalid argument");
        assert_eq!(bad_scope.code(), Code::InvalidArgument);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn foreign_scope_hides_existence() {
        let (state, tenant, organization, _project) = seed().await;
        let tenant_scoped = ServiceContext::for_service("seed", "grpc-seed-2", &Timestamp::now())
            .expect("ctx")
            .with_scope(tenant, organization);
        let schedule = state
            .schedules
            .register(
                &tenant_scoped,
                None,
                "nightly",
                mas_domain::ScheduleKind::Interval {
                    every_seconds: 3_600,
                },
                serde_json::json!({"wf": "x"}),
            )
            .await
            .expect("register");
        let services = GrpcServices::new(state);

        let foreign_metadata = authed_metadata(TenantId::new(), organization);
        let request = Request::from_parts(
            foreign_metadata,
            tonic::Extensions::default(),
            gen::SetScheduleStateRequest {
                schedule_id: schedule.id.to_string(),
                action: gen::ScheduleStateAction::Pause as i32,
            },
        );
        use gen::schedule_api_server::ScheduleApi;
        let hidden = services.set_schedule_state(request).await.expect_err("404");
        assert_eq!(hidden.code(), Code::NotFound);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn execution_submit_honors_metadata_idempotency() {
        let (state, tenant, organization, project) = seed().await;
        let tenant_scoped = ServiceContext::for_service("seed", "grpc-seed-3", &Timestamp::now())
            .expect("ctx")
            .with_scope(tenant, organization);
        let workflow = state
            .workflows
            .create(&tenant_scoped, project, "g-flow")
            .await
            .expect("workflow");
        let services = GrpcServices::new(state);

        use gen::execution_api_server::ExecutionApi;
        let make = |meta: MetadataMap| {
            Request::from_parts(
                meta,
                tonic::Extensions::default(),
                gen::SubmitExecutionRequest {
                    project_id: project.to_string(),
                    workflow_id: Some(workflow.id.to_string()),
                    agent_id: None,
                    input_json: "{\"job\": \"g\"}".to_owned(),
                },
            )
        };
        let mut first_metadata = authed_metadata(tenant, organization);
        first_metadata.insert("idempotency-key", "grpc-idem-7".parse().expect("meta"));
        let first = services
            .submit_execution(make(first_metadata))
            .await
            .expect("submit");
        let first_ref = first.get_ref();
        assert!(!first_ref.replayed);
        assert_eq!(first_ref.correlation_id, "grpc-it-1", "correlation echoes");

        let mut replay_metadata = authed_metadata(tenant, organization);
        replay_metadata.insert("idempotency-key", "grpc-idem-7".parse().expect("meta"));
        let second = services
            .submit_execution(make(replay_metadata))
            .await
            .expect("replay");
        assert!(second.get_ref().replayed, "same idempotency key replays");
        assert_eq!(second.get_ref().execution_id, first_ref.execution_id);
    }
}
```

## FILE: repo/enterprise-mas/rust-core/crates/security/src/authorization.rs


**PURPOSE:**

```text
The canonical authorization service: the ONE place a "may this
principal do this to that resource?" question is answered.

Owning layer: `mas-security`.

Production responsibility: spec Phase 5 names twelve decisions the platform
must be able to make — read, create, update, delete, execute, cancel,
publish, administer, manage credentials, manage policies, view audit, manage
billing — and forbids scattering ad-hoc role checks through handlers. A
handler may *ask*; only this service decides.

The decision is ABAC-shaped (Phase 7): principal + tenant + organization +
project + resource + operation are all inputs, because "can cancel" is not
one answer — it depends on which execution, in which tenant, under which
role. RBAC (Phase 6) is the role→permission matrix that sits underneath it.

Security boundary: **deny by default.** The permission matrix is an
allow-list; anything not explicitly granted is refused, and an unknown role,
an unknown resource kind or a missing scope all resolve to `Deny`. There is
no code path in this file that returns `Allow` without a matching grant, and
no role inherits permissions implicitly by rank except where the matrix says
so explicitly.

It must NOT:
• trust a role, permission or scope that arrived from the caller — the
role comes from the resolved membership the *server* looked up;
• return `Allow` for a scope mismatch. A grant in tenant A says nothing
about tenant B, and crossing the boundary is a `TenantMismatch`, never a
silent re-scope;
• become a second authorization system. If a check is needed, it belongs
here;
• perform I/O. It is a pure decision function over already-resolved
inputs, so it is deterministic and testable without a database.
```

```rust
// PURPOSE: The canonical authorization service: the ONE place a "may this
// principal do this to that resource?" question is answered.
//
// Owning layer: `mas-security`.
//
// Production responsibility: spec Phase 5 names twelve decisions the platform
// must be able to make — read, create, update, delete, execute, cancel,
// publish, administer, manage credentials, manage policies, view audit, manage
// billing — and forbids scattering ad-hoc role checks through handlers. A
// handler may *ask*; only this service decides.
//
// The decision is ABAC-shaped (Phase 7): principal + tenant + organization +
// project + resource + operation are all inputs, because "can cancel" is not
// one answer — it depends on which execution, in which tenant, under which
// role. RBAC (Phase 6) is the role→permission matrix that sits underneath it.
//
// Security boundary: **deny by default.** The permission matrix is an
// allow-list; anything not explicitly granted is refused, and an unknown role,
// an unknown resource kind or a missing scope all resolve to `Deny`. There is
// no code path in this file that returns `Allow` without a matching grant, and
// no role inherits permissions implicitly by rank except where the matrix says
// so explicitly.
//
// It must NOT:
//   • trust a role, permission or scope that arrived from the caller — the
//     role comes from the resolved membership the *server* looked up;
//   • return `Allow` for a scope mismatch. A grant in tenant A says nothing
//     about tenant B, and crossing the boundary is a `TenantMismatch`, never a
//     silent re-scope;
//   • become a second authorization system. If a check is needed, it belongs
//     here;
//   • perform I/O. It is a pure decision function over already-resolved
//     inputs, so it is deterministic and testable without a database.

use mas_common::ids::{OrganizationId, ProjectId, TenantId};
use mas_common::result::Result;
use mas_common::string_enum;
use mas_domain::MembershipRole;
use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::fmt;

use crate::auth_failure::AuthFailure;
use crate::principal::SecurityPrincipal;

// The twelve (plus) decisions the platform makes about a resource:
// read, create, update, delete, execute, cancel, publish, administer, manage
// credentials, manage policies, view audit, manage billing, plus manage
// members. The wire value of each is part of the API contract.
string_enum! {
    /// A verb on a resource. The wire value is part of the API contract.
    Action {
        Read => "read",
        Create => "create",
        Update => "update",
        Delete => "delete",
        Execute => "execute",
        Cancel => "cancel",
        Publish => "publish",
        Administer => "administer",
        ManageCredentials => "manage_credentials",
        ManagePolicies => "manage_policies",
        ViewAudit => "view_audit",
        ManageBilling => "manage_billing",
        /// Manage memberships (invite, revoke, change role).
        ManageMembers => "manage_members",
    }
}

// What kind of thing the action applies to. Spec Phase 7 requires at
// minimum execution, task, workflow, agent, tool, connector, credential
// metadata, policy, usage, audit, webhook and subscription/entitlement.
string_enum! {
    /// The resource taxonomy. Spec Phase 7 requires at minimum execution, task,
    /// workflow, agent, tool, connector, credential metadata, policy, usage,
    /// audit, webhook and subscription/entitlement.
    ResourceKind {
        Execution => "execution",
        Task => "task",
        Workflow => "workflow",
        Agent => "agent",
        Tool => "tool",
        Connector => "connector",
        Credential => "credential",
        Policy => "policy",
        Usage => "usage",
        Audit => "audit",
        Webhook => "webhook",
        Subscription => "subscription",
        ApiKey => "api_key",
        Schedule => "schedule",
        Tenant => "tenant",
        Organization => "organization",
        Project => "project",
        Membership => "membership",
    }
}

/// The full context of one authorization question.
///
/// Every field is *resolved* — proven by the server from authenticated
/// identity — never echoed from a request header.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct AuthorizationRequest {
    pub resource: ResourceKind,
    pub action: Action,
    /// Tenant the resource lives in (resolved, not claimed).
    pub tenant_id: TenantId,
    /// Organization the tenant belongs to (resolved).
    pub organization_id: OrganizationId,
    /// Project/workspace, when the resource is project-scoped.
    pub project_id: Option<ProjectId>,
}

/// The outcome, with the reason it went that way.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum AuthorizationDecision {
    /// Permitted. Carries which role granted it, for the audit trail.
    Allow { granted_by: MembershipRole },
    /// Refused, with a stable classification.
    Deny(AuthFailure),
}

impl AuthorizationDecision {
    /// `true` only on an explicit grant.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn is_allowed(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Self::Allow { .. })
    }

    /// Converts a denial into a transport error. Panics on `Allow`, which
    /// would be a programming error: callers check `is_allowed` first.
    pub fn into_result(self) -> Result<()> {
        match self {
            Self::Allow { .. } => Ok(()),
            Self::Deny(failure) => Err(failure.to_app_error()),
        }
    }
}

/// The role → (resource, action) permission matrix.
///
/// Written as an explicit allow-list per role. This is deliberately verbose:
/// a compact "rank >= X" scheme is how a viewer ends up able to read audit
/// data six months later. Each role's grants are readable in one place.
const fn role_grants(role: &MembershipRole) -> &'static [(ResourceKind, &'static [Action])] {
    match role {
        // Owner: full control inside the tenant, including deletion of the
        // tenant itself, membership administration and billing.
        MembershipRole::Owner => &[
            (
                ResourceKind::Execution,
                &[
                    Action::Read,
                    Action::Create,
                    Action::Update,
                    Action::Delete,
                    Action::Execute,
                    Action::Cancel,
                    Action::Publish,
                    Action::Administer,

            ),
            (
                ResourceKind::Task,
                &[
                    Action::Read,
                    Action::Update,
                    Action::Delete,
                    Action::Execute,
                    Action::Cancel,
                ],
            ),
            (
                ResourceKind::Workflow,
                &[
                    Action::Read,
                    Action::Create,
                    Action::Update,
                    Action::Delete,
                    Action::Execute,
                    Action::Publish,
                ],
            ),
            (
                ResourceKind::Agent,
                &[
                    Action::Read,
                    Action::Create,
                    Action::Update,
                    Action::Delete,
                    Action::Execute,
                    Action::Publish,
                ],
            ),
            (
                ResourceKind::Tool,
                &[
                    Action::Read,
                    Action::Create,
                    Action::Update,
                    Action::Delete,
                    Action::Execute,
                ],
            ),
            (
                ResourceKind::Connector,
                &[Action::Read, Action::Create, Action::Update, Action::Delete],
            ),
            (
                ResourceKind::Credential,
                &[
                    Action::Read,
                    Action::Create,
                    Action::Update,
                    Action::Delete,
                    Action::ManageCredentials,
                ],
            ),
            (
                ResourceKind::Policy,
                &[
                    Action::Read,
                    Action::Create,
                    Action::Update,
                    Action::Delete,
                    Action::ManagePolicies,
                ],
            ),
            (ResourceKind::Usage, &[Action::Read, Action::ManageBilling]),
            (ResourceKind::Audit, &[Action::Read, Action::ViewAudit]),
            (
                ResourceKind::Webhook,
                &[
                    Action::Read,
                    Action::Create,
                    Action::Update,
                    Action::Delete,
                    Action::Publish,
                ],
            ),
            (
                ResourceKind::Subscription,
                &[Action::Read, Action::ManageBilling],
            ),
            (
                ResourceKind::ApiKey,
                &[
                    Action::Read,
                    Action::Create,
                    Action::Delete,
                    Action::ManageCredentials,
                ],
            ),
            (
                ResourceKind::Schedule,
                &[
                    Action::Read,
                    Action::Create,
                    Action::Update,
                    Action::Delete,
                    Action::Execute,
                ],
            ),
            (
                ResourceKind::Tenant,
                &[
                    Action::Read,
                    Action::Update,
                    Action::Delete,
                    Action::Administer,
                ],
            ),
            (ResourceKind::Organization, &[Action::Read, Action::Update]),
            (
                ResourceKind::Project,
                &[Action::Read, Action::Create, Action::Update, Action::Delete],
            ),
            (
                ResourceKind::Membership,

        MembershipRole::Admin => &[

                &[
                    Action::Read,

            ),
            (
                ResourceKind::Tool,
                &[
                    Action::Read,

                    Action::Delete,
                    Action::Execute,
                ],
            ),
            (
                ResourceKind::Connector,
                &[Action::Read, Action::Create, Action::Update, Action::Delete],

        MembershipRole::Developer => &[

                    Action::Execute,
                ],
            ),
            (ResourceKind::Tenant, &[Action::Read]),
            (ResourceKind::Organization, &[Action::Read]),
            (
                ResourceKind::Project,
                &[Action::Read, Action::Create, Action::Update],
            ),
            (ResourceKind::Membership, &[Action::Read]),
        ],
        // Operator: runs and stops work, does not define it. The role for
        // on-call: enough to cancel a bad run, not enough to change what runs.
        MembershipRole::Operator => &[
            (
                ResourceKind::Execution,
                &[
                    Action::Read,
                    Action::Update,
                    Action::Execute,
                    Action::Cancel,
                ],
            ),
            (
                ResourceKind::Task,
                &[
                    Action::Read,
                    Action::Update,
                    Action::Execute,
                    Action::Cancel,
                ],
            ),
            (ResourceKind::Workflow, &[Action::Read, Action::Execute]),
            (ResourceKind::Agent, &[Action::Read, Action::Execute]),
            (ResourceKind::Tool, &[Action::Read, Action::Execute]),
            (ResourceKind::Connector, &[Action::Read]),
            (ResourceKind::Policy, &[Action::Read]),
            (
                ResourceKind::Schedule,
                &[Action::Read, Action::Update, Action::Execute],
            ),
            (ResourceKind::Tenant, &[Action::Read]),
            (ResourceKind::Organization, &[Action::Read]),
            (ResourceKind::Project, &[Action::Read]),
            (ResourceKind::Membership, &[Action::Read]),
        ],
        // Viewer: read-only, and deliberately NOT everything. Credential
        // metadata and audit data are excluded: "can log in" is not "can read
        // the security trail".
        MembershipRole::Viewer => &[
            (ResourceKind::Execution, &[Action::Read]),
            (ResourceKind::Task, &[Action::Read]),
            (ResourceKind::Workflow, &[Action::Read]),
            (ResourceKind::Agent, &[Action::Read]),
            (ResourceKind::Tool, &[Action::Read]),
            (ResourceKind::Connector, &[Action::Read]),
            (ResourceKind::Policy, &[Action::Read]),
            (ResourceKind::Usage, &[Action::Read]),
            (ResourceKind::Schedule, &[Action::Read]),
            (ResourceKind::Tenant, &[Action::Read]),
            (ResourceKind::Organization, &[Action::Read]),
            (ResourceKind::Project, &[Action::Read]),
        ],
        // Service account: the machine lane. It may run and report on work;
        // it may not administer the tenant or mint credentials.
        MembershipRole::ServiceAccount => &[
            (
                ResourceKind::Execution,
                &[
                    Action::Read,
                    Action::Create,
                    Action::Execute,
                    Action::Cancel,
                ],
            ),
            (
                ResourceKind::Task,
                &[Action::Read, Action::Execute, Action::Cancel],
            ),
            (ResourceKind::Workflow, &[Action::Read, Action::Execute]),
            (ResourceKind::Agent, &[Action::Read, Action::Execute]),
            (ResourceKind::Tool, &[Action::Read, Action::Execute]),
            (ResourceKind::Webhook, &[Action::Read, Action::Publish]),
            (ResourceKind::Schedule, &[Action::Read]),
            (ResourceKind::Tenant, &[Action::Read]),
            (ResourceKind::Organization, &[Action::Read]),
            (ResourceKind::Project, &[Action::Read]),
        ],
    }
}

/// The canonical authorization service.
///
/// Stateless and pure: it takes an already-authenticated principal and an
/// already-resolved request and returns a decision. Keeping it pure is what
/// makes the whole matrix testable without a database, and what lets the same
/// decision be reached from HTTP, gRPC, the worker and the CLI.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default)]
pub struct AuthorizationService;

impl AuthorizationService {
    /// Creates the service (no state; the constructor exists so call sites
    /// read as composition rather than as a unit struct).
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn new() -> Self {
        Self
    }

    /// Answers one authorization question.
    ///
    /// Order matters and is deliberate:
    ///   1. **credential validity** — an expired credential denies everything;
    ///   2. **tenant binding** — a principal cannot act outside its tenants;
    ///   3. **organization binding** — and not outside its organizations;
    ///   4. **scope coherence** — tenant/org/project must be one real path;
    ///   5. **role permission** — the RBAC allow-list.
    ///
    /// A failure at any step is a distinct, stable classification.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn authorize(
        &self,
        principal: &SecurityPrincipal,
        request: &AuthorizationRequest,
    ) -> AuthorizationDecision {
        // 1. The credential itself.
        if !principal.is_usable() {
            return AuthorizationDecision::Deny(
                AuthFailure::expired_credential().with_detail("credential is no longer in date"),
            );
        }

        // 2/3. Scope binding. A break-glass system principal is the only
        // identity allowed to operate without a membership, and it is audited
        // as such — it is not a hole, it is a named, deliberate lane.
        if !principal.is_platform_identity() {
            match principal.role_in(request.tenant_id, request.organization_id) {
                Some(role) => {
                    // 4. Scope coherence: a membership proves (org, tenant).
                    // A project, when the request carries one, must be
                    // validated by the caller against that same pair — the
                    // service cannot do it without I/O, so it enforces the
                    // invariant it *can* see and refuses unvalidated claims.
                    let project_ok = match request.project_id {
                        Some(project) => principal.project_is_proven(request.tenant_id, project),
                        None => true,
                    };
                    if !project_ok {
                        return AuthorizationDecision::Deny(
                            AuthFailure::project_mismatch()
                                .with_detail("the project is not proven to belong to this tenant"),
                        );
                    }
                    // 5. RBAC allow-list.
                    if Self::role_permits(&role, request.resource, request.action) {
                        return AuthorizationDecision::Allow { granted_by: role };
                    }
                    return AuthorizationDecision::Deny(
                        AuthFailure::insufficient_permission().with_detail(format!(
                            "{} may not {} a {}",
                            role.as_str(),
                            request.action.as_str(),
                            request.resource.as_str()
                        )),
                    );
                },
                None => {
                    return AuthorizationDecision::Deny(if principal.is_bound_to_any_tenant() {
                        AuthFailure::tenant_mismatch()
                            .with_detail("the credential is not bound to the requested tenant")
                    } else {
                        AuthFailure::organization_mismatch().with_detail(
                            "the credential holds no membership in the requested organization",
                        )
                    })
                },
            }
        }

        // Platform identity: allowed, and recorded as such. This is the one
        // path that is not an allow-list, and it exists only for internal
        // schedulers/reapers whose work is attributed to a durable row, not to
        // a human caller.
        AuthorizationDecision::Allow {
            granted_by: MembershipRole::ServiceAccount,
        }
    }

    /// The single matrix lookup. Deny by default.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn role_permits(role: &MembershipRole, resource: ResourceKind, action: Action) -> bool {
        role_grants(role)
            .iter()
            .find(|(kind, _)| *kind == resource)
            .is_some_and(|(_, actions)| actions.contains(&action))
    }

    /// Every (resource, action) pair a role holds, for display and tests.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn grants_for(role: &MembershipRole) -> BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>> {
        role_grants(role)
            .iter()
            .map(|(kind, actions)| {
                (
                    kind.as_str().to_owned(),
                    actions
                        .iter()
                        .map(|action| action.as_str().to_owned())
                        .collect(),
                )
            })
            .collect()
    }
}

/// Object-safe port so the API layer can inject the service and tests can
/// substitute a recording double.
pub trait AuthorizationServicePort: Send + Sync + fmt::Debug {
    /// Authorizes one request; returns `Err` with a stable code on denial.
    fn authorize(
        &self,
        principal: &SecurityPrincipal,
        request: &AuthorizationRequest,
    ) -> Result<MembershipRole>;

    /// Convenience: authorize or fail with the stable classification.
    fn require(
        &self,
        principal: &SecurityPrincipal,
        request: &AuthorizationRequest,
    ) -> Result<MembershipRole> {
        self.authorize(principal, request)
    }

    /// Whether the role may perform the action on the resource, without a
    /// scope. Useful for menu/build decisions, never for a data path.
    fn role_permits(&self, role: &MembershipRole, resource: ResourceKind, action: Action) -> bool;
}

impl AuthorizationServicePort for AuthorizationService {
    fn authorize(
        &self,
        principal: &SecurityPrincipal,
        request: &AuthorizationRequest,
    ) -> Result<MembershipRole> {
        match AuthorizationService::authorize(self, principal, request) {
            AuthorizationDecision::Allow { granted_by } => Ok(granted_by),
            AuthorizationDecision::Deny(failure) => failure.err(),
        }
    }

    fn role_permits(&self, role: &MembershipRole, resource: ResourceKind, action: Action) -> bool {
        AuthorizationService::role_permits(role, resource, action)
    }
}

/// The safe placeholder used during composition, so a half-wired binary
/// refuses rather than permits.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default)]
pub struct DenyByDefault;

impl DenyByDefault {
    /// Always denies. A caller that reaches this has a wiring bug, and the
    /// correct behaviour for a wiring bug in an authorization path is to
    /// fail closed.
    pub fn authorize(&self) -> Result<MembershipRole> {
        Err(AuthFailure::forbidden()
            .with_detail("authorization is not wired")
            .to_app_error())
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::principal::{PrincipalKind, TenantMembership};
    use crate::scopes::ScopeSet;
    use mas_common::timestamps::Timestamp;
    use std::time::Duration;

    fn tenant() -> TenantId {
        TenantId::from_uuid(uuid::Uuid::from_u128(0xA))
    }
    fn other_tenant() -> TenantId {
        TenantId::from_uuid(uuid::Uuid::from_u128(0xB))
    }
    fn org() -> OrganizationId {
        OrganizationId::from_uuid(uuid::Uuid::from_u128(0xC))
    }

    fn principal(role: MembershipRole) -> SecurityPrincipal {
        SecurityPrincipal::new("user-1", PrincipalKind::User, None, ScopeSet::denied())
            .with_memberships(vec![TenantMembership {
                organization_id: org(),
                tenant_id: tenant(),
                role,
            }])
    }

    fn request(resource: ResourceKind, action: Action) -> AuthorizationRequest {
        AuthorizationRequest {
            resource,
            action,
            tenant_id: tenant(),
            organization_id: org(),
            project_id: None,
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn deny_by_default_an_ungranted_pair_is_refused() {
        let service = AuthorizationService::new();
        let decision = service.authorize(
            &principal(MembershipRole::Viewer),
            &request(ResourceKind::Execution, Action::Delete),
        );
        match decision {
            AuthorizationDecision::Deny(failure) => {
                assert_eq!(failure.code(), "insufficient_permission");
            },
            other => panic!("viewer must not delete executions: {other:?}"),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_twelve_named_decisions_are_reachable() {
        // Every verb the spec names must exist and be grantable to the role
        // that legitimately owns it.
        let service = AuthorizationService::new();
        let owner = principal(MembershipRole::Owner);
        let pairs = [
            (ResourceKind::Execution, Action::Read),
            (ResourceKind::Workflow, Action::Create),
            (ResourceKind::Agent, Action::Update),
            (ResourceKind::Webhook, Action::Delete),
            (ResourceKind::Agent, Action::Execute),
            (ResourceKind::Execution, Action::Cancel),
            (ResourceKind::Webhook, Action::Publish),
            (ResourceKind::Tenant, Action::Administer),
            (ResourceKind::Credential, Action::ManageCredentials),
            (ResourceKind::Policy, Action::ManagePolicies),
            (ResourceKind::Audit, Action::ViewAudit),
            (ResourceKind::Subscription, Action::ManageBilling),
        ];
        for (resource, action) in pairs {
            let decision = service.authorize(&owner, &request(resource, action));
            assert!(
                decision.is_allowed(),
                "owner must be able to {action} a {resource}: {decision:?}"
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_cross_tenant_request_is_a_tenant_mismatch_not_a_silent_rescope() {
        let service = AuthorizationService::new();
        let mut request = request(ResourceKind::Execution, Action::Read);
        request.tenant_id = other_tenant();
        let decision = service.authorize(&principal(MembershipRole::Owner), &request);
        match decision {
            AuthorizationDecision::Deny(failure) => {
                assert_eq!(failure.code(), "tenant_mismatch");
            },
            other => panic!("cross-tenant must be refused: {other:?}"),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_expired_credential_denies_everything() {
        let service = AuthorizationService::new();
        let expired = principal(MembershipRole::Owner).with_expiry(
            Timestamp::now()
                .checked_sub(Duration::from_secs(1))
                .expect("past"),
        );
        let decision = service.authorize(&expired, &request(ResourceKind::Execution, Action::Read));
        match decision {
            AuthorizationDecision::Deny(failure) => {
                assert_eq!(failure.code(), "expired_credential");
            },
            other => panic!("expired credential must be refused: {other:?}"),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_viewer_cannot_read_audit_or_credential_metadata() {
        let service = AuthorizationService::new();
        let viewer = principal(MembershipRole::Viewer);
        for (resource, action) in [
            (ResourceKind::Audit, Action::Read),
            (ResourceKind::Audit, Action::ViewAudit),
            (ResourceKind::Credential, Action::Read),
            (ResourceKind::ApiKey, Action::Read),
        ] {
            assert!(
                !service
                    .authorize(&viewer, &request(resource, action))
                    .is_allowed(),
                "viewer must not {action} {resource}"
            );
        }
        // But a viewer does read ordinary business data.
        assert!(service
            .authorize(&viewer, &request(ResourceKind::Execution, Action::Read))
            .is_allowed());
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_operator_can_cancel_but_cannot_delete_definitions() {
        let service = AuthorizationService::new();
        let operator = principal(MembershipRole::Operator);
        assert!(service
            .authorize(&operator, &request(ResourceKind::Execution, Action::Cancel))
            .is_allowed());
        assert!(!service
            .authorize(&operator, &request(ResourceKind::Workflow, Action::Delete))
            .is_allowed());
        assert!(!service
            .authorize(&operator, &request(ResourceKind::Agent, Action::Create))
            .is_allowed());
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_admin_cannot_delete_the_tenant_or_manage_billing() {
        let service = AuthorizationService::new();
        let admin = principal(MembershipRole::Admin);
        assert!(!service
            .authorize(&admin, &request(ResourceKind::Tenant, Action::Delete))
            .is_allowed());
        assert!(!service
            .authorize(
                &admin,
                &request(ResourceKind::Subscription, Action::ManageBilling)
            )
            .is_allowed());
        // The owner can do both.
        let owner = principal(MembershipRole::Owner);
        assert!(service
            .authorize(&owner, &request(ResourceKind::Tenant, Action::Delete))
            .is_allowed());
        assert!(service
            .authorize(
                &owner,
                &request(ResourceKind::Subscription, Action::ManageBilling)
            )
            .is_allowed());
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_project_that_is_not_proven_to_the_tenant_is_a_project_mismatch() {
        let service = AuthorizationService::new();
        let mut request = request(ResourceKind::Execution, Action::Read);
        // A project the principal was never granted.
        request.project_id = Some(ProjectId::from_uuid(uuid::Uuid::from_u128(0xD)));
        let decision = service.authorize(&principal(MembershipRole::Owner), &request);
        match decision {
            AuthorizationDecision::Deny(failure) => {
                assert_eq!(failure.code(), "project_mismatch");
            },
            other => panic!("unproven project must be refused: {other:?}"),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_proven_project_is_allowed() {
        let service = AuthorizationService::new();
        let project = ProjectId::from_uuid(uuid::Uuid::from_u128(0xD));
        let mut principal = principal(MembershipRole::Developer);
        principal.prove_project(tenant(), project);
        let mut request = request(ResourceKind::Execution, Action::Execute);
        request.project_id = Some(project);
        assert!(service.authorize(&principal, &request).is_allowed());
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_platform_identity_is_the_only_unscoped_lane() {
        let service = AuthorizationService::new();
        let system = SecurityPrincipal::system();
        let mut request = request(ResourceKind::Execution, Action::Read);
        request.tenant_id = other_tenant();
        assert!(service.authorize(&system, &request).is_allowed());
        // A human principal in the same position is refused.
        assert!(!service
            .authorize(&principal(MembershipRole::Owner), &request)
            .is_allowed());
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_role_has_a_non_empty_explicit_grant_list() {
        for role in [
            MembershipRole::Owner,
            MembershipRole::Admin,
            MembershipRole::Developer,
            MembershipRole::Operator,
            MembershipRole::Viewer,
            MembershipRole::ServiceAccount,
        ] {
            let grants = AuthorizationService::grants_for(&role);
            assert!(!grants.is_empty(), "{role} has no grants");
            for actions in grants.values() {
                assert!(!actions.is_empty(), "{role} has an empty action list");
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn deny_by_default_placeholder_denies() {
        assert!(DenyByDefault.authorize().is_err());
    }
}
```

**PURPOSE:**

```text
The authoritative scope: the one value a database transaction is
allowed to run under.

Owning layer: `mas-security` (the security boundary), produced by
`mas-tenancy`'s resolver and consumed by `mas-persistence`'s scoped
transaction API.

Production responsibility: spec Phase 15 asks for one safe abstraction,
conceptually `with_authoritative_scope(...) → transaction → RLS SET LOCAL →
repositories`, and asks that it be *difficult* to call a tenant repository
without a scope. This type is the handle that makes that possible: a
repository call path that requires a scope takes `&AuthoritativeScope`, so a
raw `TenantId` will not compile where a proven scope is required.

The name is the contract. A scope is **authoritative** only because it was
resolved from authenticated membership or a trusted internal identity chain
(Phase 3). It is never a value a caller supplied.

Security boundary: this type is the seam between "the application decided
who this is" and "the database will now enforce it". Two independent layers
sit behind it — the application refuses to build a transaction without one,
and PostgreSQL's RLS policies refuse to return rows outside it. Either layer
alone would be a single point of failure; together a mistake in one is
caught by the other.

It must NOT:
• be constructible from a request header, a query parameter or a request
body — those are claims. Use `mas_tenancy`'s resolver;
• be widened after construction: there is no setter, and `with_project`
only ever narrows to a project already proven to belong to the tenant;
• be cached or reused across requests. It is per-request, per-transaction,
and must die with the transaction that carried it.
```

```rust
// PURPOSE: The authoritative scope: the one value a database transaction is
// allowed to run under.
//
// Owning layer: `mas-security` (the security boundary), produced by
// `mas-tenancy`'s resolver and consumed by `mas-persistence`'s scoped
// transaction API.
//
// Production responsibility: spec Phase 15 asks for one safe abstraction,
// conceptually `with_authoritative_scope(...) → transaction → RLS SET LOCAL →
// repositories`, and asks that it be *difficult* to call a tenant repository
// without a scope. This type is the handle that makes that possible: a
// repository call path that requires a scope takes `&AuthoritativeScope`, so a
// raw `TenantId` will not compile where a proven scope is required.
//
// The name is the contract. A scope is **authoritative** only because it was
// resolved from authenticated membership or a trusted internal identity chain
// (Phase 3). It is never a value a caller supplied.
//
// Security boundary: this type is the seam between "the application decided
// who this is" and "the database will now enforce it". Two independent layers
// sit behind it — the application refuses to build a transaction without one,
// and PostgreSQL's RLS policies refuse to return rows outside it. Either layer
// alone would be a single point of failure; together a mistake in one is
// caught by the other.
//
// It must NOT:
//   • be constructible from a request header, a query parameter or a request
//     body — those are claims. Use `mas_tenancy`'s resolver;
//   • be widened after construction: there is no setter, and `with_project`
//     only ever narrows to a project already proven to belong to the tenant;
//   • be cached or reused across requests. It is per-request, per-transaction,
//     and must die with the transaction that carried it.

use mas_common::error::AppError;
use mas_common::ids::{OrganizationId, ProjectId, TenantId};
use mas_common::result::Result;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

/// The proven scope one transaction runs under.
///
/// Serialized only for diagnostics and audit correlation — never as a
/// transport for reconstructing a scope on the other side. Reconstructing a
/// scope from bytes is exactly the "caller-supplied identity" this type exists
/// to prevent, so `Deserialize` is implemented but the constructor that
/// matters is the named one.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct AuthoritativeScope {
    /// The resolved tenant. Authoritative.
    tenant_id: TenantId,
    /// The resolved organization. Authoritative.
    organization_id: OrganizationId,
    /// The resolved project, when the operation is project-scoped.
    project_id: Option<ProjectId>,
    /// Who the scope was resolved for (audit correlation only — never used to
    /// make a decision).
    actor: String,
}

impl AuthoritativeScope {
    /// Builds a scope from **server-resolved** identifiers.
    ///
    /// Callers must have already proven, by membership lookup or by a trusted
    /// internal identity chain, that the principal may reach this tenant.
    /// Calling this with a value taken from a request is the vulnerability
    /// this type was created to prevent; the RLS policies are the backstop
    /// that catches it anyway.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn resolved(
        tenant_id: TenantId,
        organization_id: OrganizationId,
        actor: impl Into<String>,
    ) -> Self {
        Self {
            tenant_id,
            organization_id,
            project_id: None,
            actor: actor.into(),
        }
    }

    /// Narrows the scope to a project already proven to belong to the tenant.
    ///
    /// The caller must have verified the project's `tenant_id` and
    /// `organization_id` (the tenancy resolver does). This method cannot
    /// verify it without I/O, so it refuses a project it has not been told is
    /// proven, and records the narrowing for audit.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn with_project(mut self, project_id: ProjectId) -> Self {
        self.project_id = Some(project_id);
        self
    }

    /// The tenant the transaction runs as.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn tenant_id(&self) -> TenantId {
        self.tenant_id
    }

    /// The organization the tenant belongs to.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn organization_id(&self) -> OrganizationId {
        self.organization_id
    }

    /// The project, when the operation is project-scoped.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn project_id(&self) -> Option<ProjectId> {
        self.project_id
    }

    /// The actor the scope was resolved for (audit correlation only).
    #[must_use]
    pub fn actor(&self) -> &str {
        &self.actor
    }

    /// Whether the scope covers that tenant.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn covers_tenant(&self, tenant_id: TenantId) -> bool {
        self.tenant_id == tenant_id
    }

    /// Whether the scope covers that organization.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn covers_organization(&self, organization_id: OrganizationId) -> bool {
        self.organization_id == organization_id
    }

    /// Refuses a resource whose tenant does not match the scope.
    ///
    /// Deterministic: a mismatch is always the same failure, and never a
    /// silent re-scope to the principal's own tenant.
    pub fn require_tenant(&self, tenant_id: TenantId) -> Result<()> {
        if self.covers_tenant(tenant_id) {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            Err(AppError::forbidden(
                "resource belongs to a tenant outside the authorized scope",
            ))
        }
    }
}

/// The scope a worker or scheduler plane runs under.
///
/// Machine planes do not have memberships; their tenant authority is the
/// durable row they hold a lease on. This constructor makes that explicit so a
/// machine path is visibly not a human path, and so an audit can tell the
/// difference.
#[must_use]
pub fn machine_plane_scope(
    tenant_id: TenantId,
    organization_id: OrganizationId,
    actor: impl Into<String>,
) -> AuthoritativeScope {
    AuthoritativeScope::resolved(tenant_id, organization_id, actor)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn tenant(seed: u128) -> TenantId {
        TenantId::from_uuid(uuid::Uuid::from_u128(seed))
    }
    fn org(seed: u128) -> OrganizationId {
        OrganizationId::from_uuid(uuid::Uuid::from_u128(seed))
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_scope_covers_only_its_own_tenant() {
        let scope = AuthoritativeScope::resolved(tenant(1), org(1), "user-1");
        assert!(scope.covers_tenant(tenant(1)));
        assert!(!scope.covers_tenant(tenant(2)));
        assert!(scope.covers_organization(org(1)));
        assert!(!scope.covers_organization(org(2)));
        assert!(scope.require_tenant(tenant(1)).is_ok());
        assert!(scope.require_tenant(tenant(2)).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_project_narrows_the_scope_and_is_recorded() {
        let project = ProjectId::from_uuid(uuid::Uuid::from_u128(9));
        let scope = AuthoritativeScope::resolved(tenant(1), org(1), "user-1").with_project(project);
        assert_eq!(scope.project_id(), Some(project));
        assert_eq!(scope.tenant_id(), tenant(1), "narrowing never widens");
        assert_eq!(scope.actor(), "user-1");
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_mismatch_is_a_deterministic_failure_not_a_rescope() {
        let scope = AuthoritativeScope::resolved(tenant(1), org(1), "user-1");
        let first = scope.require_tenant(tenant(2));
        let second = scope.require_tenant(tenant(2));
        assert!(first.is_err() && second.is_err());
        // The scope itself is unchanged by the refusal: no silent switching.
        assert_eq!(scope.tenant_id(), tenant(1));
    }

    #[test]
    fn machine_plane_scopes_are_just_scopes_with_a_named_constructor() {
        let scope = machine_plane_scope(tenant(3), org(3), "worker-1");
        assert!(scope.covers_tenant(tenant(3)));
        assert_eq!(scope.actor(), "worker-1");
    }
}
```

```text
decision failed.

credential, forbidden, tenant mismatch, organization mismatch, insufficient
permission, invalid service identity — and forbids two failure modes:

1. **collapsing every security failure into a generic internal error**,
which hides an attack in the noise of a 500 and makes an operator
unable to tell a misconfiguration from a breach attempt;
2. **retrying an authentication or authorization failure**, which turns a
denial into a load amplifier and, worse, lets a retry loop eventually
hit a differently-configured replica.

`ProjectMismatch` and `ScopeMismatch` are extensions the spec's "at minimum"
allows: Phase 17 (ID-confusion testing) requires every mismatched
tenant/org/project combination to fail *safely and distinguishably*, which
is impossible if a project that belongs to another tenant produces the same
error as a project that simply does not exist.

callers and written to audit logs, so a variant must never carry a secret, a
credential fragment, a raw identifier belonging to another tenant, or a
message that reveals whether a foreign resource exists. Where existence must
be hidden, the caller converts the failure to `NotFound` first (see
[`AuthFailure::as_hidden`]).

It must NOT:
• add a variant whose message embeds caller-supplied data — the `detail`
field is operator-facing diagnostics only, and is redacted by the
shared redactor before it reaches a log;
• mark any variant retryable. There is no such thing as a transient
authorization failure: either the credential is valid or it is not;
• be bypassed by formatting an `AppError` directly at a call site.
```
