## FILE: repo/enterprise-mas/rust-core/crates/persistence/src/directory.rs


**PURPOSE:**

```text
The PostgreSQL implementation of the tenancy directory ports.

Owning layer: `mas-persistence`.

Production responsibility: spec Phases 3 and 4. `mas_tenancy`'s
`mas_tenancy::TenantResolver` is correct and fail-closed, but until this module
existed its ports had only in-memory implementations — so the authoritative
resolver could not run in production at all, and every entrypoint instead
read `x-tenant-id` from the request. This module is what makes
"tenant comes from identity" true against a real database.

Security boundary: these reads are the *only* unscoped reads in the
system. They run on a dedicated pool whose role (`mas_directory`, created
by migration `0015`) holds `SELECT` on the four hierarchy catalog tables
and `BYPASSRLS` for no other purpose. That is a deliberate, minimal,
documented exception — see the migration header for why it cannot be
avoided and why widening `mas_app` instead would be worse.

It must NOT:
• be constructed from the runtime pool — the constructors take a
separately configured directory pool and the type name says so;
• read or write any table outside the four catalog tables;
• be used by a request-serving repository. It answers "what may this
principal reach", never "give me this tenant's executions";
• trust the ids it is handed. It looks facts up; whether a principal may
use them is `TenantResolver`'s decision, made from the returned rows.
```


**COMPLETE CONTENT** (442 lines):

```rust
//! PURPOSE: The PostgreSQL implementation of the tenancy directory ports.
//!
//! Owning layer: `mas-persistence`.
//!
//! Production responsibility: spec Phases 3 and 4. `mas_tenancy`'s
//! `mas_tenancy::TenantResolver` is correct and fail-closed, but until this module
//! existed its ports had only in-memory implementations — so the authoritative
//! resolver could not run in production at all, and every entrypoint instead
//! read `x-tenant-id` from the request. This module is what makes
//! "tenant comes from identity" true against a real database.
//!
//! Security boundary: these reads are the *only* unscoped reads in the
//! system. They run on a dedicated pool whose role (`mas_directory`, created
//! by migration `0015`) holds `SELECT` on the four hierarchy catalog tables
//! and `BYPASSRLS` for no other purpose. That is a deliberate, minimal,
//! documented exception — see the migration header for why it cannot be
//! avoided and why widening `mas_app` instead would be worse.
//!
//! It must NOT:
//!   • be constructed from the runtime pool — the constructors take a
//!     separately configured directory pool and the type name says so;
//!   • read or write any table outside the four catalog tables;
//!   • be used by a request-serving repository. It answers "what may this
//!     principal reach", never "give me this tenant's executions";
//!   • trust the ids it is handed. It looks facts up; whether a principal may
//!     use them is `TenantResolver`'s decision, made from the returned rows.

use mas_common::enums::TenantStatus;
use mas_common::error::AppError;
use mas_common::ids::{MembershipId, OrganizationId, ProjectId, TenantId, UserId};
use mas_common::result::Result;
use mas_common::timestamps::Timestamp;
use mas_domain::{Membership, Organization, Project, ProjectConfig, Slug, Tenant};
use mas_tenancy::{MembershipDirectoryPort, TenantDirectoryPort};
use sqlx::{PgPool, Row};

use crate::error::map_sqlx;

/// The four catalog tables this module is permitted to touch.
///
/// Kept as a named constant so a reviewer can see the entire surface at a
/// glance, and so a future change that needs a fifth table is a visible
/// decision rather than a one-line edit.
pub const DIRECTORY_TABLES: &[&str] = &["organizations", "tenants", "projects", "memberships"];

/// PostgreSQL tenancy directory.
///
/// Holds the directory pool, never the runtime pool.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct PgTenantDirectory {
    pool: PgPool,
}

impl PgTenantDirectory {
    /// Binds the directory to the pool configured from
    /// `MAS_DATABASE_DIRECTORY_URL`.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn new(directory_pool: PgPool) -> Self {
        Self {
            pool: directory_pool,
        }
    }
}

/// PostgreSQL membership directory.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct PgMembershipDirectory {
    pool: PgPool,
}

impl PgMembershipDirectory {
    /// Binds the directory to the pool configured from
    /// `MAS_DATABASE_DIRECTORY_URL`.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn new(directory_pool: PgPool) -> Self {
        Self {
            pool: directory_pool,
        }
    }
}

/// Errors from a required text column that the schema declares `NOT NULL`.
fn missing(column: &str) -> AppError {
    AppError::internal(format!("directory row missing {column}"))
}

/// Parses a status text column into its domain enum, failing closed: an
/// unrecognised status is treated as unusable rather than as the most
/// permissive one.
fn parse_tenant_status(raw: &str) -> Result<TenantStatus> {
    raw.trim()
        .parse::<TenantStatus>()
        .map_err(|_| AppError::internal(format!("unknown tenant status {raw}")))
}

/// Hydrates a slug, which the database already constrains but which the type
/// re-validates so an out-of-band edit cannot smuggle a bad value into a
/// domain object.
fn slug(row: &sqlx::postgres::PgRow, column: &str) -> Result<Slug> {
    let raw: String = row.try_get(column).map_err(map_sqlx)?;
    Slug::new(&raw)
}

/// Hydrates a `jsonb` object column into a `serde_json::Map`.
///
/// A non-object value can only come from an out-of-band edit; it is refused
/// rather than coerced, because a settings blob of the wrong shape silently
/// changes behaviour.
fn object(
    row: &sqlx::postgres::PgRow,
    column: &str,
) -> Result<serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>> {
    let value: serde_json::Value = row.try_get(column).map_err(map_sqlx)?;
    match value {
        serde_json::Value::Object(map) => Ok(map),
        other => Err(AppError::internal(format!(
            "column {column} must be a json object, found {other}"
        ))),
    }
}

/// Hydrates a typed `jsonb` column (`settings`, `config`).
fn typed<T: serde::de::DeserializeOwned>(row: &sqlx::postgres::PgRow, column: &str) -> Result<T> {
    let value: serde_json::Value = row
        .try_get(column)
        .map_err(map_sqlx)
        .unwrap_or(serde_json::Value::Object(Default::default()));
    serde_json::from_value(value)
        .map_err(|error| AppError::internal(format!("column {column} is malformed: {error}")))
}

fn parse_enum<T: std::str::FromStr>(raw: &str, what: &str) -> Result<T> {
    raw.trim()
        .parse::<T>()
        .map_err(|_| AppError::internal(format!("unknown {what} {raw}")))
}

fn ts(row: &sqlx::postgres::PgRow, column: &str) -> Result<Timestamp> {
    row.try_get::<chrono::DateTime<chrono::Utc>, _>(column)
        .map(Timestamp::from_datetime)
        .map_err(map_sqlx)
}

#[async_trait::async_trait]
impl TenantDirectoryPort for PgTenantDirectory {
    async fn get_tenant(&self, id: TenantId) -> Result<Option<Tenant>> {
        let row = sqlx::query(
            "SELECT id, organization_id, name, slug, status, environment, isolation_mode, settings, created_at, updated_at
               FROM tenants WHERE id = $1",
        )
        .bind(id.to_database_string())
        .fetch_optional(&self.pool)
        .await
        .map_err(map_sqlx)?;
        row.map(|row| {
            let id = TenantId::from_uuid(row.try_get::<uuid::Uuid, _>("id").map_err(map_sqlx)?);
            let organization_id = OrganizationId::from_uuid(
                row.try_get::<uuid::Uuid, _>("organization_id")
                    .map_err(map_sqlx)?,
            );
            let tenant = Tenant::reconstitute(
                id,
                organization_id,
                row.try_get::<String, _>("name").map_err(map_sqlx)?,
                slug(&row, "slug")?,
                parse_tenant_status(&row.try_get::<String, _>("status").map_err(map_sqlx)?)?,
                parse_enum(
                    &row.try_get::<String, _>("environment").map_err(map_sqlx)?,
                    "environment",
                )?,
                parse_enum(
                    &row.try_get::<String, _>("isolation_mode")
                        .map_err(map_sqlx)?,
                    "isolation mode",
                )?,
                object(&row, "settings")?,
                ts(&row, "created_at")?,
                ts(&row, "updated_at")?,
            );
            // The row is the authority on ownership, so this can only fire on
            // a schema/FK violation. Asserting it here means a directory read
            // can never hand back a tenant whose owner disagrees with itself.
            tenant.assert_belongs_to(organization_id)?;
            Ok(tenant)
        })
        .transpose()
    }

    async fn get_organization(&self, id: OrganizationId) -> Result<Option<Organization>> {
        let row = sqlx::query(
            "SELECT id, legal_name, display_name, slug, status, settings, created_at, updated_at
               FROM organizations WHERE id = $1",
        )
        .bind(id.to_database_string())
        .fetch_optional(&self.pool)
        .await
        .map_err(map_sqlx)?;
        row.map(|row| {
            Ok(Organization {
                id: OrganizationId::from_uuid(
                    row.try_get::<uuid::Uuid, _>("id").map_err(map_sqlx)?,
                ),
                legal_name: row.try_get::<String, _>("legal_name").map_err(map_sqlx)?,
                display_name: row.try_get::<String, _>("display_name").map_err(map_sqlx)?,
                slug: slug(&row, "slug")?,
                status: parse_enum(
                    &row.try_get::<String, _>("status").map_err(map_sqlx)?,
                    "organization status",
                )?,
                settings: object(&row, "settings")?,
                created_at: ts(&row, "created_at")?,
                updated_at: ts(&row, "updated_at")?,
            })
        })
        .transpose()
    }

    async fn get_project(&self, id: ProjectId) -> Result<Option<Project>> {
        let row = sqlx::query(
            "SELECT id, tenant_id, organization_id, name, slug, description, status, config, created_at, updated_at
               FROM projects WHERE id = $1",
        )
        .bind(id.to_database_string())
        .fetch_optional(&self.pool)
        .await
        .map_err(map_sqlx)?;
        row.map(|row| {
            Ok(Project {
                id: ProjectId::from_uuid(row.try_get::<uuid::Uuid, _>("id").map_err(map_sqlx)?),
                tenant_id: TenantId::from_uuid(
                    row.try_get::<uuid::Uuid, _>("tenant_id")
                        .map_err(map_sqlx)?,
                ),
                organization_id: OrganizationId::from_uuid(
                    row.try_get::<uuid::Uuid, _>("organization_id")
                        .map_err(map_sqlx)?,
                ),
                name: row.try_get::<String, _>("name").map_err(map_sqlx)?,
                slug: slug(&row, "slug")?,
                description: row
                    .try_get::<Option<String>, _>("description")
                    .map_err(map_sqlx)?,
                status: parse_enum(
                    &row.try_get::<String, _>("status").map_err(map_sqlx)?,
                    "project status",
                )?,
                config: typed::<ProjectConfig>(&row, "config")?,
                created_at: ts(&row, "created_at")?,
                updated_at: ts(&row, "updated_at")?,
            })
        })
        .transpose()
    }

    async fn list_tenants(&self, organization_id: OrganizationId) -> Result<Vec<Tenant>> {
        let rows = sqlx::query(
            "SELECT id, organization_id, name, slug, status, environment, isolation_mode, settings, created_at, updated_at
               FROM tenants WHERE organization_id = $1 ORDER BY id",
        )
        .bind(organization_id.to_database_string())
        .fetch_all(&self.pool)
        .await
        .map_err(map_sqlx)?;
        let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(rows.len());
        for row in rows {
            let id = TenantId::from_uuid(row.try_get::<uuid::Uuid, _>("id").map_err(map_sqlx)?);
            // Reuse the single-row path so there is exactly one hydration of
            // a tenant row in the codebase.
            if let Some(tenant) = self.get_tenant(id).await? {
                out.push(tenant);
            }
        }
        Ok(out)
    }

    async fn list_projects(&self, tenant_id: TenantId) -> Result<Vec<Project>> {
        let rows = sqlx::query(
            "SELECT id, tenant_id, organization_id, name, slug, description, status, config, created_at, updated_at
               FROM projects WHERE tenant_id = $1 ORDER BY id",
        )
        .bind(tenant_id.to_database_string())
        .fetch_all(&self.pool)
        .await
        .map_err(map_sqlx)?;
        let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(rows.len());
        for row in rows {
            let id = ProjectId::from_uuid(row.try_get::<uuid::Uuid, _>("id").map_err(map_sqlx)?);
            if let Some(project) = self.get_project(id).await? {
                out.push(project);
            }
        }
        Ok(out)
    }

    async fn upsert_organization(&self, _organization: &Organization) -> Result<()> {
        Err(directory_is_read_only("upsert_organization"))
    }

    async fn upsert_tenant(&self, _tenant: &Tenant) -> Result<()> {
        Err(directory_is_read_only("upsert_tenant"))
    }

    async fn upsert_project(&self, _project: &Project) -> Result<()> {
        Err(directory_is_read_only("upsert_project"))
    }
}

/// The directory role has no write grants, by design.
///
/// Refusing here rather than letting PostgreSQL refuse means the failure is
/// self-explanatory and happens before a connection is checked out.
fn directory_is_read_only(operation: &str) -> AppError {
    AppError::internal(format!(
        "the tenancy directory is read-only; {operation} is a privileged \
         operation that must run through the tenancy service on the runtime pool"
    ))
}

fn hydrate_membership(row: &sqlx::postgres::PgRow) -> Result<Membership> {
    let roles: serde_json::Value = row.try_get("roles").map_err(map_sqlx)?;
    let roles = roles
        .as_array()
        .ok_or_else(|| missing("roles"))?
        .iter()
        .map(|value| parse_enum(value.as_str().unwrap_or_default(), "membership role"))
        .collect::<Result<std::collections::BTreeSet<_>>>()?;
    let status: String = row.try_get("status").map_err(map_sqlx)?;
    Ok(Membership {
        id: MembershipId::from_uuid(row.try_get::<uuid::Uuid, _>("id").map_err(map_sqlx)?),
        user_id: UserId::from_uuid(row.try_get::<uuid::Uuid, _>("user_id").map_err(map_sqlx)?),
        organization_id: OrganizationId::from_uuid(
            row.try_get::<uuid::Uuid, _>("organization_id")
                .map_err(map_sqlx)?,
        ),
        tenant_id: row
            .try_get::<Option<uuid::Uuid>, _>("tenant_id")
            .map_err(map_sqlx)?
            .map(TenantId::from_uuid),
        roles,
        status: parse_enum(&status, "membership status")?,
        invited_at: ts(row, "invited_at")?,
        joined_at: row
            .try_get::<Option<chrono::DateTime<chrono::Utc>>, _>("joined_at")
            .map_err(map_sqlx)?
            .map(Timestamp::from_datetime),
        created_at: ts(row, "created_at")?,
        updated_at: ts(row, "updated_at")?,
    })
}

#[async_trait::async_trait]
impl MembershipDirectoryPort for PgMembershipDirectory {
    async fn memberships_for_user(&self, user_id: UserId) -> Result<Vec<Membership>> {
        // Deliberately includes every status: the resolver decides what an
        // `invited` or `suspended` membership may do. Filtering here would
        // put authorization policy in a query.
        let rows = sqlx::query(
            "SELECT id, user_id, organization_id, tenant_id, roles, status, invited_at, joined_at, created_at, updated_at
               FROM memberships WHERE user_id = $1 ORDER BY id",
        )
        .bind(user_id.to_database_string())
        .fetch_all(&self.pool)
        .await
        .map_err(map_sqlx)?;
        rows.iter().map(hydrate_membership).collect()
    }

    async fn memberships_in_organization(
        &self,
        organization_id: OrganizationId,
    ) -> Result<Vec<Membership>> {
        let rows = sqlx::query(
            "SELECT id, user_id, organization_id, tenant_id, roles, status, invited_at, joined_at, created_at, updated_at
               FROM memberships WHERE organization_id = $1 ORDER BY id",
        )
        .bind(organization_id.to_database_string())
        .fetch_all(&self.pool)
        .await
        .map_err(map_sqlx)?;
        rows.iter().map(hydrate_membership).collect()
    }

    async fn upsert(&self, _membership: &Membership) -> Result<()> {
        Err(directory_is_read_only("upsert membership"))
    }

    async fn get(&self, id: MembershipId) -> Result<Option<Membership>> {
        let row = sqlx::query(
            "SELECT id, user_id, organization_id, tenant_id, roles, status, invited_at, joined_at, created_at, updated_at
               FROM memberships WHERE id = $1",
        )
        .bind(id.to_database_string())
        .fetch_optional(&self.pool)
        .await
        .map_err(map_sqlx)?;
        row.as_ref().map(hydrate_membership).transpose()
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// The grant surface must stay exactly the four catalog tables. This is
    /// the assertion a reviewer of a future change will trip over.
    #[test]
    fn the_directory_surface_is_four_catalog_tables() {
        assert_eq!(
            DIRECTORY_TABLES,
            ["organizations", "tenants", "projects", "memberships"]
        );
        for table in DIRECTORY_TABLES {
            assert!(
                !matches!(
                    *table,
                    "executions" | "tasks" | "agents" | "credentials" | "usage" | "audit_events"
                ),
                "{table} is tenant data and must never be in the directory surface"
            );
        }
    }

    /// A status the platform does not recognise must fail closed rather than
    /// resolve to the most permissive status.
    #[test]
    fn unknown_statuses_fail_closed() {
        assert!(parse_tenant_status("active").is_ok());
        assert!(parse_tenant_status("suspended").is_ok());
        assert!(
            parse_tenant_status("totally-made-up").is_err(),
            "an unrecognised status must never read as active"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn writes_are_refused_before_reaching_the_database() {
        // Constructing a pool is not possible without a server; the refusal
        // is a pure function, so it is asserted directly.
        let error = directory_is_read_only("upsert_tenant");
        assert!(error.to_string().contains("read-only"));
    }
}
```

## FILE: repo/enterprise-mas/rust-core/crates/api/src/scope_resolution.rs


**PURPOSE:**

```text
Turn an authenticated principal plus the scope a request *claims*
into the one scope the request is actually entitled to.

Owning layer: `mas-api` (the process edge), delegating the authoritative
decision to `mas-tenancy`'s `TenantResolver`.

Production responsibility: spec Phase 3. Before this module existed the API
took `x-tenant-id` and `x-organization-id` at face value (`context.rs`,
`middleware.rs`, `grpc.rs`), which meant any authenticated caller could name
any tenant. Here those headers are demoted to what they are — hints about
which of the caller's *own* reachable tenants it means — and the answer is
recomputed from identity and the membership directory.

Security boundary: this is the boundary at which a caller-supplied value
stops being a claim and either becomes a proven scope or becomes a failure.
Two rules govern every path through it:

1. A tenant the principal cannot reach does not produce "forbidden". It
produces the same "not found" as a tenant that does not exist, because
"forbidden" would confirm the tenant is there (Phase 4, existence
hiding).
2. A conflict is a deterministic failure, never a silent correction. If a
caller names tenant A and organization B and those do not belong
together, the request fails; the server does not quietly substitute
tenant A's real organization and carry on.

It must NOT:
• fall back to the claimed tenant when resolution fails;
• treat an absent header as "any tenant";
• produce a scope for a principal whose credential has expired;
• be bypassable by calling a handler that skips the middleware — the
scope is the only thing `RequestContext::require_scope` will hand out.
```

```rust
// PURPOSE: Turn an authenticated principal plus the scope a request *claims*
// into the one scope the request is actually entitled to.
//
// Owning layer: `mas-api` (the process edge), delegating the authoritative
// decision to `mas-tenancy`'s `TenantResolver`.
//
// Production responsibility: spec Phase 3. Before this module existed the API
// took `x-tenant-id` and `x-organization-id` at face value (`context.rs`,
// `middleware.rs`, `grpc.rs`), which meant any authenticated caller could name
// any tenant. Here those headers are demoted to what they are — hints about
// which of the caller's *own* reachable tenants it means — and the answer is
// recomputed from identity and the membership directory.
//
// Security boundary: this is the boundary at which a caller-supplied value
// stops being a claim and either becomes a proven scope or becomes a failure.
// Two rules govern every path through it:
//
//   1. A tenant the principal cannot reach does not produce "forbidden". It
//      produces the same "not found" as a tenant that does not exist, because
//      "forbidden" would confirm the tenant is there (Phase 4, existence
//      hiding).
//   2. A conflict is a deterministic failure, never a silent correction. If a
//      caller names tenant A and organization B and those do not belong
//      together, the request fails; the server does not quietly substitute
//      tenant A's real organization and carry on.
//
// It must NOT:
//   • fall back to the claimed tenant when resolution fails;
//   • treat an absent header as "any tenant";
//   • produce a scope for a principal whose credential has expired;
//   • be bypassable by calling a handler that skips the middleware — the
//     scope is the only thing `RequestContext::require_scope` will hand out.

use mas_common::ids::{OrganizationId, ProjectId, TenantId};
use mas_common::result::Result;
use mas_security::{AuthFailure, AuthoritativeScope, SecurityPrincipal};
use mas_tenancy::TenantResolver;
use std::collections::BTreeSet;
use std::fmt;

/// What the request *asked* for. Hints, never authority.
///
/// Named `ScopeClaims` rather than `Scope` so every call site reads as "a
/// claim" — the type name is the first line of defence against a future
/// reader mistaking it for a decision.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ScopeClaims {
    /// `x-tenant-id`, if sent.
    pub tenant: Option<TenantId>,
    /// `x-organization-id`, if sent.
    pub organization: Option<OrganizationId>,
    /// `x-project-id` (or the project path segment), if sent.
    pub project: Option<ProjectId>,
}

/// The outcome: a scope, and the principal as the directory proved it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ResolvedRequest {
    /// The principal, carrying the role the directory proved for this scope.
    pub principal: SecurityPrincipal,
    /// The scope every repository call in this request must run under.
    pub scope: AuthoritativeScope,
}

/// Resolves request scope from identity.
///
/// Holds the tenancy resolver, and therefore the directory ports. There is no
/// constructor that works without one, so a half-wired process cannot resolve
/// scope at all.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct RequestScopeResolver {
    resolver: TenantResolver,
}

impl fmt::Debug for RequestScopeResolver {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("RequestScopeResolver")
            .finish_non_exhaustive()
    }
}

impl RequestScopeResolver {
    /// Binds the resolver to a directory.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn new(resolver: TenantResolver) -> Self {
        Self { resolver }
    }

    /// Resolves the scope for one request.
    ///
    /// Order matters and is deny-by-default:
    ///   1. the credential must be temporally usable;
    ///   2. the target tenant is chosen — from the claim if the principal can
    ///      reach it, otherwise unambiguously from the principal's binding;
    ///   3. the tenancy resolver re-proves tenant, organization and project
    ///      against the directory;
    ///   4. a claimed organization that disagrees with the tenant's real one
    ///      is a hard, deterministic mismatch.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// * `UNAUTHORIZED` — expired or unusable credential;
    /// * `VALIDATION_FAILED` — no tenant claim and no unambiguous binding;
    /// * `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` — the tenant/project is unreachable, which is
    ///   indistinguishable from absent by design;
    /// * `FORBIDDEN` — the tenant or organization is not operational, or the
    ///   claimed organization does not match the tenant's.
    pub async fn resolve(
        &self,
        principal: &SecurityPrincipal,
        claims: ScopeClaims,
    ) -> Result<ResolvedRequest> {
        // 1. Credential validity. An expired credential is an authentication
        //    failure and is never retried.
        if !principal.is_usable() {
            return Err(AuthFailure::expired_credential().to_app_error());
        }

        // 2. Choose the target tenant from identity, using the claim only as a
        //    selector among what the principal can already reach.
        let tenant_id = self.choose_tenant(principal, claims.tenant)?;

        // 3. Re-prove everything against the directory. The resolver hides
        //    cross-tenant existence and refuses non-operational tenants.
        let outcome = match self
            .resolver
            .resolve(Some(principal), tenant_id, claims.project)
            .await
        {
            Ok(outcome) => outcome,
            Err(error) if error.error_code() == "RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND" => {
                // Distinguish nothing: an unreachable tenant and an absent one
                // are the same answer, on purpose.
                return Err(AuthFailure::tenant_mismatch().as_hidden("tenant"));
            },
            Err(error) => return Err(error),
        };

        let resolved_organization = outcome.context.organization_id;

        // 4. A claimed organization that disagrees with the tenant's real one
        //    is blocked outright. This is the `tenant A + organization B` case
        //    from Phase 4: it is rejected rather than silently corrected,
        //    because a caller that believes two ids go together is a caller
        //    with a bug or an intent, and neither should be accommodated.
        if let Some(claimed) = claims.organization {
            if claimed != resolved_organization {
                return Err(AuthFailure::organization_mismatch().to_app_error());
            }
        }

        // The directory's answer about the role, not the principal's claim.
        let highest_role = outcome
            .context
            .roles
            .iter()
            .copied()
            .max_by_key(mas_domain::MembershipRole::rank);
        let principal = match highest_role {
            Some(role) => principal.clone().with_resolved_role(role),
            None => principal.clone(),
        };

        let mut scope = AuthoritativeScope::resolved(
            tenant_id,
            resolved_organization,
            principal.actor_id.clone(),
        );
        if let Some(project) = claims.project {
            // Only reachable here if the resolver proved the project belongs
            // to this tenant and organization; it errors otherwise.
            scope = scope.with_project(project);
        }

        Ok(ResolvedRequest { principal, scope })
    }

    /// Chooses the tenant: the claim when the principal can reach it, else the
    /// principal's own unambiguous binding.
    fn choose_tenant(
        &self,
        principal: &SecurityPrincipal,
        claimed: Option<TenantId>,
    ) -> Result<TenantId> {
        if let Some(claimed) = claimed {
            // The claim selects among reachable tenants. Anything else is
            // hidden, not refused.
            if !principal.can_reach_tenant(claimed) {
                return Err(AuthFailure::tenant_mismatch().as_hidden("tenant"));
            }
            return Ok(claimed);
        }

        // No claim: derive from identity, and only when unambiguous.
        if let Some(bound) = principal.tenant_id {
            return Ok(bound);
        }
        let distinct: BTreeSet<TenantId> = principal
            .memberships
            .iter()
            .map(|grant| grant.tenant_id)
            .collect();
        match distinct.len() {
            1 => Ok(distinct
                .into_iter()
                .next()
                .ok_or_else(|| AuthFailure::unauthenticated().to_app_error())?),
            0 => Err(mas_common::error::AppError::invalid_field(
                "x-tenant-id",
                "required",
                "this identity has no tenant binding of its own and must name one",
            )),
            _ => Err(mas_common::error::AppError::invalid_field(
                "x-tenant-id",
                "required",
                "the principal can reach more than one tenant; name one",
            )),
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use mas_domain::MembershipRole;
    use mas_security::{PrincipalKind, ScopeSet, TenantMembership};
    use mas_tenancy::{InMemoryDirectory, InMemoryMemberships, TenantDirectoryPort};
    use std::sync::Arc;

    fn id(seed: u128) -> uuid::Uuid {
        uuid::Uuid::from_u128(seed)
    }

    async fn world() -> (RequestScopeResolver, TenantId, OrganizationId, ProjectId) {
        let directory = Arc::new(InMemoryDirectory::new());
        let memberships = Arc::new(InMemoryMemberships::new());

        let organization = mas_domain::Organization::create(
            "Acme",
            "Acme",
            mas_domain::Slug::new("acme").expect("slug"),
        )
        .expect("org");
        let mut tenant = mas_domain::Tenant::create(
            organization.id,
            "Acme Prod",
            mas_domain::Slug::new("acme-prod").expect("slug"),
            mas_common::enums::Environment::Production,
            mas_domain::IsolationMode::SharedRls,
        )
        .expect("tenant");
        tenant.activate().expect("activate");
        let project = mas_domain::Project::create(
            tenant.id,
            organization.id,
            "Default",
            mas_domain::Slug::new("default").expect("slug"),
        )
        .expect("project");

        directory.upsert_organization(&organization).await.unwrap();
        directory.upsert_tenant(&tenant).await.unwrap();
        directory.upsert_project(&project).await.unwrap();

        let other_org = mas_domain::Organization::create(
            "Other",
            "Other",
            mas_domain::Slug::new("other").expect("slug"),
        )
        .expect("org");
        let mut other_tenant = mas_domain::Tenant::create(
            other_org.id,
            "Other Prod",
            mas_domain::Slug::new("other-prod").expect("slug"),
            mas_common::enums::Environment::Production,
            mas_domain::IsolationMode::SharedRls,
        )
        .expect("tenant");
        other_tenant.activate().expect("activate");
        directory.upsert_organization(&other_org).await.unwrap();
        directory.upsert_tenant(&other_tenant).await.unwrap();

        let resolver = TenantResolver::new(directory, memberships);
        (
            RequestScopeResolver::new(resolver),
            tenant.id,
            organization.id,
            project.id,
        )
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_principal_resolves_to_its_own_tenant_without_any_header() {
        let (resolver, tenant, organization, _project) = world().await;
        let principal = SecurityPrincipal::new(
            id(1).to_string(),
            PrincipalKind::ApiKey,
            Some(tenant),
            ScopeSet::denied(),
        )
        .with_organization(organization)
        .with_role(MembershipRole::Developer);

        let resolved = resolver
            .resolve(&principal, ScopeClaims::default())
            .await
            .expect("resolve");
        assert_eq!(resolved.scope.tenant_id(), tenant);
        assert_eq!(resolved.scope.organization_id(), organization);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_forged_tenant_header_is_hidden_not_forbidden() {
        let (resolver, tenant, organization, _project) = world().await;
        let other_tenant = TenantId::from_uuid(id(0xBBBB));
        let principal = SecurityPrincipal::new(
            id(1).to_string(),
            PrincipalKind::ApiKey,
            Some(tenant),
            ScopeSet::denied(),
        )
        .with_organization(organization)
        .with_role(MembershipRole::Developer);

        let error = resolver
            .resolve(
                &principal,
                ScopeClaims {
                    tenant: Some(other_tenant),
                    ..ScopeClaims::default()
                },
            )
            .await
            .expect_err("must not resolve");
        assert_eq!(error.error_code(), "RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND");
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_mismatched_organization_claim_is_a_deterministic_forbidden() {
        let (resolver, tenant, organization, _project) = world().await;
        let foreign_org = OrganizationId::from_uuid(id(0xCCCC));
        let principal = SecurityPrincipal::new(
            id(1).to_string(),
            PrincipalKind::ApiKey,
            Some(tenant),
            ScopeSet::denied(),
        )
        .with_organization(organization)
        .with_role(MembershipRole::Developer);

        let error = resolver
            .resolve(

                ScopeClaims {
                    organization: Some(foreign_org),
                    ..ScopeClaims::default()
                },
            )

        assert_eq!(error.error_code(), "FORBIDDEN");
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_cross_tenant_project_is_invisible() {
        let (resolver, tenant, organization, _project) = world().await;
        let principal = SecurityPrincipal::new(

            PrincipalKind::ApiKey,
            Some(tenant),

        )
        .with_organization(organization)
        .with_role(MembershipRole::Developer);

        // A project id belonging to the *other* tenant.

        let error = resolver
            .resolve(

                ScopeClaims {
                    project: Some(foreign_project),
                    ..ScopeClaims::default()

    #[tokio::test]

    #[tokio::test]

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn an_ambiguous_principal_must_name_a_tenant() {

        let principal = SecurityPrincipal::new(

        )
        .with_memberships(vec![

            ),
        ]);

        let error = resolver
            .resolve(&principal, ScopeClaims::default())
            .await
            .expect_err("ambiguous");
        assert_eq!(error.error_code(), "VALIDATION_FAILED");
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_principal_with_one_membership_resolves_to_it() {
        let (resolver, tenant, organization, _project) = world().await;
        let principal = SecurityPrincipal::new(
            id(1).to_string(),
            PrincipalKind::User,
            None,
            ScopeSet::denied(),
        )
        .with_memberships(vec![TenantMembership::new(
            organization,
            tenant,
            MembershipRole::Viewer,
        )]);

        let resolved = resolver
            .resolve(&principal, ScopeClaims::default())
            .await
            .expect("resolve");
        assert_eq!(resolved.scope.tenant_id(), tenant);
        // A directory with no membership rows for this user has no role to
        // prove, so the principal carries none — deny-by-default.
        assert_eq!(
            resolved.principal.role_in(tenant, organization),
            Some(MembershipRole::Viewer)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn auth_failures_are_never_retryable() {
        // A caller that retries an authorization failure is a caller looping
        // on a door that will not open; the type says so explicitly.
        assert!(!AuthFailure::tenant_mismatch().is_retryable());
        assert!(!AuthFailure::organization_mismatch().is_retryable());
    }

    #[test]
    fn hiding_a_resource_produces_not_found() {
        let hidden = AuthFailure::tenant_mismatch().as_hidden("tenant");
        assert_eq!(hidden.error_code(), "RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND");
        assert!(!AuthFailure::tenant_mismatch().is_authentication_failure());
    }
}
```

**PURPOSE:**

```text
Production API-key verification — the credential-to-principal
boundary.

Owning layer: `mas-api` (the process edge).

Production responsibility: look a presented API key up by its hash,
check expiry and revocation, and build the principal — carrying the
tenant and organization the KEY is bound to, not the ones the caller
asked for.

Security boundary: before this module was corrected the caller's
`x-tenant-id` header silently overrode the key's own tenant, so any key
could act in any tenant. Verification now carries the key's binding, and
the request's headers are only ever hints resolved against it.

It must NOT:
• take the tenant or organization from the request;
• accept an expired, revoked, or unknown key;
• return a reason that distinguishes "unknown key" from "revoked key".

Production bearer verification: database-backed API keys.

Flow per request (the only raw-secret-bearing code path in the API):
1. Reject tokens not shaped like `mas_<64 hex>` (precise fail-closed
shape check; anything else is not this platform's key family).
2. Take the visible prefix (`mas_` + first 8 chars), query candidates.
3. SHA-256 the raw token and compare digests in constant time — never
length-related loops, never logs with secret material.
4. Lifecycle guards (active, unexpired), stamp `last_used_at`
fire-and-forget, and produce a **tenant-bound** principal.

# What changed and why

The previous version returned `Principal { subject: <key id>, kind: ApiKey }`
and threw away `ApiKeyRow.tenant_id`. The caller's `x-tenant-id` header then
decided the scope, which meant a valid key minted in tenant A could be
presented with `x-tenant-id: B`. Verification now carries the key's own
tenant and organization into the principal, so the binding survives
authentication (spec Phase 8: keys are tenant-bound).

No caches: keys are revocable and revocation must take effect at the
next request (the same property that makes `last_used_at` meaningful).
```


**COMPLETE CONTENT** (252 lines):

```rust
//! PURPOSE: Production API-key verification — the credential-to-principal
//! boundary.
//!
//! Owning layer: `mas-api` (the process edge).
//!
//! Production responsibility: look a presented API key up by its hash,
//! check expiry and revocation, and build the principal — carrying the
//! tenant and organization the KEY is bound to, not the ones the caller
//! asked for.
//!
//! Security boundary: before this module was corrected the caller's
//! `x-tenant-id` header silently overrode the key's own tenant, so any key
//! could act in any tenant. Verification now carries the key's binding, and
//! the request's headers are only ever hints resolved against it.
//!
//! It must NOT:
//!   • take the tenant or organization from the request;
//!   • accept an expired, revoked, or unknown key;
//!   • return a reason that distinguishes "unknown key" from "revoked key".

//! Production bearer verification: database-backed API keys.
//!
//! Flow per request (the only raw-secret-bearing code path in the API):
//! 1. Reject tokens not shaped like `mas_<64 hex>` (precise fail-closed
//!    shape check; anything else is not this platform's key family).
//! 2. Take the visible prefix (`mas_` + first 8 chars), query candidates.
//! 3. SHA-256 the raw token and compare digests in constant time — never
//!    length-related loops, never logs with secret material.
//! 4. Lifecycle guards (active, unexpired), stamp `last_used_at`
//!    fire-and-forget, and produce a **tenant-bound** principal.
//!
//! # What changed and why
//!
//! The previous version returned `Principal { subject: <key id>, kind: ApiKey }`
//! and threw away `ApiKeyRow.tenant_id`. The caller's `x-tenant-id` header then
//! decided the scope, which meant a valid key minted in tenant A could be
//! presented with `x-tenant-id: B`. Verification now carries the key's own
//! tenant and organization into the principal, so the binding survives
//! authentication (spec Phase 8: keys are tenant-bound).
//!
//! No caches: keys are revocable and revocation must take effect at the
//! next request (the same property that makes `last_used_at` meaningful).

use async_trait::async_trait;
use mas_persistence::repositories::api_keys::ApiKeyStore;

use crate::auth::TokenVerifierPort;
use mas_common::constants::{API_KEY_PREFIX, API_KEY_VISIBLE_PREFIX_LEN};
use mas_common::error::AppError;
use mas_common::ids::UserId;
use mas_common::result::Result;
use mas_security::{PrincipalKind, ScopeSet, SecurityPrincipal, TenantMembership};

const UNAUTHENTICATED: &str = "unauthenticated";

/// Database-backed verifier for the production bearer boundary.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct PostgresApiKeyVerifier {
    store: ApiKeyStore,
}

impl PostgresApiKeyVerifier {
    /// Binds a verifier to the shared pool-backed store.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn new(store: ApiKeyStore) -> Self {
        Self { store }
    }

    /// Extracts the well-known public shard of a raw key.
    fn visible_prefix(raw: &str) -> String {
        raw.chars()
            .take(API_KEY_PREFIX.len() + API_KEY_VISIBLE_PREFIX_LEN)
            .collect()
    }

    /// Constant-time hex digest comparison (a timing oracle here would
    /// subdivide the digest space — the comparison never short-circuits).
    fn digests_equal(a: &str, b: &str) -> bool {
        let left = a.as_bytes();
        let right = b.as_bytes();
        if left.len() != right.len() {
            return false;
        }
        let mut acc = 0u8;
        for (x, y) in left.iter().zip(right.iter()) {
            acc |= x ^ y;
        }
        acc == 0
    }

    /// Shape guard: `mas_` + exactly 64 lowercase hex characters.
    fn is_shaped_like_platform_key(raw: &str) -> bool {
        let Some(rest) = raw.strip_prefix(API_KEY_PREFIX) else {
            return false;
        };
        rest.len() == 64
            && rest
                .chars()
                .all(|c| c.is_ascii_hexdigit() && !c.is_ascii_uppercase())
    }

    /// Lifts the row's scopes into a `ScopeSet`.
    ///
    /// A row whose scopes cannot be parsed is a minting or migration bug, and
    /// the safe reading of it is "no scopes" rather than "all scopes".
    fn scopes_from(row: &mas_persistence::repositories::api_keys::ApiKeyRow) -> ScopeSet {
        serde_json::from_value::<Vec<String>>(row.scopes.clone())
            .ok()
            .and_then(|scopes| ScopeSet::new(scopes).ok())
            .unwrap_or_else(ScopeSet::denied)
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl TokenVerifierPort for PostgresApiKeyVerifier {
    async fn verify(&self, token: &str) -> Result<SecurityPrincipal> {
        // All failure paths share ONE error body: no oracle refinement.
        let unauthenticated = || AppError::unauthorized(UNAUTHENTICATED);

        if !Self::is_shaped_like_platform_key(token) {
            return Err(unauthenticated());
        }
        let candidates = self
            .store
            .find_by_prefix(&Self::visible_prefix(token))
            .await
            .map_err(|_| unauthenticated())?;
        let digest = mas_security::api_keys::hash_key(token);
        let Some(row) = candidates
            .into_iter()
            .find(|candidate| Self::digests_equal(&candidate.secret_hash, &digest))
        else {
            return Err(unauthenticated());
        };
        if row.status != "active" {
            return Err(unauthenticated());
        }
        if let Some(expires_at) = row.expires_at {
            if expires_at <= chrono::Utc::now() {
                return Err(unauthenticated());
            }
        }
        // Telemetry best-effort: never let the marker write block authN.
        let _ = self.store.touch_last_used(row.id).await;

        // The key row decides the tenant. This is the whole point of the
        // change: a bearer secret is bound to the tenant that minted it, and
        // no header on the request can move it.
        let tenant_id = mas_common::ids::TenantId::from_uuid(row.tenant_id);
        let organization_id = mas_common::ids::OrganizationId::from_uuid(row.organization_id);

        let mut principal = SecurityPrincipal::new(
            format!("api-key:{}", row.id),
            PrincipalKind::ApiKey,
            Some(tenant_id),
            Self::scopes_from(&row),
        )
        .with_organization(organization_id)
        .with_role(row.role);

        // The key's own binding is a credential grant, expressed in the same
        // shape the resolver uses for memberships so one code path answers
        // "what role here" for every kind of principal.
        principal
            .memberships
            .push(TenantMembership::new(organization_id, tenant_id, row.role));

        if let Some(user_id) = row.user_id {
            // A key minted by a user is still a key: the actor is the key, and
            // the creating user is recorded for audit only. It never widens
            // the key's authority.
            principal
                .roles
                .push(format!("created_by:{}", UserId::from_uuid(user_id)));
        }

        Ok(principal)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn shape_guard_pins_the_contracted_format() {
        assert!(PostgresApiKeyVerifier::is_shaped_like_platform_key(
            &format!("mas_{}", "a".repeat(64))
        ));
        assert!(!PostgresApiKeyVerifier::is_shaped_like_platform_key(
            "mas_short"
        ));
        assert!(!PostgresApiKeyVerifier::is_shaped_like_platform_key(
            &format!("mas_{}", "A".repeat(64))
        ));
        assert!(!PostgresApiKeyVerifier::is_shaped_like_platform_key(
            &format!("posix_{}", "a".repeat(64))
        ));
        assert!(!PostgresApiKeyVerifier::is_shaped_like_platform_key(
            &format!("mas_{}", "a".repeat(63))
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn digest_compare_is_exact_and_long_length_safe() {
        let digest = "a".repeat(64);
        assert!(PostgresApiKeyVerifier::digests_equal(&digest, &digest));
        assert!(!PostgresApiKeyVerifier::digests_equal(
            &digest,
            &"a".repeat(63)
        ));
        assert!(!PostgresApiKeyVerifier::digests_equal(
            &digest,
            &"b".repeat(64)
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn visible_prefix_formula_matches_api_constants() {
        let token = format!("mas_{}", "deadbeef".repeat(8));
        let prefix = PostgresApiKeyVerifier::visible_prefix(&token);
        assert_eq!(
            prefix.len(),
            API_KEY_PREFIX.len() + API_KEY_VISIBLE_PREFIX_LEN
        );
        assert!(token.starts_with(&prefix));
    }

    /// A key row whose scopes are unusable must not become a wildcard.
    #[test]
    fn unparseable_scopes_degrade_to_no_scopes() {
        let row = mas_persistence::repositories::api_keys::ApiKeyRow {
            id: uuid::Uuid::now_v7(),
            tenant_id: uuid::Uuid::now_v7(),
            organization_id: uuid::Uuid::now_v7(),
            role: mas_domain::MembershipRole::ServiceAccount,
            user_id: None,
            name: "svc".to_owned(),
            prefix: "mas_deadbeef".to_owned(),
            secret_hash: "a".repeat(64),
            scopes: serde_json::json!("not-an-array"),
            status: "active".to_owned(),
            expires_at: None,
            last_used_at: None,
        };
        let scopes = PostgresApiKeyVerifier::scopes_from(&row);
        assert!(
            !scopes.permits("executions:read"),
            "a malformed scope blob must not grant anything"
        );
    }
}
```

## FILE: repo/enterprise-mas/rust-core/crates/scheduler-service/src/egress.rs


**PURPOSE:**

```text
The real network client behind the SSRF guard.

Owning layer: `mas-scheduler-service` (and, by extension, any process that
makes outbound HTTP). `mas-integrations` deliberately ships no concrete
client so the policy layer stays testable; this is the production binding
of `HttpClientPort`.

Production responsibility: spec Phase 23. The guard in
`mas_integrations::http_guard` was correct and complete but had no
dependents — the scheduler's outbound dispatcher built a bare
`reqwest::Client` and posted straight to whatever URL it was configured
with, so the guard was dead code. Every outbound request now goes through
`GuardedHttpClient<ReqwestEgress>`.

Security boundary: this is the only place in the scheduler process where a
socket is opened to a host named by configuration. It is therefore where
DNS rebinding is defeated: the hostname is resolved here, every answer is
checked by `EgressPolicy::pin_resolution`, and the connection is made to
the pinned *address* with the original `Host` header preserved. A hostile
DNS record that answers with `169.254.169.254` on the second lookup cannot
win, because the address is pinned before the socket is opened and never
re-resolved.

It must NOT:
• let `reqwest` resolve the hostname itself — that would reintroduce the
TOCTOU window the pinning exists to close;
• follow redirects itself. Redirects belong to `GuardedHttpClient`, which
re-validates every hop against the policy;
• read an unbounded response body. The cap is enforced here as well as in
the guard, because a cap that exists in only one layer is a cap that
disappears the moment the other is bypassed.
```


**COMPLETE CONTENT** (267 lines):

```rust
// PURPOSE: The real network client behind the SSRF guard.
//
// Owning layer: `mas-scheduler-service` (and, by extension, any process that
// makes outbound HTTP). `mas-integrations` deliberately ships no concrete
// client so the policy layer stays testable; this is the production binding
// of `HttpClientPort`.
//
// Production responsibility: spec Phase 23. The guard in
// `mas_integrations::http_guard` was correct and complete but had no
// dependents — the scheduler's outbound dispatcher built a bare
// `reqwest::Client` and posted straight to whatever URL it was configured
// with, so the guard was dead code. Every outbound request now goes through
// `GuardedHttpClient<ReqwestEgress>`.
//
// Security boundary: this is the only place in the scheduler process where a
// socket is opened to a host named by configuration. It is therefore where
// DNS rebinding is defeated: the hostname is resolved here, every answer is
// checked by `EgressPolicy::pin_resolution`, and the connection is made to
// the pinned *address* with the original `Host` header preserved. A hostile
// DNS record that answers with `169.254.169.254` on the second lookup cannot
// win, because the address is pinned before the socket is opened and never
// re-resolved.
//
// It must NOT:
//   • let `reqwest` resolve the hostname itself — that would reintroduce the
//     TOCTOU window the pinning exists to close;
//   • follow redirects itself. Redirects belong to `GuardedHttpClient`, which
//     re-validates every hop against the policy;
//   • read an unbounded response body. The cap is enforced here as well as in
//     the guard, because a cap that exists in only one layer is a cap that
//     disappears the moment the other is bypassed.

use std::net::IpAddr;
use std::time::Duration;

use async_trait::async_trait;
use mas_common::error::AppError;
use mas_common::result::Result;
use mas_integrations::http_guard::{
    EgressPolicy, HttpClientPort, HttpMethod, HttpRequest, HttpResponse,
};

/// A `reqwest` client bound to the egress policy.
///
/// Holds a `reqwest::Client` with redirects disabled: following them here
/// would move a security decision out of the guard, which is the one place
/// that re-checks the destination of every hop.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct ReqwestEgress {
    client: reqwest::Client,
    policy: EgressPolicy,
}

impl ReqwestEgress {
    /// Builds a client with redirects off and a hard connect/read timeout.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// Fails only if the underlying client cannot be constructed, which is a
    /// process-level misconfiguration rather than a request failure.
    pub fn new(policy: EgressPolicy) -> Result<Self> {
        let client = reqwest::Client::builder()
            // Redirects are the guard's job, not ours.
            .redirect(reqwest::redirect::Policy::none())
            .https_only(policy.https_only)
            .build()
            .map_err(|err| AppError::external_service("http-client", err.to_string()))?;
        Ok(Self { client, policy })
    }

    /// The policy this client enforces.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn policy(&self) -> &EgressPolicy {
        &self.policy
    }

    /// Resolves `host` and returns the one address the socket may use.
    ///
    /// Every answer is checked, not just the first: a resolver that returns
    /// one public and one private address is refused outright, because a
    /// client that retries on failure would otherwise reach the private one.
    async fn pin(&self, host: &str, port: u16, internal_endpoint: bool) -> Result<IpAddr> {
        let authority = format!("{host}:{port}");
        // `std`'s resolver is blocking, so it runs off the async worker.
        // Pinning must happen before the socket is opened either way; doing
        // it here keeps the resolution and the connect in the same call.
        let resolved = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
            std::net::ToSocketAddrs::to_socket_addrs(&authority)
                .map(|iter| iter.collect::<Vec<std::net::SocketAddr>>())
        })
        .await
        .map_err(|err| {
            AppError::external_service("http-egress", format!("dns resolution task failed: {err}"))
        })?
        .map_err(|err| {
            AppError::external_service(
                "http-egress",
                format!("dns resolution of {host} failed: {err}"),
            )
        })?;
        let addresses: Vec<IpAddr> = resolved.iter().map(std::net::SocketAddr::ip).collect();
        self.policy
            .pin_resolution_for(&addresses, internal_endpoint)
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl HttpClientPort for ReqwestEgress {
    async fn send(&self, request: &HttpRequest) -> Result<HttpResponse> {
        let url = url::Url::parse(request.url.as_str()).map_err(|err| {
            AppError::internal(format!("validated SafeUrl failed re-parse: {err}"))
        })?;
        let host = url
            .host_str()
            .ok_or_else(|| AppError::validation("egress url has no host"))?
            .to_owned();
        let port = url.port_or_known_default().unwrap_or(443);

        // Resolve first, pin the address, then connect to the address. `Host`
        // carries the original name so TLS and virtual hosting still work.
        let pinned = self
            .pin(&host, port, request.url.is_internal_endpoint())
            .await?;

        let method = match request.method {
            HttpMethod::Get => reqwest::Method::GET,
            HttpMethod::Post => reqwest::Method::POST,
            HttpMethod::Put => reqwest::Method::PUT,
        };

        // Rebuild the URL against the pinned address so no second resolution
        // can happen inside `reqwest`.
        let mut pinned_url = url.clone();
        pinned_url
            .set_ip_host(pinned)
            .map_err(|_| AppError::internal("could not pin the resolved address into the url"))?;

        let mut builder = self
            .client
            .request(method, pinned_url)
            .timeout(Duration::from_millis(request.timeout_ms))
            .header(reqwest::header::HOST, host.clone());
        for (name, value) in &request.headers {
            builder = builder.header(name.as_str(), value.as_str());
        }
        if !request.body.is_empty() {
            builder = builder.body(request.body.clone());
        }

        let response = builder.send().await.map_err(|err| {
            AppError::external_service("http-egress", format!("request to {host} failed: {err}"))
        })?;

        let status = response.status().as_u16();
        let mut headers = Vec::new();
        for (name, value) in response.headers().iter() {
            headers.push((
                name.as_str().to_ascii_lowercase(),
                value.to_str().unwrap_or_default().to_owned(),
            ));
        }

        // The body cap is enforced here, not only in the guard: this is the
        // layer that actually reads the bytes.
        let bytes = response.bytes().await.map_err(|err| {
            AppError::external_service(
                "http-egress",
                format!("reading the response from {host} failed: {err}"),
            )
        })?;
        if bytes.len() > self.policy.max_body_bytes {
            return Err(AppError::external_service(
                "http-egress",
                format!(
                    "response body from {host} exceeded the {} byte cap",
                    self.policy.max_body_bytes
                ),
            ));
        }

        Ok(HttpResponse {
            status,
            headers,
            body: bytes.to_vec(),
        })
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use mas_integrations::http_guard::is_publicly_routable;
    use std::net::{IpAddr, Ipv4Addr, Ipv6Addr};

    fn addr(raw: &str) -> IpAddr {
        raw.parse().expect("ip")
    }

    /// The address classes Phase 23 enumerates: loopback, private RFC1918,
    /// link-local, the cloud metadata address, unique-local IPv6 and
    /// IPv4-mapped IPv6 must all be refused.
    #[test]
    fn every_forbidden_address_class_is_refused() {
        let policy = EgressPolicy::default();
        for forbidden in [
            "127.0.0.1",
            "127.1.2.3",
            "::1",
            "10.0.0.1",
            "172.16.0.1",
            "192.168.1.1",
            "169.254.169.254",
            "169.254.0.1",
            "0.0.0.0",
            "255.255.255.255",
            "fd00::1",
            "fe80::1",
            "::ffff:127.0.0.1",
        ] {
            assert!(
                !is_publicly_routable(&addr(forbidden)),
                "{forbidden} must not be considered publicly routable"
            );
            assert!(
                policy.pin_resolution(&[addr(forbidden)]).is_err(),
                "pin_resolution must refuse {forbidden}"
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn public_addresses_are_allowed() {
        let policy = EgressPolicy::default();
        for allowed in ["93.184.216.34", "2606:2800:220:1:248:1893:25c8:1946"] {
            assert!(is_publicly_routable(&addr(allowed)), "{allowed} is public");
            assert!(policy.pin_resolution(&[addr(allowed)]).is_ok());
        }
    }

    /// A resolver that mixes one good answer with one bad one is refused:
    /// a client that retries on failure would otherwise reach the bad one.
    #[test]
    fn a_single_bad_answer_poisons_the_whole_resolution() {
        let policy = EgressPolicy::default();
        let mixed = [addr("93.184.216.34"), addr("169.254.169.254")];
        assert!(policy.pin_resolution(&mixed).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_empty_resolution_is_a_failure_not_a_default() {
        let policy = EgressPolicy::default();
        assert!(policy.pin_resolution(&[]).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_client_disables_redirects_so_the_guard_owns_them() {
        let client = ReqwestEgress::new(EgressPolicy::default()).expect("client");
        assert_eq!(client.policy().max_redirects, 3);
    }

    #[test]
    fn ipv4_mapped_ipv6_is_judged_by_its_embedded_address() {
        let mapped = IpAddr::V6(Ipv4Addr::new(10, 0, 0, 1).to_ipv6_mapped());
        assert!(!is_publicly_routable(&mapped));
        let public = IpAddr::V6(Ipv6Addr::LOCALHOST);
        assert!(!is_publicly_routable(&public));
    }
}
```

## FILE: repo/enterprise-mas/rust-core/crates/integrations/src/http_guard.rs


**PURPOSE:**

```text
The SSRF egress guard — the policy every production outbound
HTTP call goes through.

Owning layer: `mas-integrations`.

Production responsibility: decide whether a destination is reachable at
all: reject link-local, loopback, and metadata addresses unless a caller
names them explicitly as internal endpoints.

Security boundary: without this, any feature that fetches a URL becomes a
request forgery into the cluster. Reaching a private range is a decision
somebody makes on purpose, in code, for a named host.

It must NOT:
• allow a redirect to re-target an approved request into a private
range;
• be optional for production callers — `HttpDispatcher` holds one and
every dispatch goes through it;
• resolve a hostname more than once (DNS rebinding).

Hardened egress: the SSRF enforcement layer promised by `SafeUrl`.

`SafeUrl` performs first-line validation at parse time (scheme, no
embedded credentials, no private/loopback IP literals). This module adds
everything parse time *cannot* know:
```
