## FILE: repo/enterprise-mas/rust-core/crates/scheduling/src/runner.rs


**PURPOSE:**

```text
The deterministic scheduler runtime: which due schedules a tick
fires, in what order, and how a failed run is retried.

Owning layer: `mas-scheduling` (domain logic; no clock, no I/O of its own).

Production responsibility: turn "these schedules are due" into an ordered,
fair, overlap-safe list of runs, and report every branch in a
`TickReport`. Time is a parameter, never read from a clock, so every
branch is unit-testable.

Security boundary: the runtime decides *when* work fires, never *whose*
work it is. Tenancy arrives in `DueWork` from the store's due-scan, and the
runtime passes it through untouched — it has no mechanism and no license to
infer, default, or substitute a tenant. Fairness interleaving keys on
tenant so a large tenant cannot starve a small one, which is an
availability property and not an isolation one: isolation is enforced by
row-level security in the store, below the runtime.

It must NOT:
• read a clock — `now` is always a parameter;
• touch a database, a broker or a socket: those are ports;
• swallow a per-schedule failure into a whole-tick failure.

The deterministic scheduler runtime: scan → lease → queue → dispatch,
plus crash recovery.

`tick(now)` takes an explicit timestamp, so the whole lifecycle is
unit-testable without sleeping; the production driver
(`scheduler-service`) simply calls `tick(Timestamp::now())` on a
`tokio::time::interval` and renews its leases.

One tick:
1. Scan due schedules through the store (`list_due`).
2. For each due schedule: renew its lease (fencing) — contention loses
the schedule to the other replica, and that's *correct*.
3. Catch-up decision (domain rules + policy) and overlap check.
4. Enqueue the resulting runs (queue dedups exact replays).
5. Pop the fair batch and hand it to the [`DispatchPort`].
6. Record runs + write the advanced schedule state back.
```


**COMPLETE CONTENT** (599 lines):

```rust
//! PURPOSE: The deterministic scheduler runtime: which due schedules a tick
//! fires, in what order, and how a failed run is retried.
//!
//! Owning layer: `mas-scheduling` (domain logic; no clock, no I/O of its own).
//!
//! Production responsibility: turn "these schedules are due" into an ordered,
//! fair, overlap-safe list of runs, and report every branch in a
//! `TickReport`. Time is a parameter, never read from a clock, so every
//! branch is unit-testable.
//!
//! Security boundary: the runtime decides *when* work fires, never *whose*
//! work it is. Tenancy arrives in `DueWork` from the store's due-scan, and the
//! runtime passes it through untouched — it has no mechanism and no license to
//! infer, default, or substitute a tenant. Fairness interleaving keys on
//! tenant so a large tenant cannot starve a small one, which is an
//! availability property and not an isolation one: isolation is enforced by
//! row-level security in the store, below the runtime.
//!
//! It must NOT:
//!   • read a clock — `now` is always a parameter;
//!   • touch a database, a broker or a socket: those are ports;
//!   • swallow a per-schedule failure into a whole-tick failure.

//! The deterministic scheduler runtime: scan → lease → queue → dispatch,
//! plus crash recovery.
//!
//! `tick(now)` takes an explicit timestamp, so the whole lifecycle is
//! unit-testable without sleeping; the production driver
//! (`scheduler-service`) simply calls `tick(Timestamp::now())` on a
//! `tokio::time::interval` and renews its leases.
//!
//! One tick:
//! 1. Scan due schedules through the store (`list_due`).
//! 2. For each due schedule: renew its lease (fencing) — contention loses
//!    the schedule to the other replica, and that's *correct*.
//! 3. Catch-up decision (domain rules + policy) and overlap check.
//! 4. Enqueue the resulting runs (queue dedups exact replays).
//! 5. Pop the fair batch and hand it to the [`DispatchPort`].
//! 6. Record runs + write the advanced schedule state back.

use mas_common::error::AppError;
use mas_common::ids::{ExecutionId, ScheduleId};
use mas_common::result::Result;
use mas_common::timestamps::Timestamp;

use crate::due::{DueScanner, DueWork, ScanConfig};
use crate::lease::{schedule_resource, Lease, LeaseStorePort};
use crate::policies::{
    decide_catch_up, decide_overlap, CatchUpPolicy, OverlapAction, OverlapPolicy,
};
use crate::queue::DelayedQueue;
use crate::store::ScheduleStorePort;

/// How one dispatched work item was accepted downstream.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum DispatchAck {
    /// Execution created; the run is in flight.
    Started {
        /// The created execution tracking id.
        execution: ExecutionId,
    },
    /// Work accepted but deferred (dispatcher at capacity); scheduler will
    /// keep the run queued for the next tick.
    Deferred,
}

/// What the runtime hands work to (the execution engine adapter).
#[async_trait::async_trait]
pub trait DispatchPort: Send + Sync + std::fmt::Debug {
    /// Dispatches one due run; failing here keeps the run queued next tick.
    async fn dispatch(&self, work: &DueWork) -> Result<DispatchAck>;

    /// Whether a schedule currently has an in-flight run (overlap input).
    async fn is_running(&self, schedule: ScheduleId) -> Result<bool>;

    /// Marks a schedule's run finished (success or failure — overlap bookkeeping).
    async fn mark_finished(&self, schedule: ScheduleId) -> Result<()>;
}

/// Delegation so a shared dispatcher can be handed to [`SchedulerRuntime`].
///
/// The scheduler process picks its dispatcher at boot — durable submission or
/// an internal HTTP call — so the concrete type is only known at runtime and
/// arrives behind an `Arc`. Without this impl every caller would need a
/// hand-written forwarding wrapper, and each wrapper would be one more place
/// for a future method to be silently forgotten.
#[async_trait::async_trait]
impl<T> DispatchPort for std::sync::Arc<T>
where
    T: DispatchPort + ?Sized,
{
    async fn dispatch(&self, work: &DueWork) -> Result<DispatchAck> {
        (**self).dispatch(work).await
    }

    async fn is_running(&self, schedule: ScheduleId) -> Result<bool> {
        (**self).is_running(schedule).await
    }

    async fn mark_finished(&self, schedule: ScheduleId) -> Result<()> {
        (**self).mark_finished(schedule).await
    }
}

/// Runtime configuration.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct SchedulerConfig {
    /// This replica's identity (lease holder).
    pub replica_id: String,
    /// Scan size per tick.
    pub scan: ScanConfig,
    /// Max runs dispatched per tick.
    pub dispatch_batch: usize,
    /// Overlap default when the schedule does not declare one.
    pub default_overlap: OverlapPolicy,
    /// Catch-up default when the schedule has `catch_up = false`.
    pub default_catch_up: CatchUpPolicy,
}

impl SchedulerConfig {
    /// Validates the knobs.
    pub fn validated(self) -> Result<Self> {
        if self.replica_id.trim().is_empty() {
            return Err(AppError::validation("replica_id must not be empty"));
        }
        self.scan.validated()?;
        if self.dispatch_batch == 0 || self.dispatch_batch > 10_000 {
            return Err(AppError::validation("dispatch_batch must be 1..=10_000"));
        }
        Ok(self)
    }

    /// Reasonable single-replica defaults for tests/local dev.
    pub fn local(replica_id: impl Into<String>) -> Result<Self> {
        Self {
            replica_id: replica_id.into(),
            scan: ScanConfig::default(),
            dispatch_batch: 100,
            default_overlap: OverlapPolicy::default(),
            default_catch_up: CatchUpPolicy::Skip,
        }
        .validated()
    }
}

/// What happened in one tick (observability + tests).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct TickReport {
    /// Schedules the store returned as candidates.
    pub scanned: usize,
    /// Due schedules after filtering.
    pub due: usize,
    /// Runs dispatched successfully this tick.
    pub dispatched: usize,
    /// Runs skipped by overlap policy.
    pub overlap_skipped: usize,
    /// Runs skipped by catch-up policy.
    pub catch_up_skipped: usize,
    /// Schedules lost to lease contention (another replica owns them).
    pub lease_lost: usize,
    /// Dispatch failures (runs remain queued; retried next tick).
    pub dispatch_errors: usize,
}

/// What startup recovery did.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct RecoveryReport {
    /// Leases reaped as expired (their holders are presumed dead).
    pub leases_reaped: usize,
    /// Due schedules immediately re-enqueued after restart.
    pub schedules_rescanned: usize,
}

/// The deterministic scheduler runtime.
pub struct SchedulerRuntime<S: ScheduleStorePort, L: LeaseStorePort, D: DispatchPort> {
    store: S,
    leases: L,
    dispatch: D,
    queue: DelayedQueue,
    config: SchedulerConfig,
}

impl<S, L, D> std::fmt::Debug for SchedulerRuntime<S, L, D>
where
    S: ScheduleStorePort,
    L: LeaseStorePort,
    D: DispatchPort,
{
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("SchedulerRuntime")
            .field("replica", &self.config.replica_id)
            .field("queue_len", &self.queue.len())
            .finish_non_exhaustive()
    }
}

impl<S: ScheduleStorePort, L: LeaseStorePort, D: DispatchPort> SchedulerRuntime<S, L, D> {
    /// Builds a runtime from its ports.
    pub fn new(store: S, leases: L, dispatch: D, config: SchedulerConfig) -> Result<Self> {
        let config = config.validated()?;
        Ok(Self {
            store,
            leases,
            dispatch,
            queue: DelayedQueue::default(),
            config,
        })
    }

    /// Startup recovery: reaps expired leases (so due schedules are
    /// acquirable again) and re-enqueues anything already due.
    pub async fn recover(&mut self, now: &Timestamp) -> Result<RecoveryReport> {
        let reaped = self.leases.reap_expired(now).await?;
        if !reaped.is_empty() {
            tracing::info!(count = reaped.len(), "reaped expired scheduler leases");
        }
        let due = self
            .store
            .list_due(now, self.config.scan.batch_limit)
            .await?;
        let scanned = due.len();
        let batch = DueScanner::scan(&due, now, &self.config.scan)?;
        for work in batch {
            let _ = self.queue.push(work)?;
        }
        Ok(RecoveryReport {
            leases_reaped: reaped.len(),
            schedules_rescanned: scanned,
        })
    }

    /// One scheduler tick. Never fails wholesale: per-schedule failures are
    /// counted in the report and retried next tick.
    pub async fn tick(&mut self, now: &Timestamp) -> Result<TickReport> {
        let mut report = TickReport::default();

        // 1) scan
        let candidates = self
            .store
            .list_due(now, self.config.scan.batch_limit)
            .await?;
        report.scanned = candidates.len();
        let due_work = DueScanner::scan(&candidates, now, &self.config.scan)?;
        report.due = due_work.len();

        // 2-4) per-schedule pipeline
        for work in due_work {
            match self.prepare_run(&work, now).await {
                Prepared::Runs(works) => {
                    for work in works {
                        let _ = self.queue.push(work)?;
                    }
                },
                Prepared::OverlapSkip => report.overlap_skipped += 1,
                Prepared::CatchUpSkip(skipped) => report.catch_up_skipped += skipped,
                Prepared::LeaseLost => report.lease_lost += 1,
            }
        }

        // 5) dispatch the fair batch
        let batch = self.queue.take_due(now, self.config.dispatch_batch);
        for work in batch {
            match self.dispatch.dispatch(&work).await {
                Ok(DispatchAck::Started { .. }) => {
                    report.dispatched += 1;
                    self.complete_run(&work, now).await;
                },
                Ok(DispatchAck::Deferred) => {
                    // Back in the queue for next tick.
                    if let Err(err) = self.queue.push(work.clone()) {
                        tracing::warn!(error = %err, run = %work.run_key(), "re-queue failed");
                    }
                },
                Err(err) => {
                    report.dispatch_errors += 1;
                    tracing::warn!(
                        error = %err,
                        run = %work.run_key(),
                        "dispatch failed; run re-queued"
                    );
                    if let Err(push_err) = self.queue.push(work.clone()) {
                        tracing::warn!(error = %push_err, run = %work.run_key(), "re-queue failed");
                    }
                },
            }
        }
        Ok(report)
    }

    /// Runs one due schedule through lease + catch-up + overlap, returning
    /// the runs to enqueue (0..=1+N: bounded catch-up replays then the due
    /// tick) or the skip classification.
    async fn prepare_run(&self, work: &DueWork, now: &Timestamp) -> Prepared {
        // 1. Lease: fencing against the other replica. Losing is normal
        //    multi-replica operation, not an error.
        let resource = schedule_resource(&work.schedule_id);
        match self
            .leases
            .try_acquire(
                &resource,
                &self.config.replica_id,
                crate::lease::DEFAULT_LEASE_TTL,
                now,
            )
            .await
        {
            Ok(lease) => {
                self.note_lease_held(work.schedule_id, lease);
            },
            Err(err) if err.error_code() == "CONFLICT" => return Prepared::LeaseLost,
            Err(err) => {
                tracing::warn!(error = %err, resource = %resource, "lease acquisition failed");
                return Prepared::LeaseLost;
            },
        }

        // 2. Refresh the schedule (it may have changed since the scan).
        let Some(schedule) = (match self.store.get(work.schedule_id).await {
            Ok(s) => s,
            Err(err) => {
                tracing::warn!(error = %err, "schedule refresh failed");
                return Prepared::LeaseLost;
            },
        }) else {
            return Prepared::CatchUpSkip(1);
        };

        // 3. Overlap: previous run still executing?
        let running = self.dispatch.is_running(schedule.id).await.unwrap_or(false);
        if decide_overlap(self.config.default_overlap, running) == OverlapAction::Skip {
            return Prepared::OverlapSkip;
        }

        // 4. Catch-up over ticks *strictly before* the due tick:
        //    enumerate planned ticks after `last_run_at` but before this
        //    tick — those are the ones a pause/downtime made us miss.
        let since = schedule.last_run_at.unwrap_or(work.planned_at);
        let before_due = work
            .planned_at
            .checked_sub(std::time::Duration::from_millis(1))
            .unwrap_or(work.planned_at);
        let policy = CatchUpPolicy::for_schedule(&schedule);
        let decision = match decide_catch_up(&schedule, since, &before_due, policy) {
            Ok(d) => d,
            Err(err) => {
                tracing::warn!(error = %err, schedule = %schedule.id, "catch-up decision failed");
                return Prepared::CatchUpSkip(1);
            },
        };

        let mut runs: Vec<DueWork> = decision
            .fire_at
            .iter()
            .map(|planned_at| DueWork {
                planned_at: *planned_at,
                ..work.clone()
            })
            .collect();
        // The due tick itself always fires.
        runs.push(work.clone());
        Prepared::Runs(runs)
    }

    fn note_lease_held(&self, schedule: ScheduleId, lease: Lease) {
        let _ = (schedule, lease);
        // Held-lease registry lives with the driving service
        // (scheduler-service), which renews/releases on shutdown; the
        // runtime itself treats acquisition as the fencing point.
    }

    /// After a successful dispatch: record the run + advance the schedule.
    async fn complete_run(&self, work: &DueWork, now: &Timestamp) {
        if let Err(err) = self
            .store
            .record_run(work.schedule_id, work.planned_at)
            .await
        {
            tracing::warn!(error = %err, "run record write failed (exactly-once ledger)");
        }
        if let Ok(Some(mut schedule)) = self.store.get(work.schedule_id).await {
            let fired_at = *now;
            if let Err(err) = schedule.mark_fired(fired_at) {
                tracing::warn!(error = %err, "schedule advance failed");
                return;
            }
            if let Err(err) = self.store.save(&schedule).await {
                tracing::warn!(error = %err, "schedule write-back failed");
            }
        }
    }

    /// Queue depth (observability).
    #[must_use]
    pub fn queue_len(&self) -> usize {
        self.queue.len()
    }
}

enum Prepared {
    Runs(Vec<DueWork>),
    OverlapSkip,
    CatchUpSkip(usize),
    LeaseLost,
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::lease::InMemoryLeaseStore;
    use crate::store::InMemoryScheduleStore;
    use mas_common::ids::TenantId;
    use mas_domain::schedule::{Schedule, ScheduleKind};
    use std::collections::BTreeSet;
    use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};
    use std::sync::Mutex;

    #[derive(Debug, Default)]
    struct FakeDispatch {
        started: AtomicUsize,
        running: Mutex<BTreeSet<ScheduleId>>,
        failing_left: Mutex<u32>,
    }

    #[async_trait::async_trait]
    impl DispatchPort for FakeDispatch {
        async fn dispatch(&self, work: &DueWork) -> Result<DispatchAck> {
            let mut failing = self.failing_left.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
            if *failing > 0 {
                *failing -= 1;
                return Err(AppError::internal("synthetic dispatch failure"));
            }
            drop(failing);
            self.started.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
            self.running
                .lock()
                .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
                .insert(work.schedule_id);
            Ok(DispatchAck::Started {
                execution: ExecutionId::new(),
            })
        }

        async fn is_running(&self, schedule: ScheduleId) -> Result<bool> {
            Ok(self
                .running
                .lock()
                .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
                .contains(&schedule))
        }

        async fn mark_finished(&self, schedule: ScheduleId) -> Result<()> {
            self.running
                .lock()
                .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
                .remove(&schedule);
            Ok(())
        }
    }

    fn due_schedule(name: &str, every_seconds: u64, lateness: u64) -> Schedule {
        let mut s = Schedule::new(
            TenantId::new(),
            None,
            name,
            ScheduleKind::Interval { every_seconds },
            serde_json::json!({"operation": "noop"}),
        )
        .expect("schedule");
        s.enable().expect("enable");
        s.next_run_at = Some(
            Timestamp::now()
                .checked_sub(std::time::Duration::from_secs(lateness))
                .expect("past"),
        );
        s
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn full_tick_dispatches_once_and_advances_schedule() {
        let store = InMemoryScheduleStore::new();
        let schedule = due_schedule("hourly", 3600, 30);
        let id = schedule.id;
        store.seed(schedule);
        let mut runtime = SchedulerRuntime::new(
            store,
            InMemoryLeaseStore::new(),
            FakeDispatch::default(),
            SchedulerConfig::local("replica-1").expect("config"),
        )
        .expect("runtime");

        let now = Timestamp::now();
        let report = runtime.tick(&now).await.expect("tick");
        assert_eq!(report.scanned, 1);
        assert_eq!(report.due, 1);
        assert_eq!(report.dispatched, 1);
        assert_eq!(report.catch_up_skipped, 0);
        assert_eq!(runtime.queue_len(), 0);

        // Schedule advanced: next_run_at moved past now; not due anymore.
        let stored = runtime.store.get(id).await.expect("get").expect("exists");
        assert!(stored.last_run_at.is_some());
        assert!(stored.next_run_at.is_some_and(|n| n.is_future()));

        // Next tick: nothing due — exactly-once.
        let report = runtime.tick(&now).await.expect("tick2");
        assert_eq!(report.due, 0);
        assert_eq!(report.dispatched, 0);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn overlap_skip_keeps_the_tick_for_later() {
        let store = InMemoryScheduleStore::new();
        let schedule = due_schedule("long", 60, 30);
        store.seed(schedule.clone());
        let dispatch = FakeDispatch::default();
        dispatch
            .running
            .lock()
            .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
            .insert(schedule.id); // pretend previous run still going
        let mut runtime = SchedulerRuntime::new(
            store,
            InMemoryLeaseStore::new(),
            dispatch,
            SchedulerConfig::local("replica-1").expect("config"),
        )
        .expect("runtime");

        let now = Timestamp::now();
        let report = runtime.tick(&now).await.expect("tick");
        assert_eq!(report.dispatched, 0);
        assert_eq!(
            report.overlap_skipped, 1,
            "running schedule skips this tick"
        );
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn dispatch_failure_requeues_and_recovers_on_reap() {
        let store = InMemoryScheduleStore::new();
        let schedule = due_schedule("flaky", 3600, 30);
        store.seed(schedule);
        let dispatch = FakeDispatch::default();
        *dispatch
            .failing_left
            .lock()
            .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()) = 1; // first call fails
        let mut runtime = SchedulerRuntime::new(
            store,
            InMemoryLeaseStore::new(),
            dispatch,
            SchedulerConfig::local("replica-1").expect("config"),
        )
        .expect("runtime");

        let now = Timestamp::now();
        let report = runtime.tick(&now).await.expect("tick");
        assert_eq!(report.dispatch_errors, 1);
        assert_eq!(report.dispatched, 0);
        assert_eq!(runtime.queue_len(), 1, "failed run awaits next tick");

        // Same tick again would re-dispatch the queued run (now succeeding).
        let report = runtime.tick(&now).await.expect("retry tick");
        assert_eq!(report.dispatched, 1);
        assert_eq!(runtime.queue_len(), 0);

        // Recovery: expired leases reaped + due work re-enqueued.
        let leases = InMemoryLeaseStore::new();
        let stale = leases
            .try_acquire(
                &schedule_resource(&ScheduleId::new()),
                "dead-replica",
                std::time::Duration::from_secs(0),
                &now,
            )
            .await
            .expect("stale lease");
        assert!(!stale.is_active(
            &now.checked_add(std::time::Duration::from_secs(1))
                .unwrap_or(now)
        ));
        let mut runtime2 = SchedulerRuntime::new(
            InMemoryScheduleStore::new(),
            leases,
            FakeDispatch::default(),
            SchedulerConfig::local("replica-2").expect("config"),
        )
        .expect("runtime2");
        let report = runtime2
            .recover(
                &now.checked_add(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5))
                    .unwrap_or(now),
            )
            .await
            .expect("recover");
        assert_eq!(report.leases_reaped, 1);
    }
}
```

```rust
// PURPOSE:
// The production composition root for the worker process.
//
// There is exactly one bring-up path. It selects the broker and the durable
// store, binds `execution.run` to `AgentRunHandler` over a connected,
// health-probed gRPC bridge, and aborts the boot when bridge configuration is
// missing or the bridge is unreachable. A worker that cannot reach the AI
// orchestrator must not start: starting anyway would let it claim tasks and
// then report failures for work it could never have performed.
//
// There is deliberately no `--dev-inmemory` lane and no echo handler. A second
// bring-up path that answers tasks with canned output is a second execution
// lifecycle, and the two cannot be told apart from the outside: both report
// success. The queue plumbing is exercised by `mas-worker`'s own tests against
// a real in-process broker, which is where that coverage belongs.

//! `mas-worker` process bootstrap.
//!
//! Bring-up: durable handler registry + durable attempt coordination in
//! PostgreSQL. The **broker lane** selects at boot via `broker.kind`:
//! `pg` (default, SKIP-LOCKED claims over the durable task tables) or `nats`
//! (feature `nats`, JetStream stream + explicit-ack pull consumers over
//! `MAS_NATS_URL` / `broker.nats_url`).
//!
//! Every claim, every attempt and every settlement goes through
//! `DurableExecutionPort`, so the worker holds no authoritative state of its
//! own: a restart re-derives everything from the database.
//!
//! Consumer provisioning, the AI bridge health probe, and fast-fail on missing
//! configuration all happen before the loop starts.
//!
//! Environment: `MAS_DATABASE_URL`, the AI bridge settings (see
//! `agent_execution`), plus `MAS_NATS_URL` for the nats lane.

mod agent_execution;

use std::sync::Arc;

// `AgentBridge` is imported for its `health()` method, which the boot-time
// readiness probe calls on the concrete bridge.
use agent_execution::{AgentBridgeSettings, AgentRunHandler};
use mas_execution::AgentBridge;
use mas_messaging::broker::BrokerPort;
use mas_worker::consumer::{ConsumerConfig, TaskConsumer};
use mas_worker::handler::OperationDispatcher;
use mas_worker::AttemptCoordinator;
use mas_worker::ConsumerOutcome;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    std::process::exit(match run().await {
        Ok(()) => 0,
        Err(err) => {
            eprintln!("mas-worker: {err}");
            2
        },
    });
}

/// The single bring-up path.
///
/// Order matters and is deliberate:
///
/// 1. **Config** — every value the worker needs is resolved before anything is
///    bound.
/// 2. **Database** — the durable store is the only authority the worker has, so
///    it is connected first.
/// 3. **Broker lane** — selected and health-probed, so a worker never starts
///    against a broker it cannot see.
/// 4. **Durable attempt coordination** — claims, attempts and settlements all
///    go through `DurableExecutionPort`; the worker keeps no authoritative
///    state of its own, so a restart re-derives everything.
/// 5. **AI bridge** — connected and health-probed. A missing or unreachable
///    bridge aborts the boot rather than starting a worker that would claim
///    tasks it cannot run.
/// 6. **Consume** — `execution.run` dispatches through
///    `AgentRunHandler` → canonical runtime → gRPC bridge → Python.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// Returns a human-readable boot failure. Every failure path names the knob
/// that has to change, because a worker that refuses to start is only useful
/// if the operator can tell why.
async fn run() -> Result<(), String> {
    use mas_persistence::pool::{Database, DatabaseUrl, PoolConfig};
    use mas_persistence::repositories::PgDurableExecution;

    let layered = mas_common::config::load_layered().map_err(|e| format!("config: {e}"))?;
    let merger = mas_common::config::Merger::new(&layered);
    let worker_name = merger.string("MAS_WORKER_NAME", "worker.worker_name", "worker-1");
    let poll_ms = merger
        .u64("MAS_WORKER_POLL_MS", "worker.poll_interval_ms", 100)
        .map_err(|e| format!("config: {e}"))?;
    let consumer_name = merger.string("MAS_WORKER_CONSUMER", "worker.consumer_name", "tasks-main");
    let max_in_flight = merger
        .u64("MAS_WORKER_MAX_IN_FLIGHT", "worker.max_in_flight", 8)
        .map_err(|e| format!("config: {e}"))?
        .max(1) as usize;
    let lease_ttl_ms = merger
        .u64("MAS_WORKER_LEASE_TTL_MS", "worker.lease_ttl_ms", 15_000)
        .map_err(|e| format!("config: {e}"))?
        .max(1_000);

    let url = merger.string("MAS_DATABASE_URL", "database.url", "");
    if url.is_empty() {
        return Err(
            "mas-worker requires database.url / MAS_DATABASE_URL: the durable \
                    pipeline has no in-memory mode, because a claim this process cannot \
                    lose on restart is not a claim"
                .to_owned(),
        );
    }
    // ── Worker plane pool ──────────────────────────────────────────────
    //
    // A worker claim is `SELECT … FROM tasks FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, and it
    // scans every tenant's queue on purpose: the tenant authority is the row
    // the lease is won on, which by definition is unknown until the query
    // returns. That makes the worker one of the planes that cannot be
    // expressed as an RLS policy, so it connects as `mas_worker` — a role
    // whose BYPASSRLS is confined to the durable execution tables (migration
    // 0017). It has no grant on credentials, api_keys or sessions, so a
    // compromised worker cannot read tenant secrets.
    //
    // `MAS_DATABASE_URL` is still required: it is the pool the migration
    // ledger is verified against and the pool any non-tenant work uses. There
    // is no fallback from the worker plane to the runtime pool — under
    // `mas_app` the claim would return zero rows and the worker would idle
    // while looking healthy.
    let runtime_url = DatabaseUrl::new(url).map_err(|e| format!("database url: {e}"))?;
    let mut runtime_config =
        PoolConfig::for_url(runtime_url, "mas-worker").map_err(|e| format!("database: {e}"))?;
    runtime_config.max_connections = merger
        .u64("MAS_DATABASE_MAX_CONNS", "database.max_connections", 16)
        .map_err(|e| format!("config: {e}"))?
        .try_into()
        .unwrap_or(16);
    let runtime_database = Database::connect(&runtime_config)
        .await
        .map_err(|e| format!("database: {e}"))?;
    let pool = runtime_database.pool().clone();

    // Migrations must be current. A worker that claims tasks against a stale
    // schema would fence and settle them against columns that no longer
    // exist, which is a corruption and not an outage.
    let runner = mas_persistence::migrations::MigrationRunner::new(pool.clone());
    runner
        .ensure_table()
        .await
        .map_err(|e| format!("migrations: {e}"))?;
    runner
        .verify()
        .await
        .map_err(|e| format!("migration ledger drift — apply scripts/migrate.sh up first: {e}"))?;

    // The worker plane is a *different database role*, so it needs its own
    // URL — the whole point is that the credential differs.
    let worker_url = merger.string("MAS_DATABASE_WORKER_URL", "database.worker_url", "");
    if worker_url.is_empty() {
        return Err(
            "mas-worker requires database.worker_url / MAS_DATABASE_WORKER_URL: the \
             worker plane claims tasks across tenants and therefore runs as the \
             mas_worker role (migrations/0017_plane_roles); falling back to the \
             runtime role would make every claim return zero rows"
                .to_owned(),
        );
    }
    let worker_url =
        DatabaseUrl::new(worker_url).map_err(|e| format!("worker database url: {e}"))?;
    let mut worker_config = PoolConfig::for_url(worker_url, "mas-worker-plane")
        .map_err(|e| format!("worker database: {e}"))?;
    worker_config.max_connections = merger
        .u64("MAS_DATABASE_MAX_CONNS", "database.max_connections", 16)
        .map_err(|e| format!("config: {e}"))?
        .try_into()
        .unwrap_or(16);
    let worker_database = Database::connect(&worker_config)
        .await
        .map_err(|e| format!("worker database: {e}"))?;
    let worker_pool = worker_database.pool().clone();

    let (broker, broker_lane) = select_broker(&merger, &worker_pool).await?;

    // The durable execution port is the worker's only authority. Attempts are
    // claimed, fenced and settled through it, so the worker holds nothing that
    // a restart would lose.
    // Claims, attempts and settlements all run on the worker plane. Once a
    // lease is won, the row itself names the tenant, and the worker derives
    // everything else from the database rather than from anything the broker
    // told it.
    let durable: Arc<dyn mas_application::durable::DurableExecutionPort> =
        Arc::new(PgDurableExecution::new(worker_pool));
    let attempts = Arc::new(
        AttemptCoordinator::new(
            durable,
            worker_name.clone(),
            max_in_flight,
            std::time::Duration::from_millis(lease_ttl_ms),
        )
        .map_err(|e| format!("attempt coordinator: {e}"))?,
    );

    let handlers_env = merger.string("MAS_WORKER_HANDLERS", "worker.handlers", "");
    let bound = handlers_env
        .split(',')
        .map(str::trim)
        .filter(|h| !h.is_empty())
        .collect::<Vec<_>>();

    // The AI bridge is resolved BEFORE the consumer starts, and a missing
    // configuration aborts the boot. Binding an echo handler here instead would
    // turn every execution into a silent no-op that reports success.
    let mut dispatcher = OperationDispatcher::new();
    if bound.contains(&"execution.run") {
        let settings =
            AgentBridgeSettings::from_merger(&merger).map_err(|e| format!("ai bridge: {e}"))?;
        eprintln!(
            "mas-worker: connecting ai bridge at {}",
            settings.endpoint()
        );
        let bridge = settings
            .connect()
            .await
            .map_err(|e| format!("ai bridge connect: {e}"))?;

        match bridge.health().await {
            Ok(()) => eprintln!("mas-worker: ai orchestrator healthy"),
            Err(error) => {
                return Err(format!(
                    "ai orchestrator health probe failed: {error}. \
                     refusing to start a worker whose AI runtime is unreachable"
                ))
            },
        }

        // The cancellation token the graceful-drain path owns: cancelling it
        // stops in-flight AI work instead of abandoning it mid-run.
        let cancellation = mas_orchestration::cancellation::CancellationToken::new();
        dispatcher = dispatcher.with_handler(
            "execution.run",
            Arc::new(AgentRunHandler::new(Arc::new(bridge), cancellation)),
        );
    }
    let ops: Vec<&str> = dispatcher.operations();
    eprintln!("mas-worker: handlers bound = {ops:?} (unknown ops ⇒ permanent-fail pipeline)");

    let consumer = TaskConsumer::new(
        broker,
        attempts,
        Arc::new(dispatcher),
        ConsumerConfig {
            consumer_name,
            poll_interval: std::time::Duration::from_millis(poll_ms),
            worker_name,
            max_in_flight,
            lease_ttl: std::time::Duration::from_millis(lease_ttl_ms),
            ..ConsumerConfig::default()
        },
    );
    let (handle, watch) = mas_worker::grace::channel();
    tokio::spawn(mas_worker::grace::watch_signals(handle));
    eprintln!("mas-worker: claiming mas.tasks.* via {broker_lane} lane");
    let outcome: ConsumerOutcome = consumer
        .run(watch)
        .await
        .map_err(|e| format!("consumer: {e}"))?;
    eprintln!(
        "drained: acked={} naks={} terms={} completed={} failed={} abandoned={}",
        outcome.acked,
        outcome.naks,
        outcome.terms,
        outcome.completed,
        outcome.failed,
        outcome.abandoned,
    );
    Ok(())
}

/// Broker selection: `broker.kind` picks the durable task lane.
///
/// * `pg` (default) — `PgTaskBroker` over the claims/outbox tables (SKIP
///   LOCKED); no extra infrastructure beyond PostgreSQL.
/// * `nats` (feature `nats`) — JetStream stream `broker.stream`,
///   explicit-ack pull consumers, DLQ lane via the adapter; requires
///   `MAS_NATS_URL` / `broker.nats_url`. The lifecycle store remains
///   PostgreSQL either way.
///
/// Invalid kinds fail fast at boot; the lane is otherwise invisible to the
/// consumer loop above (both satisfy `BrokerPort`).
#[derive(Debug)]
enum LaneDecision {
    Pg,
    #[cfg(feature = "nats")]
    Nats {
        url: String,
    },
}

/// Pure boot-fail rules, unit-testable without a server.
fn resolve_lane(kind: &str, nats_url: &str) -> Result<LaneDecision, String> {
    match kind {
        "pg" => Ok(LaneDecision::Pg),
        "nats" => {
            #[cfg(feature = "nats")]
            {
                if nats_url.is_empty() {
                    return Err(
                        "broker.kind=nats requires MAS_NATS_URL / broker.nats_url".to_owned()
                    );
                }
                Ok(LaneDecision::Nats {
                    url: nats_url.to_owned(),
                })
            }
            #[cfg(not(feature = "nats"))]
            {
                let _ = nats_url;
                Err(
                    "broker.kind=nats requires building mas-worker with `--features nats`"
                        .to_owned(),
                )
            }
        },
        other => Err(format!(
            "broker.kind must be one of pg|nats (got {other:?})"
        )),
    }
}

async fn select_broker(
    merger: &mas_common::config::Merger<'_>,
    pool: &sqlx::PgPool,
) -> Result<(Arc<dyn BrokerPort>, String), String> {
    use mas_persistence::repositories::broker::PgTaskBroker;

    let kind = merger.string("MAS_BROKER_KIND", "broker.kind", "pg");
    let nats_url = merger.string("MAS_NATS_URL", "broker.nats_url", "");
    match resolve_lane(&kind, &nats_url)? {
        LaneDecision::Pg => Ok((
            Arc::new(PgTaskBroker::new(pool.clone())) as Arc<dyn BrokerPort>,
            "pg (SKIP LOCKED)".to_owned(),
        )),
        #[cfg(feature = "nats")]
        LaneDecision::Nats { url } => {
            let stream = merger.string("MAS_BROKER_STREAM", "broker.stream", "MAS_TASKS");
            let ack_wait_ms = merger
                .u64("MAS_BROKER_ACK_WAIT_MS", "broker.ack_wait_ms", 30_000)
                .map_err(|e| format!("config: {e}"))?;
            let config = mas_messaging::nats::NatsBrokerConfig::for_url(url)
                .with_stream(stream)
                .with_ack_wait(std::time::Duration::from_millis(ack_wait_ms));
            let broker = mas_messaging::nats::NatsBroker::connect(&config)
                .await
                .map_err(|e| format!("nats broker: {e}"))?;
            // Boot-time liveness probe: refuse to start a worker that
            // cannot see its task lane.
            broker
                .ping()
                .await
                .map_err(|e| format!("nats health probe: {e}"))?;
            Ok((
                Arc::new(broker) as Arc<dyn BrokerPort>,
                "nats (JetStream)".to_owned(),
            ))
        },
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn resolve_lane_defaults_to_pg_and_rejects_unknown_kinds() {
        assert!(matches!(resolve_lane("pg", ""), Ok(LaneDecision::Pg)));
        assert!(matches!(
            resolve_lane("pg", "anything"),
            Ok(LaneDecision::Pg)
        ));
        let err = resolve_lane("redis", "")
            .expect_err("unknown broker kinds must fail at boot, not silently degrade");
        assert!(err.contains("broker.kind"), "names the knob: {err}");
        assert!(err.contains("redis"), "echoes the invalid value: {err}");
    }

    #[cfg(feature = "nats")]
    #[test]
    fn resolve_lane_nats_requires_a_url() {
        let err =
            resolve_lane("nats", "").expect_err("nats lane without a URL must refuse to boot");
        assert!(err.contains("MAS_NATS_URL"), "names the missing key: {err}");
        let ok = resolve_lane("nats", "nats://127.0.0.1:4222")
            .expect("nats with URL selects the nats lane");
        match ok {
            LaneDecision::Nats { url } => assert_eq!(url, "nats://127.0.0.1:4222"),
            _ => panic!("expected Nats decision"),
        }
    }

    #[cfg(not(feature = "nats"))]
    #[test]
    fn resolve_lane_nats_without_feature_gives_build_guidance() {
        let err = resolve_lane("nats", "nats://127.0.0.1:4222")
            .expect_err("nats lane requires the nats feature build");
        assert!(
            err.contains("--features nats"),
            "message tells the operator what to rebuild with: {err}"
        );
    }

    // -- production composition ---------------------------------------------
    //
    // These read this file and the manifest as data. The alternative --
    // booting a worker against a real database to observe which handler it
    // registered -- is not available in a unit test, and the property being
    // guaranteed is structural anyway: which symbols the production path is
    // allowed to name.

    /// This file's own source, and the manifest that gates dev-only bridges.
    const MAIN_SOURCE: &str = include_str!("main.rs");
    const MANIFEST: &str = include_str!("../Cargo.toml");

    /// The production composition root: from its start to the test module.
    ///
    /// Stopping at `mod tests` is not cosmetic. `include_str!` embeds this
    /// whole file, tests included, and the tests below necessarily *name* the
    /// symbols they forbid. Scanning to the end of the file would match the
    /// assertions themselves and fail for no real reason.
    fn production_source() -> &'static str {
        let start = MAIN_SOURCE
            .find("async fn run(")
            .expect("run() is the one and only production composition root");
        let end = MAIN_SOURCE
            .find("\nmod tests")
            .expect("the test module ends the file's production region");
        &MAIN_SOURCE[start..end]
    }

    /// The `mas-execution` dependency line, with any comment removed.
    ///
    /// The manifest *discusses* `dev-bridges` in a comment explaining why it is
    /// absent, so a naive `contains` matches the explanation rather than the
    /// declaration. Only the dependency line itself is evidence.
    fn execution_dependency_line() -> String {
        MANIFEST
            .lines()
            .find(|line| line.trim_start().starts_with("mas-execution"))
            .map(|line| line.split("//").next().unwrap_or("").to_owned())
            .expect("the worker depends on mas-execution")
    }

    #[test]
    fn echo_handler_never_reaches_the_production_path() {
        // `EchoHandler` exists so the demo can prove queue plumbing works. If it
        // is ever referenced from the production path, every execution becomes a
        // no-op that reports success -- the single most dangerous outcome in
        // this system, because it is indistinguishable from working.
        let production = production_source();
        assert!(
            !production.contains("EchoHandler"),
            "EchoHandler must stay confined to the demo path; \
             a worker that echoes reports successes it never produced"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_production_path_never_names_the_in_memory_bridge() {
        let production = production_source();
        assert!(
            !production.contains("InMemoryAgentBridge"),
            "production must dispatch through the real gRPC bridge, \
             not an in-memory stand-in"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_production_path_binds_the_grpc_bridge() {
        // Positive counterpart to the two above: it is not enough that the
        // forbidden symbols are absent, the real adapter must actually be wired
        // in, or a future refactor could satisfy both by binding nothing.
        let production = production_source();
        assert!(
            production.contains("AgentBridgeSettings"),
            "the production path must resolve the bridge from settings"
        );
        assert!(
            production.contains("settings\n            .connect()")
                || production.contains("settings.connect()")
                || production.contains(".connect()"),
            "the production path must connect the bridge before consuming"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_worker_never_enables_the_dev_bridges_feature() {
        // The strongest guarantee available: `InMemoryAgentBridge` only exists
        // when `mas-execution/dev-bridges` is on. Keeping it out of this
        // manifest makes an in-memory production bridge a compile error rather
        // than a review-time question.
        assert!(
            !execution_dependency_line().contains("dev-bridges"),
            "the worker must depend on mas-execution without dev-bridges; \
             enabling it would make an in-memory bridge nameable in production"
        );
    }
}
```

```text
The production `AgentBridge` adapter: Rust -> gRPC -> Python.

Translates a domain `AgentRunRequest` into the `AgentBridgeApi.RunAgent`
wire call and the reply back into an `AgentRunVerdict`. It refuses to send a
request without an authoritative tenant/organization scope, derives the RPC
deadline from the request's own deadline rather than guessing, races the
call against the request's cancellation token, and maps gRPC statuses onto
typed errors whose retryability matches the platform's canonical mapping.

! gRPC adapter implementing `mas-execution`'s [`AgentBridge`] port against

!

! adapter only translates: it turns a domain
! [`AgentRunRequest`] into the
! `AgentBridgeApi.RunAgent` wire call, and turns the reply back into an
! [`AgentRunVerdict`]. It never
! transitions execution state and never writes platform tables.
!
! # Behaviour
!
! * **Authoritative scope is mandatory.** A request without a tenant/organization
!   is refused locally rather than sent; the Python side enforces the same rule.
! * **Deadline is derived, not guessed.** The RPC deadline is the remaining
!   wall-clock until `request.deadline`, floored at a minimum sane value so a
!   near-expired request fails fast instead of hanging.
! * **Cancellation is observed.** The run future is raced against the request's
!   cancellation token. When cancellation wins, a `cancelled` verdict is
!   returned instead of leaving work running on the Python side.

!   `AppError`s whose retryability matches the platform's canonical mapping, so
!   the caller's retry policy behaves identically to any other lane.
! * **No silent success.** A provider failure surfaced by Python arrives as
!   `AgentRunVerdict::Failed` carrying its own `retryable` flag; it is never
!   converted into a success here.
```
