## FILE: repo/enterprise-mas/rust-core/scripts/provision-plane-roles.sh


**PURPOSE:**

```text
Provisions the machine-plane database roles with credentials, so a deployed
cluster can actually authenticate as them. Migrations 0015, 0017 and 0019
create `mas_directory`, `mas_worker`, `mas_outbox`, `mas_audit` and
`mas_scheduler` as NOLOGIN on purpose: an unconfigured deployment must not
be able to authenticate as a plane role by accident. Something has to grant
them LOGIN, and this is that thing.

Owning layer: operations. Run by a human or by the provisioning pipeline,
never by the application at boot.

Production responsibility: read each role's password from its own
environment variable, refuse to invent one, and apply the grant inside a
single psql session so a partial provisioning cannot leave one plane able to
log in and another not.

Security boundary: this script handles live credentials. It therefore
• never accepts a password as an argument (the process table is readable);
• never echoes one — `set +x` is forced and every value is passed through
psql variables rather than interpolated into logged SQL;
• refuses to run when a required variable is empty, and refuses to use
`--dev` against anything other than a loopback host;
• grants LOGIN and nothing else. The privilege surface of each role was
decided in the migration that created it and is not widened here.

It must NOT:
• be invoked by service code, a container entrypoint, or a migration;
• grant a role any privilege beyond LOGIN;
• fall back to a default password.
```


**COMPLETE CONTENT** (159 lines):

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# PURPOSE:
# Provisions the machine-plane database roles with credentials, so a deployed
# cluster can actually authenticate as them. Migrations 0015, 0017 and 0019
# create `mas_directory`, `mas_worker`, `mas_outbox`, `mas_audit` and
# `mas_scheduler` as NOLOGIN on purpose: an unconfigured deployment must not
# be able to authenticate as a plane role by accident. Something has to grant
# them LOGIN, and this is that thing.
#
# Owning layer: operations. Run by a human or by the provisioning pipeline,
# never by the application at boot.
#
# Production responsibility: read each role's password from its own
# environment variable, refuse to invent one, and apply the grant inside a
# single psql session so a partial provisioning cannot leave one plane able to
# log in and another not.
#
# Security boundary: this script handles live credentials. It therefore
#   • never accepts a password as an argument (the process table is readable);
#   • never echoes one — `set +x` is forced and every value is passed through
#     psql variables rather than interpolated into logged SQL;
#   • refuses to run when a required variable is empty, and refuses to use
#     `--dev` against anything other than a loopback host;
#   • grants LOGIN and nothing else. The privilege surface of each role was
#     decided in the migration that created it and is not widened here.
#
# It must NOT:
#   • be invoked by service code, a container entrypoint, or a migration;
#   • grant a role any privilege beyond LOGIN;
#   • fall back to a default password.

set -euo pipefail
set +x  # credentials are in the environment; never trace them

usage() {
    cat <<'USAGE'
provision-plane-roles.sh — grant LOGIN to the machine-plane roles.

Usage:
    MAS_DATABASE_ADMIN_URL=postgres://migrator:...@host:5432/mas \
    MAS_APP_PASSWORD=...            \
    MAS_DIRECTORY_PASSWORD=...      \
    MAS_WORKER_PASSWORD=...         \
    MAS_OUTBOX_PASSWORD=...         \
    MAS_AUDIT_PASSWORD=...          \
    MAS_SCHEDULER_PASSWORD=...      \
    scripts/provision-plane-roles.sh

Options:
    --dev       Generate random passwords and provision a local test cluster.
                Refuses to run against a non-loopback host.
    --dry-run   Print the statements that would run, with every password
                replaced by ********.
    -h, --help  This message.

Every password is read from the environment. None has a default.
USAGE
}

DEV=0
DRY_RUN=0
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
        --dev) DEV=1; shift ;;
        --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
        -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
        *) echo "unknown option: $1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
    esac
done

ADMIN_URL="${MAS_DATABASE_ADMIN_URL:-}"
[ -n "$ADMIN_URL" ] || { echo "MAS_DATABASE_ADMIN_URL is required" >&2; exit 2; }

# Refuse --dev against anything that is not this host.
if [ "$DEV" -eq 1 ]; then
    host="${ADMIN_URL#*@}"; host="${host%%/*}"; host="${host%%:*}"
    case "$host" in
        127.0.0.1|localhost|"") : ;;
        *) echo "--dev may only target a loopback host (got '$host')" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    esac
fi

random_password() {
    if command -v openssl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        openssl rand -base64 32 | tr -d '\n'
    elif [ -r /dev/urandom ]; then
        LC_ALL=C tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' < /dev/urandom | head -c 40
    else
        echo "no source of randomness available" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
}

if [ "$DEV" -eq 1 ]; then
    MAS_APP_PASSWORD="$(random_password)"
    MAS_DIRECTORY_PASSWORD="$(random_password)"
    MAS_WORKER_PASSWORD="$(random_password)"
    MAS_OUTBOX_PASSWORD="$(random_password)"
    MAS_AUDIT_PASSWORD="$(random_password)"
    MAS_SCHEDULER_PASSWORD="$(random_password)"
    echo "generated random passwords for a local cluster (not printed)" >&2
fi

# Every remaining password must come from the environment. An empty one is a
# hard error: a role that gets LOGIN with an empty password is a role anyone
# can become.
MISSING=""
for var in MAS_APP_PASSWORD MAS_DIRECTORY_PASSWORD MAS_WORKER_PASSWORD \
           MAS_OUTBOX_PASSWORD MAS_AUDIT_PASSWORD MAS_SCHEDULER_PASSWORD; do
    eval "value=\"\${$var:-}\""
    [ -n "$value" ] || MISSING="$MISSING $var"
done
if [ -n "$MISSING" ]; then
    echo "missing required password environment variables:$MISSING" >&2
    echo "no role was modified" >&2
    exit 2
fi

# `ON_ERROR_STOP` plus one session: either every role is provisioned or none
# is. Half a provisioning is worse than none, because the planes that failed
# look identical to planes that were never configured.
PSQL=(psql "$ADMIN_URL" --no-psqlrc -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 --quiet)

run_sql() {
    if [ "$DRY_RUN" -eq 1 ]; then
        sed -E "s/(PASSWORD ')[^']*(')/\1********\2/g" <<<"$1"
        return 0
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$1" | "${PSQL[@]}" \
        -v app_password="$MAS_APP_PASSWORD" \
        -v directory_password="$MAS_DIRECTORY_PASSWORD" \
        -v worker_password="$MAS_WORKER_PASSWORD" \
        -v outbox_password="$MAS_OUTBOX_PASSWORD" \
        -v audit_password="$MAS_AUDIT_PASSWORD" \
        -v scheduler_password="$MAS_SCHEDULER_PASSWORD"
}

read -r -d '' SQL <<'SQL' || true
-- The runtime role. No BYPASSRLS, and this script does not give it one:
-- request traffic is confined by row-level security, which is the whole point.
ALTER ROLE mas_app       LOGIN PASSWORD :'app_password';

-- The pre-scope directory reader.
ALTER ROLE mas_directory LOGIN PASSWORD :'directory_password';

-- The machine planes. Each holds BYPASSRLS already, granted by the migration
-- that created it and confined there by table and operation.
ALTER ROLE mas_worker    LOGIN PASSWORD :'worker_password';
ALTER ROLE mas_outbox    LOGIN PASSWORD :'outbox_password';
ALTER ROLE mas_audit     LOGIN PASSWORD :'audit_password';
ALTER ROLE mas_scheduler LOGIN PASSWORD :'scheduler_password';
SQL

run_sql "$SQL"

if [ "$DRY_RUN" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "provisioned: mas_app mas_directory mas_worker mas_outbox mas_audit mas_scheduler"
    echo "no privilege beyond LOGIN was granted; the grant surface lives in the migrations"
fi

```

Shared harness for the live-PostgreSQL suite: the environment
gate, two pool bootstraps (migrator and runtime role), and tiny hash
helpers mirroring the verifier's on-disk formulas.

Owning layer: `mas-persistence` (tests).

easiest way to ship an isolation suite that cannot fail.

holds BYPASSRLS, and asserts that fact before any test uses it. A pool that
bypasses row-level security would let every isolation assertion in the
suite pass on a policy that is switched off.

• fall back to the migrator URL when the runtime URL is missing — the
isolation tests skip loudly instead, because a vacuous green is worse
than a visible skip;
• be pointed at a production database;
• grant the runtime pool more than one connection: the pooled-connection
leakage test needs the second `acquire()` to be the same socket.

**COMPLETE CONTENT** (138 lines):

```rust
//! PURPOSE: Shared harness for the live-PostgreSQL suite: the environment
//! gate, two pool bootstraps (migrator and runtime role), and tiny hash
//! helpers mirroring the verifier's on-disk formulas.
//!
//! Owning layer: `mas-persistence` (tests).
//!
//! Production responsibility: hand each test a pool whose *identity* matches
//! what the test is actually asserting. Lifecycle and round-trip tests get the
//! migrator; isolation tests get `mas_app`. Conflating the two is the single
//! easiest way to ship an isolation suite that cannot fail.
//!
//! Security boundary: [`live_app_pool`] refuses to hand back a pool whose role
//! holds BYPASSRLS, and asserts that fact before any test uses it. A pool that
//! bypasses row-level security would let every isolation assertion in the
//! suite pass on a policy that is switched off.
//!
//! It must NOT:
//!   • fall back to the migrator URL when the runtime URL is missing — the
//!     isolation tests skip loudly instead, because a vacuous green is worse
//!     than a visible skip;
//!   • be pointed at a production database;
//!   • grant the runtime pool more than one connection: the pooled-connection
//!     leakage test needs the second `acquire()` to be the same socket.

use mas_persistence::migrations::MigrationRunner;
use mas_persistence::pool::{Database, DatabaseUrl, PoolConfig};
use sqlx::PgPool;

/// Environment variable consulted first, then `DATABASE_URL`.
pub const ENV_VAR: &str = "MAS_TEST_DATABASE_URL";

/// Reads the live database URL from the environment, when provided.
pub fn live_url() -> Option<String> {
    std::env::var(ENV_VAR)
        .ok()
        .filter(|value| !value.trim().is_empty())
        .or_else(|| {
            std::env::var("DATABASE_URL")
                .ok()
                .filter(|value| !value.trim().is_empty())
        })
}

/// Builds a migrated pool against the live URL (or `None` when the suite is
/// not enabled). Every caller ends the returned pool's test with normal
/// teardown (tables are shared deliberately — fixtures carry fresh ids).
pub async fn live_pool(owner: &'static str) -> Option<PgPool> {
    let raw = live_url().unwrap_or_else(|| {
        eprintln!(
            "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━\n\
            live_pg: skipping (set {ENV_VAR} — see docs/runbooks/postgres-live-tests.md)\n\
            ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"
        );
        String::new()
    });
    if raw.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    let url = DatabaseUrl::new(raw).expect("MAS_TEST_DATABASE_URL parses");
    let mut config = PoolConfig::for_url(url, owner).expect("pool config");
    config.max_connections = 4;
    let database = Database::connect(&config)
        .await
        .expect("live database reachable");
    let pool = database.pool().clone();
    let runner = MigrationRunner::new(pool.clone());
    runner.ensure_table().await.expect("ledger table");
    runner.migrate().await.expect("migrations applied");
    Some(pool)
}

/// Environment variable for the **runtime** database URL.
///
/// This is the pool the application itself uses: `mas_app`, a role with no
/// BYPASSRLS. Tests that assert row-level security is *doing* something have
/// to run here. Under the migrator URL every one of them would pass vacuously,
/// because a superuser bypasses the policies the test is trying to exercise.
pub const APP_ENV_VAR: &str = "MAS_TEST_DATABASE_APP_URL";

/// Builds a pool connected as the runtime role (`mas_app`).
///
/// Returns `None` when [`APP_ENV_VAR`] is unset, so the suite still runs —
/// and still skips — in an environment that has only provisioned the migrator
/// credential. The RLS tests print a notice in that case rather than passing
/// quietly, because a vacuous isolation test is worse than no isolation test.
///
/// Migrations are deliberately **not** applied from this pool: `mas_app` has
/// no DDL rights on the schema, and a test that could not tell the difference
/// between "migrations applied" and "migrations already applied" would not be
/// testing anything. Call [`live_pool`] first to bring the schema up.
pub async fn live_app_pool(owner: &'static str) -> Option<PgPool> {
    let raw = std::env::var(APP_ENV_VAR)
        .ok()
        .filter(|v| !v.trim().is_empty())?;
    let url = DatabaseUrl::new(raw).expect("MAS_TEST_DATABASE_APP_URL parses");
    let mut config = PoolConfig::for_url(url, owner).expect("pool config");
    // One connection on purpose. The pooled-connection test needs to be able
    // to take the single connection in the pool, use it for one "request",
    // hand it back, and take it again — that is the reuse it is asserting is
    // safe. A pool of twenty would let each request have a fresh connection
    // and the test would prove nothing.
    config.max_connections = 1;
    // ...and hold exactly one open, so the socket is warm and waiting. A pool
    // that lazily opened a connection per acquire would defeat the reuse this
    // exercise is about.
    config.min_connections = 1;
    let database = Database::connect(&config)
        .await
        .expect("runtime-role database reachable");
    let pool = database.pool().clone();

    // Fail loudly and immediately if this is not actually the runtime role.
    // Every assertion below is void if the connection can bypass RLS.
    let bypass: bool =
        sqlx::query_scalar("SELECT rolbypassrls FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = current_user")
            .fetch_one(&pool)
            .await
            .expect("role lookup");
    assert!(
        !bypass,
        "{APP_ENV_VAR} must connect as a role that is subject to row-level \
         security (mas_app); current_user bypasses it, so every isolation \
         assertion in this suite would pass without testing anything"
    );
    Some(pool)
}

/// SHA-256 hex digest (the on-disk `secret_hash` formula).
pub fn sha256_hex(input: &[u8]) -> String {
    use sha2::Digest;
    let digest = sha2::Sha256::digest(input);
    digest.iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect()
}

/// The public lookup prefix the verifier persists (`mas_` + first 8).
pub fn visible_prefix(raw: &str) -> String {
    raw.chars().take(4 + 8).collect()
}

```

**COMPLETE CONTENT** (174 lines):

````markdown
# Runbook: live PostgreSQL integration suite

**Location:** `crates/persistence/tests/live_pg.rs` (16 tests)
**Cost:** one PostgreSQL 16+ instance you are allowed to mutate.
**Never point at production.**

## 1. Bring up PostgreSQL

Any PostgreSQL 16+ works. Fastest disposable instance:

```bash
docker run --name mas-itest-pg \
  -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres -e POSTGRES_DB=mas_itest \
  -p 55432:5432 -d postgres:16-alpine
```

(Matches the compose service in `.devcontainer/` when you're inside the dev
container: the service `postgres` is already up; use
`postgres://postgres:postgres@postgres:5432/postgres`.)

## 1b. Two URLs, and why you need both

The suite needs **two** credentials, and the difference is the whole point.

| Variable | Role | BYPASSRLS | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MAS_TEST_DATABASE_URL` | migrator (`mas` locally) | yes | every lifecycle, schema and repository round-trip |
| `MAS_TEST_DATABASE_APP_URL` | runtime (`mas_app`) | **no** | the row-level-security assertions |

A superuser bypasses row-level security. That makes the migrator URL correct
for a test about migrations — and worthless for a test about isolation, because
a policy that is switched off cannot fail. Running `tenant_b_cannot_read_...`
on the migrator URL proves only that our SQL says `WHERE tenant_id = $1`; it
does not prove that the database would stop us if the SQL forgot.

So the three tests that end in `..._row_level_security`,
`..._previous_request_tenant` and `..._their_own_tables` run on the app URL.
**If `MAS_TEST_DATABASE_APP_URL` is unset they skip, loudly**, rather than
reporting green. A vacuous isolation test is worse than no isolation test:
it buys confidence it has not earned.

```bash
# Grant LOGIN to the plane roles the migrations deliberately create
# NOLOGIN. Passwords come from the environment, never argv.
export MAS_DATABASE_ADMIN_URL=$MAS_TEST_DATABASE_URL
export MAS_APP_PASSWORD=...       # and _DIRECTORY_ _WORKER_ _OUTBOX_ _AUDIT_
export MAS_WORKER_PASSWORD=...    #   _SCHEDULER_  — see the script for the
export MAS_SCHEDULER_PASSWORD=... #   complete list
./scripts/provision-plane-roles.sh --dry-run   # print, mask passwords
./scripts/provision-plane-roles.sh             # apply

export MAS_TEST_DATABASE_APP_URL=postgres://mas_app:...app...@127.0.0.1:55432/mas_itest
```

The script grants `LOGIN` and nothing else — no `BYPASSRLS`, no extra table
grants, no role attributes. `--dev` generates random passwords and refuses to
run against anything but loopback. `--dry-run` masks every password.

## 2. Run the suite

The suite migrates the database itself (idempotent ledger), seeds fixtures
through the real store code paths, and asserts round-trips for every
production repository:

```bash
cd rust-core
source .cargo-env
export MAS_TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:55432/mas_itest

# Full suite, with the skip banner suppressed by the env var being present:
cargo test -p mas-persistence --test live_pg

# Same thing via the migration helper first (DBA-style apply, then verify):
DATABASE_URL=$MAS_TEST_DATABASE_URL scripts/migrate.sh up
DATABASE_URL=$MAS_TEST_DATABASE_URL scripts/migrate.sh status
cargo test -p mas-persistence --test live_pg
```

The binary also honors a bare `DATABASE_URL` when `MAS_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is
unset; without either variable it prints the skip banner and exits green —
that is intentional (CI/dev loops without a database stay cheap), so **mark
the job that runs the live suite separately** and never treat the green skip
as signal.

Each test is self-contained (fresh UUID fixtures), safe to run concurrently
(`--test-threads` default), and safe to re-run against the same database.

## 3. What the suite covers

| Test | Repository(s) under test |
|---|---|
| `migrations_are_idempotent` | `MigrationRunner` (ledger apply/`verify`/) |
| `tenancy_round_trip` | `OrganizationStore`, `TenantStore`, `ProjectStore` (RLS-scoped reads) |
| `agents_round_trip` | `AgentStore`, `AgentVersionStore` incl. `UNIQUE (tenant_id, slug)` |
| `workflows_round_trip` | `WorkflowStore` |
| `executions_round_trip_and_idempotency` | `ExecutionStore` + idempotency slot |
| `schedules_due_scan_and_run_journal` | `ScheduleStore.list_due`, `record_run` (duplicate-fire guard) |
| `tasks_round_trip` | `TaskStore` (worker lifecycle port) |
| `api_keys_prefix_lookup_and_touch` | `ApiKeyStore` (`find_by_prefix`, `touch_last_used`) |
| `audit_append_list_and_counts` | `PostgresAuditLog` (append, correlation fetch, outcome counts) |
| `broker_publish_fetch_ack_round_trip` | `PgTaskBroker` (`BrokerPort` publish/fetch/ack + idempotent republish) |
| `concurrent_migrate_is_serialized` | `MigrationRunner` advisory lock under concurrency |
| `tenant_b_cannot_read_claim_cancel_or_settle_tenant_a_execution` | `ExecutionStore` under an armed cross-tenant scope |
| `the_same_idempotency_key_in_two_tenants_is_two_executions` | `ExecutionStore` idempotency slot tenancy |
| **`the_runtime_role_cannot_bypass_row_level_security`** | row-level security, **as `mas_app`** — unscoped ⇒ 0 rows; scoped ⇒ exactly one; cross-tenant `UPDATE`/`DELETE` ⇒ 0 rows affected |
| **`a_pooled_connection_does_not_inherit_the_previous_request_tenant`** | pooled-connection leakage — one socket, two callers; and the contrasting session-level-GUC case that *does* leak |
| **`the_plane_roles_are_confined_to_their_own_tables`** | privilege narrowness for `mas_worker`/`mas_audit`/`mas_outbox`/`mas_directory`/`mas_scheduler` |

### Why the pooled-connection test is a real test

The pool it exercises holds exactly **one** connection (`min = max = 1`), so
the second `acquire()` is guaranteed to be the same socket as the first. Two
things are then asserted in opposite directions, because a test that can only
fail one way can also pass for the wrong reason:

1. `SET LOCAL` (transaction scope) ⇒ the next request on that socket sees
   nothing. Verified directly against the cluster: `inside txn = 1`,
   `after commit = 0`.
2. `set_config(..., false)` (session scope) ⇒ the next request on that socket
   still sees the previous tenant's rows: `after commit = 1`. **This is the
   leak.** It is asserted, not merely described, so the reason `scoped_request`
   uses `SET LOCAL` and nothing else stays executable.

### Why the RLS test is not vacuous

Both directions were confirmed by hand before the assertion was trusted:

| Probe | Expected | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| `relrowsecurity` / `relforcerowsecurity` on `tenants` | `t` / `t` | `t` / `t` |
| `mas_app` privileges on `tenants` | must include `SELECT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE` | `DELETE,INSERT,SELECT,UPDATE` |
| unscoped `SELECT count(*) FROM tenants` as `mas_app` | `0` | `0` |
| same query as the superuser (proves rows exist) | `> 0` | `245` |

Without the second and fourth rows the first and third would be meaningless:
a role with no privileges and a table with no rows both produce `0`.

## 4. Running the binaries against the same database

```bash
export MAS_DATABASE_URL=$MAS_TEST_DATABASE_URL \
       MAS_ENV=staging \
       MAS_DATABASE_MIGRATE_ON_BOOT=false  # ledger must be verified green

cargo build -p mas-api -p mas-worker-service -p mas-scheduler-service
target/debug/mas-api         # durable stores + PostgresApiKeyVerifier
target/debug/mas-worker      # durable broker lane + pending-execution lifecycle
target/debug/mas-scheduler   # durable due-scan + scheduler journal
```

Tier-0 E2E signal after the trio is up:

```bash
DATABASE_URL=$MAS_DATABASE_URL scripts/smoke.sh
```

## 5. Clean up

```bash
docker rm -f mas-itest-pg            # if you used the disposable container
```

## 6. Failure playbook

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `connection refused` | PG not up or wrong port | `docker ps`; use the mapped port (`55432` in the example above) |
| `relation ... does not exist` on first boot | Migrations not applied | The suite applies them itself; for binary bring-up run `scripts/migrate.sh up` first |
| `duplicate key` in fixtures | Re-ran into a dirty DB you meant to reset | `dropdb/createdb` the test DB; fixtures use fresh ids and tolerate existing data otherwise |
| Skip banner prints on CI | Env var named differently | Export exactly `MAS_TEST_DATABASE_URL` (or `DATABASE_URL`) |
| `role "mas_app" does not exist` / `cannot login` | Plane roles are created `NOLOGIN` and have no password | Run `scripts/provision-plane-roles.sh` (see §1b) |
| `min_connections must be <= max_connections` | Hand-built pool config for the app pool | Not reachable from the suite; it sets both to `1` |
| `must connect as a role that is subject to row-level security` | `MAS_TEST_DATABASE_APP_URL` points at the migrator | Point it at `mas_app`; the suite refuses to continue rather than testing nothing |
| `verify` fails with checksum drift | SQL file edited after apply | Always create `migrations/NNNN_name/`, never edit an applied file's `up.sql` |

````
